title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
text: (1) This Act may be called the Companies Act, 2013.

sub_structure.2: (2) It extends to the whole of India.
sub_structure.4_a: (4) The provisions of this Act shall apply to- (a) companies incorporated under this Act or under any previous company law;

plain_english_summary: Establishes the name of the Act, its application across India, and confirms it applies to all companies incorporated under it or previous company laws.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,-

sub_structure.20: (20) "company" means a company incorporated under this Act or under any previous company law;
sub_structure.62: (62) "One Person Company" means a company which has only one person as a member;
sub_structure.68: (68) "private company" means a company having a minimum paid-up share capital... and which by its articles,- (i) restricts the right to transfer its shares; (ii) except in case of One Person Company, limits the number of its members to two hundred... (iii) prohibits any invitation to the public to subscribe for any securities...
sub_structure.69: (69) "promoter" means a person- (a) who has been named as such in a prospectus... or (b) who has control over the affairs of the company...
sub_structure.71: (71) "public company" means a company which- (a) is not a private company;

plain_english_summary: Defines crucial corporate terms for founders. It establishes what legally constitutes a 'Private Company' (limited to 200 members, cannot sell shares to the public) versus a 'Public Company' or a 'One Person Company', and legally defines who is considered a 'Promoter'.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Formation of company
text: (1) A company may be formed for any lawful purpose by- (a) seven or more persons, where the company to be formed is to be a public company; (b) two or more persons, where the company to be formed is to be a private company; or (c) one person, where the company to be formed is to be One Person Company...

sub_structure.2: (2) A company formed under sub-section (1) may be either- (a) a company limited by shares; or (b) a company limited by guarantee; or (c) an unlimited company.

plain_english_summary: Outlines the minimum founder requirements to start a company: at least 2 people for a private startup, 7 for a public company, or 1 for a One Person Company. The company can be limited by shares, guarantee, or be unlimited.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Members severally liable in certain cases
text: If at any time the number of members of a company is reduced, in the case of a public company, below seven, in the case of a private company, below two, and the company carries on business for more than six months while the number of members is so reduced, every person who is a member of the company during the time that it so carries on business after those six months and is cognisant of the fact... shall be severally liable for the payment of the whole debts of the company contracted during that time...
plain_english_summary: If a private startup's co-founder leaves and the company operates with only 1 member for more than 6 months, that remaining member loses their 'limited liability' protection and becomes personally responsible for the company's debts.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Memorandum
text: (1) The memorandum of a company shall state- (a) the name of the company with the last word "Limited" in the case of a public limited company, or the last words "Private Limited" in the case of a private limited company... (b) the State in which the registered office... is to be situated; (c) the objects for which the company is proposed to be incorporated...

sub_structure.2: (2) The name stated in the memorandum shall not- (a) be identical with or resemble too nearly to the name of an existing company... or (b) be such that its use by the company- (i) will constitute an offence... or (ii) is undesirable in the opinion of the Central Government.
sub_structure.5_i: (5)(i) Upon receipt of an application... the Registrar may... reserve the name for a period of twenty days from the date of approval...

plain_english_summary: Dictates what must be included in the Memorandum of Association (MOA), including the startup's name, registered state, and its business objects. It also sets the rules for name reservations and prohibits copying existing company names.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Articles
text: (1) The articles of a company shall contain the regulations for management of the company.

sub_structure.3: (3) The articles may contain provisions for entrenchment to the effect that specified provisions of the articles may be altered only if conditions or procedures as that are more restrictive than those applicable in the case of a special resolution, are met or complied with.
sub_structure.4: (4) The provisions for entrenchment referred to in sub-section (3) shall only be made either on formation of a company, or by an amendment in the articles agreed to by all the members of the company in the case of a private company...

plain_english_summary: The Articles of Association (AOA) contain the internal rules for running the startup. Founders can include 'entrenchment' clauses, meaning certain critical rules can only be changed if 100% of the shareholders agree, protecting minority founders.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Act to override memorandum, articles, etc.
text: Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act- (a) the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the memorandum or articles of a company, or in any agreement executed by it...

sub_structure.b: (b) any provision contained in the memorandum, articles, agreement or resolution shall, to the extent to which it is repugnant to the provisions of this Act, become or be void...

plain_english_summary: The Companies Act is the supreme law. If a startup drafts a Shareholders' Agreement, Founders' Agreement, or Articles of Association that conflict with this Act, those conflicting clauses are legally void and unenforceable.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Incorporation of company
text: (1) There shall be filed with the Registrar within whose jurisdiction the registered office of a company is proposed to be situated, the following documents and information for registration...

sub_structure.1_b: (b) a declaration in the prescribed form by an advocate, a chartered accountant... who is engaged in the formation of the company... that all the requirements of this Act... have been complied with;
sub_structure.5: (5) If any person furnishes any false or incorrect particulars of any information or suppresses any material information... in relation to the registration of a company, he shall be liable for action under section 447.
sub_structure.6: (6) Without prejudice to the provisions of sub-section (5) where, at any time after the incorporation of a company, it is proved that the company has been got incorporated by furnishing any false or incorrect information... the promoters, the persons named as the first directors... shall each be liable for action under section 447.

plain_english_summary: Lists the exact documents needed to register a startup. It carries severe warnings: if founders lie or submit fake documents during incorporation, they will be prosecuted for corporate fraud under Section 447, and the company can be shut down.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Formation of companies with charitable objects, etc.
text: (1) Where it is proved to the satisfaction of the Central Government that a person or an association of persons proposed to be registered under this Act as a limited company- (a) has in its objects the promotion of commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment or any such other object; (b) intends to apply its profits, if any, or other income in promoting its objects; and (c) intends to prohibit the payment of any dividend to its members... the Central Government may... allow that person... to be registered as a limited company... without the addition to its name of the word "Limited"...
plain_english_summary: Allows for the creation of 'Section 8' companies (non-profits). These companies must reinvest all profits into their charitable or research goals and are strictly banned from paying dividends to founders or shareholders.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Effect of registration
text: From the date of incorporation mentioned in the certificate of incorporation, such subscribers to the memorandum and all other persons, as may, from time to time, become members of the company, shall be a body corporate by the name contained in the memorandum, capable of exercising all the functions of an incorporated company under this Act and having perpetual succession with power to acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, tangible and intangible, to contract and to sue and be sued, by the said name.
plain_english_summary: The moment a startup gets its Certificate of Incorporation, it legally becomes an independent 'person' (a body corporate). It can own property, sign contracts, and sue or be sued in its own name, completely separate from its founders.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Effect of memorandum and articles
text: (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the memorandum and articles shall, when registered, bind the company and the members thereof to the same extent as if they respectively had been signed by the company and by each member, and contained covenants on its and his part to observe all the provisions of the memorandum and of the articles.

sub_structure.2: (2) All monies payable by any member to the company under the memorandum or articles shall be a debt due from him to the company.

plain_english_summary: Once registered, the MOA and AOA act as a legally binding contract between the company and its shareholders. Any money a founder or shareholder owes the company based on these documents is treated as a legal debt.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Commencement of business, etc.
text: (1) A company incorporated after the commencement of the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019 and having a share capital shall not commence any business or exercise any borrowing powers unless- (a) a declaration is filed by a director within a period of one hundred and eighty days of the date of incorporation of the company... that every subscriber to the memorandum has paid the value of the shares agreed to be taken by him...

sub_structure.1_b: (b) the company has filed with the Registrar a verification of its registered office as provided in sub-section (2) of section 12.
sub_structure.2: (2) If any default is made in complying with the requirements of this section, the company shall be liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees and every officer who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of one thousand rupees for each day during which such default continues but not exceeding an amount of one lakh rupees.
sub_structure.3: (3) Where no declaration has been filed... within a period of one hundred and eighty days... the Registrar has reasonable cause to believe that the company is not carrying on any business or operations, he may... initiate action for the removal of the name of the company from the register of companies...

plain_english_summary: A startup cannot legally start operations or borrow money until the founders deposit their initial share capital into the company bank account and file a declaration within 180 days of incorporation. Failure to do this risks heavy fines and having the company struck off the register.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Registered office of company
text: (1) A company shall, within thirty days of its incorporation and at all times thereafter, have a registered office capable of receiving and acknowledging all communications and notices as may be addressed to it.

sub_structure.3_a: (a) paint or affix its name, and the address of its registered office... on the outside of every office or place in which its business is carried on, in a conspicuous position...
sub_structure.3_c: (c) get its name, address of its registered office and the Corporate Identity Number along with telephone number... e-mail and website addresses, if any, printed in all its business letters, billheads, letter papers and in all its notices and other official publications;
sub_structure.4: (4) Notice of every change of the situation of the registered office... shall be given to the Registrar within thirty days of the change, who shall record the same.
sub_structure.8: (8) If any default is made in complying with the requirements of this section, the company and every officer who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of one thousand rupees for every day during which the default continues but not exceeding one lakh rupees.
sub_structure.9: (9) If the Registrar has reasonable cause to believe that the company is not carrying on any business or operations, he may cause a physical verification of the registered office... and if any default is found... initiate action for the removal of the name of the company...

plain_english_summary: Startups must establish a physical registered office within 30 days of incorporation. The company's name, address, and CIN (Corporate Identity Number) must be displayed on a physical board outside the office and on all official letterheads, emails, and invoices. The Registrar can physically inspect the office.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Alteration of memorandum
text: (1) Save as provided in section 61, a company may, by a special resolution and after complying with the procedure specified in this section, alter the provisions of its memorandum.

sub_structure.2: (2) Any change in the name of a company shall be subject to the provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 4 and shall not have effect except with the approval of the Central Government in writing...
sub_structure.4: (4) The alteration of the memorandum relating to the place of the registered office from one State to another shall not have any effect unless it is approved by the Central Government...
sub_structure.8: (8) A company, which has raised money from public through prospectus and still has any unutilised amount out of the money so raised, shall not change its objects for which it raised the money through prospectus unless a special resolution is passed by the company... and the dissenting shareholders shall be given an opportunity to exit...

plain_english_summary: To change its name, business objects, or move its registered office to a different state, a startup must pass a special resolution (75% shareholder approval). Shifting states or changing the name requires explicit government approval.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Alteration of articles
text: (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act and the conditions contained in its memorandum, if any, a company may, by a special resolution, alter its articles including alterations having the effect of conversion of- (a) a private company into a public company; or (b) a public company into a private company:

sub_structure.1_proviso_1: Provided that where a company being a private company alters its articles in such a manner that they no longer include the restrictions and limitations which are required to be included in the articles of a private company under this Act, the company shall, as from the date of such alteration, cease to be a private company:
sub_structure.1_proviso_2: Provided further that any alteration having the effect of conversion of a public company into a private company shall not valid unless it its approved by an order of the Central Government...

plain_english_summary: A startup can change its internal rules (AOA) or convert from a private to a public company by passing a special resolution. However, converting from a public company back into a private company is difficult and requires Central Government approval.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Alteration of memorandum or articles to be noted in every copy
text: (1) Every alteration made in the memorandum or articles of a company shall be noted in every copy of the memorandum or articles, as the case may be.

sub_structure.2: (2) If a company makes any default in complying with the provisions of sub-section (1), the company and every officer who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of one thousand rupees for every copy of the memorandum or articles issued without such alteration.

plain_english_summary: Whenever a startup updates its MOA or AOA, it must ensure every single physical and digital copy distributed going forward includes those updates. Giving out outdated copies carries a fine of ₹1,000 per copy.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Rectification of name of company
text: (1) If, through inadvertence or otherwise, a company on its first registration or on its registration by a new name, is registered by a name which,- (a) in the opinion of the Central Government, is identical with or too nearly resembles the name by which a company in existence had been previously registered... it may direct the company to change its name...

sub_structure.1_b: (b) on an application by a registered proprietor of a trade mark that the name is identical with or too nearly resembles to a registered trade mark... made to the Central Government within three years of incorporation... it may direct the company to change its name...
sub_structure.3: (3) If a company is in default in complying with any direction given under sub-section (1), the Central Government shall allot a new name to the company in such manner as may be prescribed and the Registrar shall enter the new name in the register of companies...

plain_english_summary: If a startup accidentally registers a name that is too similar to an existing company or infringes on an existing trademark, the government will order the startup to change its name. If the startup ignores the order, the government will forcibly assign it a new name.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Copies of memorandum, articles, etc., to be given to members
text: (1) A company shall, on being so requested by a member, send to him within seven days of the request and subject to the payment of such fees as may be prescribed, a copy of each of the following documents, namely:- (a) the memorandum; (b) the articles; and (c) every agreement and every resolution referred to in sub-section (1) of section 117...

sub_structure.2: (2) If a company makes any default in complying with the provisions of this section, the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable for each default, to a penalty of one thousand rupees for each day during which such default continues or one lakh rupees, whichever is less.

plain_english_summary: Shareholders have the right to request a copy of the company's MOA, AOA, and major resolutions. The startup must provide these within 7 days. Failing to do so triggers a daily penalty.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Conversion of companies already registered
text: (1) A company of any class registered under this Act may convert itself as a company of other class under this Act by alteration of memorandum and articles of the company in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where the conversion is required to be done under this section, the Registrar shall on an application made by the company... close the former registration of the company and after registering the documents referred to in sub-section (1), issue a certificate of incorporation in the same manner as its first registration.
sub_structure.3: (3) The registration of a company under this section shall not affect any debts, liabilities, obligations or contracts incurred or entered into, by or on behalf of the company before conversion...

plain_english_summary: If a startup converts from one type of company to another (e.g., Private to Public), its past debts, contracts, and legal obligations are completely unaffected and carry over to the newly converted entity.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Subsidiary company not to hold shares in its holding company
text: (1) No company shall, either by itself or through its nominees, hold any shares in its holding company and no holding company shall allot or transfer its shares to any of its subsidiary companies and any such allotment or transfer of shares of a company to its subsidiary company shall be void:

sub_structure.1_proviso_1_c: Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall apply to a case- ... (c) where the subsidiary company is a shareholder even before it became a subsidiary company of the holding company:
sub_structure.1_proviso_2: Provided further that the subsidiary company referred to in the preceding proviso shall have a right to vote at a meeting of the holding company only in respect of the shares held by it as a legal representative or as a trustee...

plain_english_summary: A subsidiary startup cannot legally buy or hold equity shares in its parent/holding company, as this creates circular ownership. Any attempt to issue shares this way is legally void. Exceptions exist if the subsidiary acts as a trustee or acquired the shares before it became a subsidiary.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Service of documents
text: (1) A document may be served on a company or an officer thereof by sending it to the company or the officer at the registered office of the company by registered post or by speed post or by courier service or by leaving it at its registered office or by means of such electronic or other mode as may be prescribed:[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) Save as provided in this Act or the rules made thereunder for filing of documents with the Registrar in electronic mode, a document may be served on Registrar or any member by sending it to him by post or by registered post or by speed post or by courier or by delivering at his office or address, or by such electronic or other mode as may be prescribed:[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Defines the legally valid ways to send official documents or notices to a company (like a lawsuit or regulatory notice) or to its shareholders. Sending an email or using registered post to the registered office address is legally binding.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Authentication of documents, proceedings and contracts
text: Save as otherwise provided in this Act,- (a) a document or proceeding requiring authentication by a company; or (b) contracts made by or on behalf of a company, may be signed by any key managerial personnel or an officer or employee of the company duly authorised by the Board in this behalf.[cite: 17]
plain_english_summary: A startup does not need its official 'common seal' to sign everyday contracts. Any Key Managerial Personnel (like a CEO or CFO) or a specifically board-authorized employee can legally sign documents and bind the company.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF COMPANY AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Execution of bills of exchange, etc.
text: (1) A bill of exchange, hundi or promissory note shall be deemed to have been made, accepted, drawn or endorsed on behalf of a company if made, accepted, drawn, or endorsed in the name of, or on behalf of or on account of, the company by any person acting under its authority, express or implied.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) A company may, by writing under its common seal, if any, authorise any person, either generally or in respect of any specified matters, as its attorney to execute other deeds on its behalf in any place either in or outside India:[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Financial instruments like promissory notes are legally valid if signed by someone acting with the startup's authority. The company can also grant Power of Attorney to someone to execute major deeds on its behalf anywhere in the world.

title: Public offer and private placement
text: (1) A public company may issue securities- (a) to public through prospectus (herein referred to as "public offer") by complying with the provisions of this Part; (b) through private placement by complying with the provisions of Part II of this Chapter; or (c) through a rights issue or a bonus issue...[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) A private company may issue securities- (a) by way of rights issue or bonus issue in accordance with the provisions of this Act; or (b) through private placement by complying with the provisions of Part II of this Chapter.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: This is the core funding rule for startups. A private startup can ONLY raise money by offering shares directly to existing shareholders (rights/bonus issues) or to a select group of investors like VCs or angels (private placement). They are strictly forbidden from offering shares to the general public.

title: Power of Securities and Exchange Board to regulate issue and transfer of securities, etc.
text: (1) The provisions contained in this Chapter, Chapter IV and in section 127 shall,- (a) in so far as they relate to- (i) issue and transfer of securities; and (ii) non-payment of dividend, by listed companies or those companies which intend to get their securities listed... be administered by the Securities and Exchange Board...[cite: 17]

sub_structure.1_b: (b) in any other case, be administered by the Central Government.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: If a company is listed on the stock market (or planning an IPO), the rules about issuing shares are heavily regulated by SEBI. For unlisted private startups, these rules are administered by the Central Government (Ministry of Corporate Affairs).

title: Document containing offer of securities for sale to be deemed prospectus
text: (1) Where a company allots or agrees to allot any securities of the company with a view to all or any of those securities being offered for sale to the public, any document by which the offer for sale to the public is made shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be a prospectus issued by the company...[cite: 17]
plain_english_summary: If a company gives shares to an intermediary with the intention that the intermediary will sell them to the public, the document used to advertise that sale is legally treated as a formal 'prospectus' and is subject to strict liability rules.

title: Matters to be stated in prospectus
text: (1) Every prospectus issued by or on behalf of a public company either with reference to its formation or subsequently... shall be dated and signed and shall state such information and set out such reports on financial information as may be specified by the Securities and Exchange Board...[cite: 17]

sub_structure.4: (4) No prospectus shall be issued by or on behalf of a company or in relation to an intended company unless on or before the date of its publication, there has been delivered to the Registrar for registration, a copy thereof signed by every person who is named therein as a director or proposed director...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.9: (9) If a prospectus is issued in contravention of the provisions of this section, the company shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to three lakh rupees and every person who is knowingly a party to the issue of such prospectus shall be punishable... with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to three lakh rupees.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: A prospectus (the document used to pitch an IPO to the public) must contain specific financial information and risk reports mandated by SEBI. It must be registered with the government before publication. Violating these rules can lead to massive fines.

title: Variation in terms of contract or objects in prospectus
text: (1) A company shall not, at any time, vary the terms of a contract referred to in the prospectus or objects for which the prospectus was issued, except subject to the approval of, or except subject to an authority given by the company in general meeting by way of special resolution:[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) The dissenting shareholders being those shareholders who have not agreed to the proposal to vary the terms of contracts or objects referred to in the prospectus, shall be given an exit offer by promoters or controlling shareholders at such exit price, and in such manner and conditions as may be specified by the Securities and Exchange Board...[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: If a startup goes public to raise funds for 'Project A', it cannot suddenly use that money for 'Project B' unless 75% of shareholders agree. The founders must also offer to buy out any shareholders who disagree with the pivot.

title: Offer of sale of shares by certain members of company
text: (1) Where certain members of a company propose, in consultation with the Board of Directors to offer, in accordance with the provisions of any law for the time being in force, whole or part of their holding of shares to the public, they may do so in accordance with such procedure as may be prescribed.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) Any document by which the offer of sale to the public is made shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be a prospectus issued by the company and all laws and rules made thereunder as to the contents of the prospectus and as to liability in respect of mis-statements in and omission from prospectus... shall apply...[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: This governs the 'Offer for Sale' (OFS) in an IPO, where early investors or founders sell their own existing shares to the public, rather than the company issuing new shares. The document used for this is strictly treated as a full prospectus.

title: Public offer of securities to be in dematerialised form
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other provisions of this Act,- (a) every company making public offer; and (b) such other class or classes of public companies as may be prescribed, shall issue the securities only in dematerialised form by complying with the provisions of the Depositories Act, 1996 and the regulations made thereunder.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.1A: (1A) In case of such class or classes of unlisted companies as may be prescribed, the securities shall be held or transferred only in dematerialised form in the manner laid down in the Depositories Act, 1996 and the regulations made thereunder.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Companies making a public offer (IPO) cannot issue paper stock certificates; shares must be issued in a digital, dematerialised (Demat) form. The government has also expanded this rule to mandate that large unlisted companies must keep their shares in Demat form as well.

title: Advertisement of prospectus
text: Where an advertisement of any prospectus of a company is published in any manner, it shall be necessary to specify therein the contents of its memorandum as regards the objects, the liability of members and the amount of share capital of the company, and the names of the signatories to the memorandum and the number of shares subscribed for by them, and its capital structure.[cite: 17]
plain_english_summary: Any public advertisement for an upcoming stock offering must clearly state the company's core business objects, its capital structure, and who the original founding signatories are.

title: Shelf prospectus
text: (1) Any class or classes of companies, as the Securities and Exchange Board may provide by regulations in this behalf, may file a shelf prospectus with the Registrar at the stage of the first offer of securities included therein which shall indicate a period not exceeding one year as the period of validity of such prospectus which shall commence from the date of opening of the first offer of securities under that prospectus, and in respect of a second or subsequent offer of such securities issued during the period of validity of that prospectus, no further prospectus is required.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) A company filing a shelf prospectus shall be required to file an information memorandum containing all material facts relating to new charges created, changes in the financial position of the company as have occurred between the first offer of securities or the previous offer of securities and the succeeding offer of securities and such other changes as may be prescribed, with the Registrar within the prescribed time, prior to the issue of a second or subsequent offer of securities under the shelf prospectus:[cite: 17]
sub_structure.2_proviso: Provided that where a company or any other person has received applications for the allotment of securities along with advance payments of subscription before the making of any such change, the company or other person shall intimate the changes to such applicants and if they express a desire to withdraw their application, the company or other person shall refund all the monies received as subscription within fifteen days thereof.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) Where an information memorandum is filed, every time an offer of securities is made under sub-section (2), such memorandum together with the shelf prospectus shall be deemed to be a prospectus.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: A 'Shelf Prospectus' allows a company to make multiple public stock offerings over a one-year period without having to file a full new prospectus every single time. They only need to file a shorter 'information memorandum' updating investors on recent financial changes.

title: Red herring prospectus
text: (1) A company proposing to make an offer of securities may issue a red herring prospectus prior to the issue of a prospectus.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) A company proposing to issue a red herring prospectus under sub-section (1) shall file it with the Registrar at least three days prior to the opening of the subscription list and the offer.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) A red herring prospectus shall carry the same obligations as are applicable to a prospectus and any variation between the red herring prospectus and a prospectus shall be highlighted as variations in the prospectus.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.4: (4) Upon the closing of the offer of securities under this section, the prospectus stating therein the total capital raised, whether by way of debt or share capital, and the closing price of the securities and any other details as are not included in the red herring prospectus shall be filed with the Registrar and the Securities and Exchange Board.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Before a final IPO price is set, a company can issue a 'Red Herring Prospectus'. This document contains all the business details but leaves out the exact number of shares being offered and their final price.

title: Issue of application forms for securities
text: (1) No form of application for the purchase of any of the securities of a company shall be issued unless such form is accompanied by an abridged prospectus:[cite: 17]

sub_structure.1_proviso_a: Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall apply if it is shown that the form of application was issued- (a) in connection with a bona fide invitation to a person to enter into an underwriting agreement with respect to such securities; or[cite: 17]
sub_structure.1_proviso_b: (b) in relation to securities which were not offered to the public.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.2: (2) A copy of the prospectus shall, on a request being made by any person before the closing of the subscription list and the offer, be furnished to him.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) If a company makes any default in complying with the provisions of this section, it shall be liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees for each default.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: If a company offers shares to the public, the application form must always be attached to a shortened, summary version of the prospectus (an abridged prospectus). Failing to attach it results in a ₹50,000 fine per default.

title: Criminal liability for mis-statements in prospectus
text: Where a prospectus, issued, circulated or distributed under this Chapter, includes any statement which is untrue or misleading in form or context in which it is included or where any inclusion or omission of any matter is likely to mislead, every person who authorises the issue of such prospectus shall be liable under section 447:[cite: 17]

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to a person if he proves that such statement or omission was immaterial or that he had reasonable grounds to believe, and did up to the time of issue of the prospectus believe, that the statement was true or the inclusion or omission was necessary.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Founders and directors face severe criminal charges (Section 447 fraud) if they knowingly include lies or omit crucial facts in a prospectus to trick the public into investing.

title: Civil liability for mis-statements in prospectus
text: (1) Where a person has subscribed for securities of a company acting on any statement included, or the inclusion or omission of any matter, in the prospectus which is misleading and has sustained any loss or damage as a consequence thereof, the company and every person who- (a) is a director of the company at the time of the issue of the prospectus; (b) has authorised himself to be named and is named in the prospectus as a director of the company... (c) is a promoter of the company; (d) has authorised the issue of the prospectus; and (e) is an expert referred to in sub-section (5) of section 26, shall, without prejudice to any punishment to which any person may be liable under section 36, be liable to pay compensation to every person who has sustained such loss or damage.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2_a: (2) No person shall be liable under sub-section (1), if he proves— (a) that, having consented to become a director of the company, he withdrew his consent before the issue of the prospectus, and that it was issued without his authority or consent; or[cite: 17]
sub_structure.2_b: (b) that the prospectus was issued without his knowledge or consent, and that on becoming aware of its issue, he forthwith gave a reasonable public notice that it was issued without his knowledge or consent.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.2_c: (c) that, as regards every misleading statement purported to be made by an expert... it was a correct and fair representation of the statement... and he had reasonable ground to believe... that the person making the statement was competent to make it...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, where it is proved that a prospectus has been issued with intent to defraud the applicants... every person referred to in sub-section (1) shall be personally responsible, without any limitation of liability, for all or any of the losses or damages that may have been incurred...[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: If investors lose money because they relied on a misleading prospectus, the directors, promoters, and experts who signed off on it can be sued personally to compensate the investors. If the lies were intentional fraud, the founders have unlimited personal liability.

title: Punishment for fraudulently inducing persons to invest money
text: Any person who, either knowingly or recklessly makes any statement, promise or forecast which is false, deceptive or misleading, or deliberately conceals any material facts, to induce another person to enter into, or to offer to enter into,- (a) any agreement for, or with a view to, acquiring, disposing of, subscribing for, or underwriting securities; or (b) any agreement, the purpose or the pretended purpose of which is to secure a profit to any of the parties from the yield of securities or by reference to fluctuations in the value of securities; or (c) any agreement for, or with a view to obtaining credit facilities from any bank or financial institution, shall be liable for action under section 447.[cite: 17]
plain_english_summary: Making fake promises or reckless financial forecasts to convince an investor to buy your startup's shares, or to trick a bank into giving you a loan, is a severe corporate crime punishable as fraud.

title: Action by affected persons
text: A suit may be filed or any other action may be taken under section 34 or section 35 or section 36 by any person, group of persons or any association of persons affected by any misleading statement or the inclusion or omission of any matter in the prospectus.[cite: 17]
plain_english_summary: Groups of investors (or shareholder associations) who were tricked by a fake prospectus can band together to file a class-action style lawsuit against the company and its founders.

title: Punishment for personation for acquisition, etc., of securities
text: (1) Any person who- (a) makes or abets making of an application in a fictitious name to a company for acquiring, or subscribing for, its securities; or (b) makes or abets making of multiple applications to a company in different names or in different combinations of his name or surname for acquiring or subscribing for its securities; or (c) otherwise induces directly or indirectly a company to allot, or register any transfer of, securities to him, or to any other person in a fictitious name, shall be liable for action under section 447.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) The provisions of sub-section (1) shall be prominently reproduced in every prospectus issued by a company and in every form of application for securities.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) Where a person has been convicted under this section, the Court may also order disgorgement of gain, if any, made by, and seizure and disposal of the securities in possession of, such person.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.4: (4) The amount received through disgorgement or disposal of securities under sub-section (3) shall be credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: It is a severe crime to use a fake name, or multiple variations of your name, to try and hoard shares during a public offering. If caught, the court will seize the illegally acquired shares and seize any profits made from them.

title: Allotment of securities by company
text: (1) No allotment of any securities of a company offered to the public for subscription shall be made unless the amount stated in the prospectus as the minimum amount has been subscribed and the sums payable on application for the amount so stated have been paid to and received by the company by cheque or other instrument.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) The amount payable on application on every security shall not be less than five per cent. of the nominal amount of the security or such other percentage or amount, as may be specified by the Securities and Exchange Board by making regulations in this behalf.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) If the stated minimum amount has not been subscribed and the sum payable on application is not received within a period of thirty days from the date of issue of the prospectus, or such other period as may be specified by the Securities and Exchange Board, the amount received under sub-section (1) shall be returned within such time and manner as may be prescribed.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.4: (4) Whenever a company having a share capital makes any allotment of securities, it shall file with the Registrar a return of allotment in such manner as may be prescribed.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.5: (5) In case of any default under sub-section (3) or sub-section (4), the company and its officer who is in default shall be liable to a penalty, for each default, of one thousand rupees for each day during which such default continues or one lakh rupees, whichever is less.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: If a company's public offering fails to raise the minimum required amount of money within 30 days, the offering is cancelled, and all application money must be refunded to investors. Once shares are successfully allotted, the company must file a 'return of allotment' with the Registrar.

title: Securities to be dealt with in stock exchanges
text: (1) Every company making public offer shall, before making such offer, make an application to one or more recognised stock exchange or exchanges and obtain permission for the securities to be dealt with in such stock exchange or exchanges.

sub_structure.3: (3) All monies received on application from the public for subscription to the securities shall be kept in a separate bank account in a scheduled bank and shall not be utilised for any purpose other than- (a) for adjustment against allotment of securities... or (b) for the repayment of monies...
sub_structure.5: (5) If a default is made in complying with the provisions of this section, the company shall be punishable with a fine which shall not be less than five lakh rupees but which may extend to fifty lakh rupees...

plain_english_summary: If a company is going public (IPO), it must legally apply to list on a stock exchange beforehand. All investor funds raised during the offer must be parked in a separate bank account and cannot be spent until the shares are successfully allotted.

title: Global depository receipt
text: A company may, after passing a special resolution in its general meeting, issue depository receipts in any foreign country in such manner, and subject to such conditions, as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Indian companies are allowed to raise capital from foreign investors by issuing Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) in overseas markets, provided they pass a special resolution (75% shareholder approval).

title: Issue of shares on private placement basis
text: (1) A company may, subject to the provisions of this section, make a private placement of securities.

sub_structure.2: (2) A private placement shall be made only to a select group of persons who have been identified by the Board... whose number shall not exceed fifty or such higher number as may be prescribed...
sub_structure.4: (4) Every identified person willing to subscribe to the private placement issue shall apply in the private placement and application issued to such person alongwith subscription money paid either by cheque or demand draft or other banking channel and not by cash:
sub_structure.6: (6) A company making an offer or invitation under this section shall allot its securities within sixty days from the date of receipt of the application money...
sub_structure.10: (10) Subject to sub-section (11), if a company makes an offer or accepts monies in contravention of this section, the company, its promoters and directors shall be liable for a penalty which may extend to the amount raised... or two crore rupees, whichever is lower...

plain_english_summary: This is the crucial law governing startup fundraising (VC and Angel rounds). A startup can offer shares to a limited group of people (private placement). They absolutely cannot accept cash (only banking channels), must allot the shares within 60 days of receiving the money, and cannot run public ads. Violations trigger massive penalties up to ₹2 Crore.

title: Kinds of share capital
text: The share capital of a company limited by shares shall be of two kinds, namely:- (a) equity share capital- (i) with voting rights; or (ii) with differential rights as to dividend, voting or otherwise... and (b) preference share capital:

sub_structure.explanation_ii: Explanation. For the purposes of this section, (ii) "preference share capital"... means that part of the issued share capital of the company which carries or would carry a preferential right with respect to- (a) payment of dividend... and (b) repayment, in the case of a winding up or repayment of capital...

plain_english_summary: A startup can issue two main types of shares: Equity Shares (standard ownership and voting) and Preference Shares (which give the investor priority in getting dividends and getting their money back if the company shuts down). Founders can also issue equity with 'differential voting rights' (e.g., more voting power for founders).

title: Nature of shares or debentures
text: The shares or debentures or other interest of any member in a company shall be movable property transferable in the manner provided by the articles of the company.
plain_english_summary: Shares in a startup are legally classified as 'movable property'. They can be bought, sold, or transferred, subject entirely to the specific rules and restrictions written in the startup's Articles of Association.

title: Numbering of shares
text: Every share in a company having a share capital shall be distinguished by its distinctive number:

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to a share held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in such share in the records of a depository.

plain_english_summary: Every physical share issued by a company must have a unique, distinguishing number. This rule does not apply to digital (dematerialised) shares held in a depository account.

title: Certificate of shares
text: (1) A certificate, issued under the common seal, if any, of the company or signed by two directors or by a director and the Company Secretary, wherever the company has appointed a Company Secretary, specifying the shares held by any person, shall be prima facie evidence of the title of the person to such shares.

sub_structure.5: (5) If a company with intent to defraud issues a duplicate certificate of shares, the company shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than five times the face value of the shares... and every officer... shall be liable for action under section 447.

plain_english_summary: A physical share certificate, signed by two directors (or a director and the company secretary), is the official legal proof that an investor owns those shares. Issuing fake or fraudulent duplicate certificates is a severe corporate crime.

title: Voting rights
text: (1) Subject to the provisions of section 43, sub-section (2) of section 50 and sub-section (1) of section 188,- (a) every member of a company limited by shares and holding equity share capital therein, shall have a right to vote on every resolution placed before the company; and (b) his voting right on a poll shall be in proportion to his share in the paid-up equity share capital of the company.

sub_structure.2: (2) Every member... holding any preference share capital... shall, in respect of such capital, have a right to vote only on resolutions placed before the company which directly affect the rights attached to his preference shares...
sub_structure.2_proviso_2: Provided further that where the dividend in respect of a class of preference shares has not been paid for a period of two years or more, such class of preference shareholders shall have a right to vote on all the resolutions placed before the company.

plain_english_summary: Equity shareholders vote on everything, proportionate to how much of the company they own. Preference shareholders usually only vote on matters directly affecting their specific rights, BUT if a startup fails to pay them their agreed dividends for two years, they gain the right to vote on EVERYTHING.

title: Variation of shareholders' rights
text: (1) Where a share capital of the company is divided into different classes of shares, the rights attached to the shares of any class may be varied with the consent in writing of the holders of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class or by means of a special resolution passed at a separate meeting of the holders of the issued shares of that class...

sub_structure.2: (2) Where the holders of not less than ten per cent. of the issued shares of a class did not consent to such variation... they may apply to the Tribunal to have the variation cancelled...

plain_english_summary: If a startup wants to change the special rights assigned to a specific class of investors (e.g., taking away veto rights from Series A investors), they need 75% approval from that specific class. Even then, a minority group (holding 10%) can petition the Tribunal to block the change.

title: Calls on shares of same class to be made on uniform basis
text: Where any calls for further share capital are made on the shares of a class, such calls shall be made on a uniform basis on all shares falling under that class.

sub_structure.explanation: Explanation. For the purposes of this section, shares of the same nominal value on which different amounts have been paid-up shall not be deemed to fall under the same class.

plain_english_summary: When a company demands that shareholders pay the remaining unpaid balance on their shares (a 'call'), it must demand the money equally and uniformly from all shareholders within that specific class.

title: Company to accept unpaid share capital, although not called up
text: (1) A company may, if so authorised by its articles, accept from any member, the whole or a part of the amount remaining unpaid on any shares held by him, even if no part of that amount has been called up.

sub_structure.2: (2) A member of the company limited by shares shall not be entitled to any voting rights in respect of the amount paid by him under sub-section (1) until that amount has been called up.

plain_english_summary: A shareholder can pay the unpaid balance on their shares early, even if the company hasn't formally asked for it yet. However, this early advance payment does not give them any extra voting rights until the company actually issues the formal call for the money.

title: Payment of dividend in proportion to amount paid-up
text: A company may, if so authorised by its articles, pay dividends in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share.
plain_english_summary: A company's internal rules (AOA) can dictate that dividends are paid out based strictly on the amount of money the shareholder has actually paid into the company, rather than the face value of the shares they hold.

title: Application of premiums received on issue of shares
text: (1) Where a company issues shares at a premium, whether for cash or otherwise, a sum equal to the aggregate amount of the premium received on those shares shall be transferred to a "securities premium account"...

sub_structure.2: (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), the securities premium account may be applied by the company- (a) towards the issue of unissued shares of the company to the members of the company as fully paid bonus shares; (b) in writing off the preliminary expenses of the company; (c) in writing off the expenses of, or the commission paid or discount allowed on, any issue of shares or debentures... (e) for the purchase of its own shares... under section 68.

plain_english_summary: When VC funds invest in a startup at a high valuation, they buy shares at a 'premium' (above the face value). This extra money must be locked in a 'Securities Premium Account' and can only be spent on very specific things, like issuing bonus shares or writing off IPO expenses.

title: Prohibition on issue of shares at discount
text: (1) Except as provided in section 54, a company shall not issue shares at a discount.

sub_structure.2: (2) Any share issued by a company at a discount shall be void.
sub_structure.2A: (2A) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-sections (1) and (2), a company may issue shares at a discount to its creditors when its debt is converted into shares in pursuance of any statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme...
sub_structure.3: (3) Where any company fails to comply with the provisions of this section, such company and every officer who is in default shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to an amount equal to the amount raised through the issue of shares at a discount of five lakh rupees, whichever is less, and the company shall also be liable to refund all monies received with interest at the rate of twelve per cent. per annum...

plain_english_summary: A startup is strictly banned from issuing shares below their nominal face value (a discount), unless they are sweat equity shares for employees or part of a formal bankruptcy restructuring. Discounted shares are legally void, and the founders must refund the money with 12% interest.

title: Issue of sweat equity shares
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in section 53, a company may issue sweat equity shares of a class of shares already issued, if the following conditions are fulfilled, namely:- (a) the issue is authorised by a special resolution passed by the company;

sub_structure.1_b: (b) the resolution specifies the number of shares, the current market price, consideration, if any, and the class or classes of directors or employees to whom such equity shares are to be issued;
sub_structure.2: (2) The rights, limitations, restrictions and provisions as are for the time being applicable to equity shares shall be applicable to the sweat equity shares issued under this section and the holders of such shares shall rank pari passu with other equity shareholders.

plain_english_summary: Startups can legally issue 'sweat equity' shares at a discount or for non-cash consideration to founders and key employees as a reward for their intellectual property or hard work. This requires a special resolution (75% shareholder approval). These shares hold the same rights as normal equity.

title: Issue and redemption of preference shares
text: (1) No company limited by shares shall, after the commencement of this Act, issue any preference shares which are irredeemable.

sub_structure.2: (2) A company limited by shares may, if so authorised by its articles, issue preference shares which are liable to be redeemed within a period not exceeding twenty years from the date of their issue...
sub_structure.2_proviso_1: Provided that a company may issue preference shares for a period exceeding twenty years for infrastructure projects...
sub_structure.2_proviso_2_a: Provided further that- (a) no such shares shall be redeemed except out of the profits of the company which would otherwise be available for dividend or out of the proceeds of a fresh issue of shares made for the purposes of such redemption;
sub_structure.2_proviso_2_c: (c) where such shares are proposed to be redeemed out of the profits of the company, there shall, out of such profits, be transferred, a sum equal to the nominal amount of the shares to be redeemed, to a reserve, to be called the Capital Redemption Reserve Account...

plain_english_summary: A startup cannot issue permanent (irredeemable) preference shares. All preference shares must be paid back (redeemed) within 20 years. To protect creditors, the company can only buy back these shares using its own profits or by issuing new shares to cover the cost.

title: Transfer and transmission of securities
text: (1) A company shall not register a transfer of securities of the company... unless a proper instrument of transfer, in such form as may be prescribed, duly stamped, dated and executed by or on behalf of the transferor and the transferee and specifying the name, address and occupation, if any, of the transferee has been delivered to the company by the transferor or the transferee within a period of sixty days from the date of execution, along with the certificate relating to the securities...

sub_structure.4_c: (4) Every company shall... deliver the certificates of all securities allotted, transferred or transmitted- (c) within a period of one month from the date of receipt by the company of the instrument of transfer under sub-section (1)...
sub_structure.6: (6) Where any default is made in complying with the provisions of sub-sections (1) to (5), the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees.

plain_english_summary: To legally transfer physical startup shares, the buyer and seller must sign a stamped 'instrument of transfer' and give it to the company within 60 days. The company then has 1 month to issue new share certificates. Failing to do this results in a ₹50,000 penalty.

title: Punishment for personation of shareholder
text: If any person deceitfully personates as an owner of any security or interest in a company, or of any share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of this Act, and thereby obtains or attempts to obtain any such security or interest or any such share warrant or coupon, or receives or attempts to receive any money due to any such owner, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.
plain_english_summary: Pretending to be a shareholder to steal their shares, steal their dividends, or illegally transfer their equity is a severe crime punishable by a mandatory minimum of 1 year in prison and up to ₹5 lakh in fines.

title: Refusal of registration and appeal against refusal
text: (1) If a private company limited by shares refuses, whether in pursuance of any power of the company under its articles or otherwise, to register the transfer of, or the transmission by operation of law of the right to, any securities or interest of a member in the company, it shall within a period of thirty days from the date on which the instrument of transfer... was delivered to the company, send notice of the refusal to the transfer or and the transferee... giving reasons for such refusal.

sub_structure.2: (2) Without prejudice to sub-section (1), the securities or other interest of any member in a public company shall be freely transferable:
sub_structure.3: (3) The transferee may appeal to the Tribunal against the refusal within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice...
sub_structure.6: (6) If a person contravenes the order of the Tribunal under this section, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.

plain_english_summary: If a private startup refuses to let an investor sell their shares (based on restrictions in the AOA), they must notify the investor within 30 days. The investor can appeal this refusal to the Tribunal. Public company shares, however, must remain freely transferable.

title: Rectification of register of members
text: (1) If the name of any person is, without sufficient cause, entered in the register of members of a company, or after having been entered in the register, is, without sufficient cause, omitted there from, or if a default is made, or unnecessary delay takes place in entering in the register, the fact of any person having become or ceased to be a member, the person aggrieved, or any member of the company, or the company may appeal in such form as may be prescribed, to the Tribunal... for rectification of the register.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Tribunal may, after hearing the parties to the appeal under sub-section (1) by order, either dismiss the appeal or direct that the transfer or transmission shall be registered by the company within a period of ten days of the receipt of the order or direct rectification of the records... and in the latter case, direct the company to pay damages, if any, sustained by the party aggrieved.

plain_english_summary: If a founder or investor is wrongly added to, removed from, or delayed in being added to the official cap table (register of members), they can appeal to the Tribunal to force the company to correct the register and pay damages.

title: Publication of authorised, subscribed and paid-up capital
text: (1) Where any notice, advertisement or other official publication, or any business letter, billhead or letter paper of a company contains a statement of the amount of the authorised capital of the company, such notice, advertisement or other official publication, or such letter, billhead or letter paper shall also contain a statement, in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters, of the amount of the capital which has been subscribed and the amount paid-up.

sub_structure.2: (2) If any default is made in complying with the requirements of sub-section (1), the company shall be liable to pay a penalty of ten thousand rupees and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to pay a penalty of five thousand rupees, for each default.

plain_english_summary: If a startup mentions its authorized share capital on its letterhead, website, notices, or advertisements, it must display its actual subscribed and paid-up capital with equal prominence to avoid misleading the public.[cite: 17]

title: Power of limited company to alter its share capital
text: (1) A limited company having a share capital may, if so authorised by its articles, alter its memorandum in its general meeting to- (a) increase its authorised share capital by such amount as it thinks expedient; (b) consolidate and divide all or any of its share capital into shares of a larger amount than its existing shares... (c) convert all or any of its fully paid-up shares into stock... (d) sub-divide its shares... (e) cancel shares which... have not been taken...[cite: 17]

sub_structure.1_b_proviso: Provided that no consolidation and division which results in changes in the voting percentage of shareholders shall take effect unless it is approved by the Tribunal on an application made in the prescribed manner;[cite: 17]
sub_structure.2: (2) The cancellation of shares under sub-section (1) shall not be deemed to be a reduction of share capital.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Allows a company, if authorized by its AOA, to increase its authorized capital to accommodate new investors, consolidate shares, split shares into smaller denominations, or cancel unissued shares.[cite: 17]

title: Further issue of share capital
text: (1) Where at any time, a company having a share capital proposes to increase its subscribed capital by the issue of further shares, such shares shall be offered- (a) to persons who, at the date of the offer, are holders of equity shares of the company in proportion... (b) to employees under a scheme of employees' stock option... (c) to any persons, if it is authorised by a special resolution... if the price of such shares is determined by the valuation report of a registered valuer...[cite: 17]

sub_structure.1_a_i: (i) the offer shall be made by notice specifying the number of shares offered and limiting a time not being less than fifteen days or such lesser number of days as may be prescribed and not exceeding thirty days...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.1_a_ii: (ii) unless the articles of the company otherwise provide, the offer aforesaid shall be deemed to include a right exercisable by the person concerned to renounce the shares offered to him...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) Nothing in this section shall apply to the increase of the subscribed capital of a company caused by the exercise of an option as a term attached to the debentures issued or loan raised by the company to convert such debentures or loans into shares...[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Governs rights issues, ESOPs (Employee Stock Option Plans), and preferential share allotments for fundraising. Existing shareholders get the first right to new shares unless a special resolution approves an allotment to employees via ESOPs or outside investors at a price backed by a registered valuation report.[cite: 17]

title: Issue of bonus shares
text: (1) A company may issue fully paid-up bonus shares to its members, in any manner whatsoever, out of- (i) its free reserves; (ii) the securities premium account; or (iii) the capital redemption reserve account: Provided that no issue of bonus shares shall be made by capitalising reserves created by the revaluation of assets.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) No company shall capitalise its profits or reserves for the purpose of issuing fully paid-up bonus shares... unless- (a) it is authorised by its articles; (b) it has, on the recommendation of the Board, been authorised in the general meeting... (c) it has not defaulted in payment of interest or principal in respect of fixed deposits or debt securities... (d) it has not defaulted in respect of statutory dues of employees...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) The bonus shares shall not be issued in lieu of dividend.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: A startup can reward existing shareholders by issuing free bonus shares out of retained profits, the securities premium account, or the capital redemption reserve, provided it has no defaults on employee dues or debt obligations.[cite: 17]

title: Notice to be given to Registrar for alteration of share capital
text: (1) Where- (a) a company alters its share capital in any manner specified in sub-section (1) of section 61; (b) an order made by the Government... has the effect of increasing authorised capital; or (c) a company redeems any redeemable preference shares, the company shall file a notice in the prescribed form with the Registrar within a period of thirty days of such alteration or increase or redemption... along with an altered memorandum.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) Where any company fails to comply with the provisions of sub-section (1), such company and every officer who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of five hundred rupees for each day during which such default continues, subject to a maximum of five lakh rupees in case of a company and one lakh rupees in case of an officer who is in default.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Whenever a company increases its authorized share capital, redeems preference shares, or alters its share structure, it must notify the ROC within 30 days along with the amended MOA or face ongoing daily fines.[cite: 17]

title: Unlimited company to provide for reserve share capital on conversion into limited company
text: An unlimited company having a share capital may, by a resolution for registration as a limited company under this Act, do either or both of the following things, namely- (a) increase the nominal amount of its share capital by increasing the nominal amount of each of its shares... (b) provide that a specified portion of its uncalled share capital shall not be capable of being called up except in the event and for the purposes of the company being wound up.[cite: 17]
plain_english_summary: If an unlimited company converts into a limited liability company, it can create a reserve capital buffer that can only be called upon if the company is being liquidated.[cite: 17]

title: Reduction of share capital
text: (1) Subject to confirmation by the Tribunal on an application by the company, a company limited by shares or limited by guarantee and having a share capital may, by a special resolution, reduce the share capital in any manner and in particular, may- (a) extinguish or reduce the liability on any of its shares in respect of the share capital not paid-up; or (b) either with or without extinguishing or reducing liability... cancel any paid-up share capital which is lost... or pay off any paid-up share capital which is in excess of the wants of the company...[cite: 17]

sub_structure.1_proviso: Provided that no such reduction shall be made if the company is in arrears in the repayment of any deposits accepted by it... or the interest payable thereon.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.3: (3) The Tribunal may, if it is satisfied that the debt or claim of every creditor... has been discharged or determined or has been secured or his consent is obtained, make an order confirming the reduction of share capital...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.10: (10) If any officer of the company- (a) knowingly conceals the name of any creditor... (b) knowingly misrepresents the nature or amount of the debt... he shall be liable under section 447.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: A company can only formally reduce its share capital (e.g., to write off accumulated losses or return unneeded capital) with special resolution approval and strict confirmation by the NCLT. Concealing creditors during this process is treated as criminal fraud.[cite: 17]

title: Restrictions on purchase by company or giving of loans by it for purchase of its shares
text: (1) No company limited by shares or by guarantee and having a share capital shall have power to buy its own shares unless the consequent reduction of share capital is effected under the provisions of this Act. (2) No public company shall give, whether directly or indirectly and whether by means of a loan, guarantee, the provision of security or otherwise, any financial assistance for the purpose of, or in connection with, a purchase or subscription made or to be made, by any person of or for any shares in the company or in its holding company.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.3_b: (3) Nothing in sub-section (2) shall apply to- (b) the provision by a company of money in accordance with any scheme approved by company through special resolution... for the purchase of, or subscription for, fully paid-up shares... held by trustees for the benefit of the employees...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.5: (5) If a company contravenes the provisions of this section, it shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to twenty-five lakh rupees and every officer... shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine...[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Companies are prohibited from giving loans, financial assistance, or guarantees to help third parties purchase their own shares, with exceptions carved out for regulated employee share trusts. Violations carry fines up to ₹25 Lakh and potential imprisonment.[cite: 17]

title: Power of company to purchase its own securities
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, but subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), a company may purchase its own shares or other specified securities (hereinafter referred to as buy-back) out of- (a) its free reserves; (b) the securities premium account; or (c) the proceeds of the issue of any shares or other specified securities...[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2_b: (b) a special resolution has been passed at a general meeting of the company authorising the buy-back: Provided that nothing contained in this clause shall apply to a case where- (i) the buy-back is, ten per cent. or less of the total paid-up equity capital and free reserves... and (ii) such buy-back has been authorised by the Board by means of a resolution passed at its meeting;[cite: 17]
sub_structure.2_c: (c) the buy-back is twenty-five per cent. or less of the aggregate of paid-up capital and free reserves of the company...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.6: (6) Where a company proposes to buy-back its own shares... it shall, before making such buy-back, file with the Registrar and the Securities and Exchange Board, a declaration of solvency signed by atleast two directors...[cite: 17]
sub_structure.7: (7) Where a company buys back its own shares... it shall extinguish and physically destroy the shares or securities so bought back within seven days of the last date of completion of buy-back.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Regulates share buybacks. A company can buy back up to 25% of its capital and reserves using free reserves or share premium, provided its post-buyback debt-to-equity ratio does not exceed 2:1. Board approval suffices for buybacks up to 10%, but higher amounts require a special resolution and a formal declaration of solvency.[cite: 17]

title: Transfer of certain sums to capital redemption reserve account
text: (1) Where a company purchases its own shares out of free reserves or securities premium account, a sum equal to the nominal value of the shares so purchased shall be transferred to the capital redemption reserve account and details of such transfer shall be disclosed in the balance sheet.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.2: (2) The capital redemption reserve account may be applied by the company, in paying up unissued shares of the company to be issued to members of the company as fully paid bonus shares.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: When a company buys back its shares using free reserves or securities premium, an amount equal to the nominal face value of those shares must be moved into a Capital Redemption Reserve (CRR) account, which can later only be used to fund fully paid bonus shares.[cite: 17]

title: Prohibition for buy-back in certain circumstances
text: (1) No company shall directly or indirectly purchase its own shares or other specified securities- (a) through any subsidiary company including its own subsidiary companies; (b) through any investment company or group of investment companies; or (c) if a default, is made by the company, in the repayment of deposits... interest payment thereon, redemption of debentures or preference shares or payment of dividend... or repayment of any term loan...[cite: 17]

sub_structure.1_c_proviso: Provided that the buy-back is not prohibited, if the default is remedied and a period of three years has lapsed after such default ceased to subsist.[cite: 17]
sub_structure.2: (2) No company shall, directly or indirectly, purchase its own shares or other specified securities in case such company has not complied with the provisions of sections 92, 123, 127 and section 129.[cite: 17]

plain_english_summary: Barring share buybacks through subsidiaries or investment vehicles, or if the company has defaulted on deposits, debt redemption, term loans, dividends, or basic filing duties like annual returns and financial statements.[cite: 17]

title: Debentures
text: (1) A company may issue debentures with an option to convert such debentures into shares, either wholly or partly at the time of redemption: Provided that the issue of debentures with an option to convert such debentures into shares, wholly or partly, shall be approved by a special resolution passed at a general meeting. (2) No company shall issue any debentures carrying any voting rights.[cite: 17]

sub_structure.4: (4) Where debentures are issued by a company under this section, the company shall create a debenture redemption reserve account out of the profits of the company available for payment of dividend...[cite: 17]
