plain_english_summary: Only a practicing Chartered Accountant (CA) can audit a company. A startup cannot hire its own employee, someone who owns shares in the startup, or someone convicted of fraud as its auditor. An auditor also cannot audit more than 20 companies at the same time.[cite: 12]

title: Remuneration of auditors
text: (1) The remuneration of the auditor of a company shall be fixed in its general meeting or in such manner as may be determined therein: Provided that the Board may fix remuneration of the first auditor appointed by it.[cite: 12]

sub_structure.2: (2) The remuneration under sub-section (1) shall, in addition to the fee payable to an auditor, include the expenses, if any, incurred by the auditor in connection with the audit of the company and any facility extended to him but does not include any remuneration paid to him for any other service rendered by him at the request of the company.[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: The founders/Board can set the fee for the very first auditor, but for all subsequent years, the auditor's fees must be approved by the shareholders at a general meeting. This fee includes audit expenses but excludes payments for non-audit advisory work.[cite: 12]

title: Powers and duties of auditors and auditing standards
text: (1) Every auditor of a company shall have a right of access at all times to the books of account and vouchers of the company, whether kept at the registered office of the company or at any other place and shall be entitled to require from the officers of the company such information and explanation as he may consider necessary...[cite: 12]

sub_structure.2: (2) The auditor shall make a report to the members of the company on the accounts examined by him... and to the best of his information and knowledge, the said accounts, financial statements give a true and fair view of the state of the company's affairs...[cite: 12]
sub_structure.12: (12) Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, if an auditor of a company in the course of the performance of his duties as auditor, has reason to believe that an offence of fraud involving such amount or amounts as may be prescribed, is being or has been committed in the company by its officers or employees, the auditor shall report the matter to the Central Government...[cite: 12]
sub_structure.15: (15) If any auditor, cost accountant, or company secretary in practice does not comply with the provisions of sub-section (12), he shall, — (a) in case of a listed company, be liable to a penalty of five lakh rupees; and (b) in case of any other company, be liable to a penalty of one lakh rupees.[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: Auditors have total, unrestricted access to the startup's financial books. If an auditor discovers that the founders or employees are committing corporate fraud, they are legally required to report it directly to the Central Government. If they stay silent to protect the company, the auditor faces heavy fines.[cite: 12]

title: Auditor not to render certain services
text: An auditor appointed under this Act shall provide to the company only such other services as are approved by the Board of Directors or the audit committee, as the case may be, but which shall not include any of the following services (whether such services are rendered directly or indirectly to the company), or its holding company or subsidiary company, namely:— (a) accounting and book keeping services; (b) internal audit; (c) design and implementation of any financial information system; (d) actuarial services; (e) investment advisory services; (f) investment banking services; (g) rendering of outsourced financial services; (h) management services; and (i) any other kind of services as may be prescribed:[cite: 12]
plain_english_summary: To prevent a conflict of interest, the CA firm that audits a startup cannot simultaneously act as its bookkeeper, internal auditor, investment banker, or financial advisor. They must remain completely independent.[cite: 12]

title: Auditor to sign audit reports, etc.
text: The person appointed as an auditor of the company shall sign the auditor's report or sign or certify any other document of the company in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 141, and the qualifications, observations or comments on financial transactions or matters, which have any adverse effect on the functioning of the company mentioned in the auditor's report shall be read before the company in general meeting and shall be open to inspection by any member of the company.[cite: 12]
plain_english_summary: The auditor must formally sign their report. If the auditor includes any 'qualifications' (warnings that the financials are inaccurate or problematic), those warnings must be read aloud to investors at the AGM and made available for inspection.[cite: 12]

title: Auditors to attend general meeting
text: All notices of, and other communications relating to, any general meeting shall be forwarded to the auditor of the company, and the auditor shall, unless otherwise exempted by the company, attend either by himself or through his authorised representative, who shall also be qualified to be an auditor, any general meeting and shall have right to be heard at such meeting on any part of the business which concerns him as the auditor.[cite: 12]
plain_english_summary: The startup's auditor (or their qualified representative) has the right to receive notices for and attend all shareholder meetings. They also have the right to speak up if the meeting touches upon their audit findings.[cite: 12]

title: Punishment for contravention
text: (1) If any of the provisions of sections 139 to 146 (both inclusive) is contravened, the company shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees and every officer of the company who is in default shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but which may extend to one lakh rupees.[cite: 12]

sub_structure.2: (2) If an auditor of a company contravenes any of the provisions of section 139, section 143, section 144 or section 145, the auditor shall be punishable with fine... or four times the remuneration of the auditor, whichever is less: Provided that if an auditor has contravened such provisions knowingly or willfully with the intention to deceive... he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and with fine...[cite: 12]
sub_structure.3: (3) Where an auditor has been convicted under sub-section (2), he shall be liable to— (i) refund the remuneration received by him to the company; and (ii) pay for damages to the company, statutory bodies or authorities or to members or creditors of the company for loss arising out of incorrect or misleading statements...[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: If a startup messes up auditor appointments, the company and officers face fines. More importantly, if an auditor breaks the rules or lies to deceive investors, the auditor goes to jail for up to 1 year, must refund their fees, and is personally liable to pay damages to the investors they misled.[cite: 12]

title: Central Government to specify audit of items of cost in respect of certain companies
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Chapter, the Central Government may, by order, in respect of such class of companies engaged in the production of such goods or providing such services as may be prescribed, direct that particulars relating to the utilisation of material or labour or to other items of cost as may be prescribed shall also be included in the books of account kept by that class of companies:[cite: 12]

sub_structure.2: (2) If the Central Government is of the opinion, that it is necessary to do so, it may, by order, direct that the audit of cost records of class of companies... shall be conducted in the manner specified in the order.[cite: 12]
sub_structure.3: (3) The audit under sub-section (2) shall be conducted by a cost accountant who shall be appointed by the Board...[cite: 12]
sub_structure.8: (8) If any default is made in complying with the provisions of this section,— (a) the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be punishable...[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: For specific heavy industries (like manufacturing or mining), the government can order the company to maintain detailed 'cost records' tracking raw materials and labor, and require a special 'Cost Audit' by a Cost Accountant in addition to the normal financial audit.[cite: 12]

title: Company to have Board of Directors
text: (1) Every company shall have a Board of Directors consisting of individuals as directors and shall have— (a) a minimum number of three directors in the case of a public company, two directors in the case of a private company, and one director in the case of a One Person Company; and (b) a maximum of fifteen directors:[cite: 12]

sub_structure.1_proviso_1: Provided that a company may appoint more than fifteen directors after passing a special resolution:[cite: 12]
sub_structure.1_proviso_2: Provided further that such class or classes of companies as may be prescribed, shall have at least one woman director.[cite: 12]
sub_structure.3: (3) Every company shall have at least one director who stays in India for a total period of not less than one hundred and eighty-two days during the financial year...[cite: 12]
sub_structure.4: (4) Every listed public company shall have at least one-third of the total number of directors as independent directors...[cite: 12]
sub_structure.6: (6) An independent director in relation to a company, means a director other than managing director or a whole-time director or a nominee director,— (a) who, in the opinion of the Board, is a person of integrity and possesses relevant expertise and experience...[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: This sets the core rules for a startup's Board of Directors. A private startup needs at least 2 directors. At least one director on the board MUST be an Indian resident (staying 182+ days in India). The law also mandates a woman director and independent directors for larger/listed companies.[cite: 12]

title: Manner of selection of independent directors and maintenance of data bank of independent directors
text: (1) Subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (5) of section 149, an independent director may be selected from a data bank containing names, addresses and qualifications of persons who are eligible and willing to act as independent directors, maintained by any body, institute or association, as may by notified by the Central Government...[cite: 12]

sub_structure.2: (2) The appointment of independent director shall be approved by the company in general meeting...[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: If a startup needs to hire an Independent Director, they can find vetted candidates from an official government-notified data bank. The shareholders must ultimately vote to approve their appointment at a general meeting.[cite: 12]

title: Appointment of director elected by small shareholders
text: A listed company may have one director elected by such small shareholders in such manner and with such terms and conditions as may be prescribed.[cite: 12]

sub_structure.explanation: Explanation.—For the purposes of this section "small shareholders" means a shareholder doing shares of nominal value of not more than twenty thousand rupees or such other sum as may be prescribed.[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: If a startup goes public, the retail investors (small shareholders owning shares with a nominal value under ₹20,000) have the collective right to elect one director to represent their interests on the board.[cite: 12]

title: Appointment of directors
text: (1) Where no provision is made in the articles of a company for the appointment of the first director, the subscribers to the memorandum who are individuals shall be deemed to be the first directors of the company until the directors are duly appointed...[cite: 12]

sub_structure.2: (2) Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, every director shall be appointed by the company in general meeting.[cite: 12]
sub_structure.3: (3) No person shall be appointed as a director of a company unless he has been allotted the Director Identification Number under section 154...[cite: 12]
sub_structure.5: (5) A person appointed as a director shall not act as a director unless he gives his consent to hold the office as director and such consent has been filed with the Registrar within thirty days of his appointment...[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: The founders who sign the incorporation documents are automatically the first directors. After that, shareholders elect directors. Critically, no one can become a director without a unique Director Identification Number (DIN), and they must formally file their consent to act as a director with the ROC.[cite: 12]

title: Application for allotment of Director Identification Number
text: Every individual intending to be appointed as director of a company shall make an application for allotment of Director Identification Number to the Central Government in such form and manner and along with such fees as may be prescribed.[cite: 12]
plain_english_summary: Before a founder or employee can legally be added to a startup's board, they must apply to the Central Government for a unique Director Identification Number (DIN).[cite: 12]

title: Allotment of Director Identification Number
text: The Central Government shall, within one month from the receipt of the application under section 153, allot a Director Identification Number to an applicant in such manner as may be prescribed.[cite: 12]
plain_english_summary: The government is required to process the application and grant the Director Identification Number (DIN) within one month of receiving it.[cite: 12]

title: Prohibition to obtain more than one Director Identification Number
text: No individual, who has already been allotted a Director Identification Number under section 154, shall apply for, obtain or possess another Director Identification Number.[cite: 12]
plain_english_summary: A person can only have one DIN for their entire lifetime, even if they sit on the board of multiple different startups. It is illegal to hold multiple DINs.[cite: 12]

title: Director to intimate Director Identification Number
text: Every existing director shall, within one month of the receipt of Director Identification Number from the Central Government, intimate his Director Identification Number to the company or all companies wherein he is a director.[cite: 12]
plain_english_summary: Once an individual receives their DIN, they have 30 days to officially inform every startup or company where they serve as a director so the companies can update their records.[cite: 12]

title: Company to inform Director Identification Number to Registrar
text: (1) Every company shall, within fifteen days of the receipt of intimation under section 156, furnish the Director Identification Number of all its directors to the Registrar or any other officer or authority as may be specified by the Central Government...[cite: 12]

sub_structure.2: (2) If a company fails to furnish Director Identification Number under sub-section (1), before the expiry of the period specified... such company shall be liable to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees and in case of continuing failure, with a further penalty of one hundred rupees for each day... subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees, and every officer... shall be liable to a penalty...[cite: 12]

plain_english_summary: Once a startup receives a director's DIN, the company has 15 days to officially file it with the Registrar (ROC). Missing this deadline triggers an immediate ₹25,000 fine plus daily penalties for the company and its officers.[cite: 12]

title: Obligation to indicate Director Identification Number
text: Every person or company, while furnishing any return, information or particulars as are required to be furnished under this Act, shall mention the Director Identification Number in such return, information or particulars in case such return, information or particulars relate to the director or contain any reference of any director.[cite: 12]
plain_english_summary: Whenever a startup files any official forms, returns, or legal documents with the government that mention a director, they must include that director's DIN.[cite: 12]

title: Short title, extent and commencement
text: (1) This Act may be called the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.2: (2) It extends to the whole of India.[cite: 11]
sub_structure.3: (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint: Provided that different dates may be appointed for different provisions...[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: Establishes the name of the Act and confirms its jurisdiction over the entirety of India.

title: Definitions
text: (1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,-[cite: 11]

sub_structure.d: (d) "body corporate" means a company as defined in clause (20) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013 and includes- (i) a limited liability partnership registered under this Act...[cite: 11]
sub_structure.j: (j) "designated partner" means any partner designated as such pursuant to section 7;[cite: 11]
sub_structure.n: (n) "limited liability partnership" means a partnership formed and registered under this Act;[cite: 11]
sub_structure.ta: (ta) "small limited liability partnership" means a limited liability partnership-- (i) the contribution of which, does not exceed twenty-five lakh rupees... and (ii) the turnover of which... does not exceed forty lakh rupees...[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: Defines key terms for LLPs, such as what constitutes a 'body corporate', 'designated partner', and the financial thresholds that qualify a business as a 'small limited liability partnership'.

title: Limited liability partnership to be body corporate
text: (1) A limited liability partnership is a body corporate formed and incorporated under this Act and is a legal entity separate from that of its partners.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.2: (2) A limited liability partnership shall have perpetual succession.[cite: 11]
sub_structure.3: (3) Any change in the partners of a limited liability partnership shall not affect the existence, rights or liabilities of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: An LLP is a separate legal entity from its founders (a body corporate). Any changes in the partners do not affect the existence, rights, or liabilities of the LLP itself.

title: Non-applicability of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932
text: Save as otherwise provided, the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (9 of 1932) shall not apply to a limited liability partnership.[cite: 11]
plain_english_summary: The old Indian Partnership Act, 1932 does not apply to an LLP. LLPs are strictly governed by this 2008 Act.

title: Partners
text: Any individual or body corporate may be a partner in a limited liability partnership:[cite: 11]

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that an individual shall not be capable of becoming a partner of a limited liability partnership, if- (a) he has been found to be of unsound mind by a Court of competent jurisdiction... (b) he is an undischarged insolvent; or (c) he has applied to be adjudicated as an insolvent and his application is pending.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: Individuals or existing companies (body corporates) can be partners in an LLP. However, individuals who are of unsound mind or are undischarged insolvents cannot legally be partners.

title: Minimum number of partners
text: (1) Every limited liability partnership shall have at least two partners.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.2: (2) If at any time the number of partners of a limited liability partnership is reduced below two and the limited liability partnership carries on business for more than six months while the number is so reduced, the person, who is the only partner... after those six months and has the knowledge of the fact... shall be liable personally for the obligations of the limited liability partnership incurred during that period.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: An LLP must have at least 2 partners. If a partner leaves and the LLP operates with only 1 partner for more than 6 months, that solo partner loses their limited liability protection and becomes personally responsible for the LLP's new debts.

title: Designated partners
text: (1) Every limited liability partnership shall have at least two designated partners who are individuals and at least one of them shall be a resident in India:[cite: 11]

sub_structure.1_proviso: Provided that in case of a limited liability partnership in which all the partners are bodies corporate... at least two individuals who are partners of such limited liability partnership or nominees of such bodies corporate shall act as designated partners.[cite: 11]
sub_structure.6: (6) Every designated partner of a limited liability partnership shall obtain a Designated Partner Identification Number (DPIN) from the Central Government...[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: An LLP must have at least two 'Designated Partners' (who must be actual people, not companies), and at least one must be a resident of India. They must obtain a Designated Partner Identification Number (DPIN) from the government.

title: Liabilities of designated partners
text: Unless expressly provided otherwise in this Act, a designated partner shall be- (a) responsible for the doing of all acts, matters and things as are required to be done by the limited liability partnership in respect of compliance of the provisions of this Act including filing of any document, return, statement... and (b) liable to all penalties imposed on the limited liability partnership for any contravention of those provisions.[cite: 11]
plain_english_summary: Designated partners are the ones legally responsible for ensuring the LLP complies with the law (like filing annual returns) and are the ones personally held liable for penalties if the LLP breaks these rules.

title: Changes in designated partners
text: A limited liability partnership may appoint a designated partner within thirty days of a vacancy arising for any reason...[cite: 11]

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that if no designated partner is appointed, or if at any time there is only one designated partner, each partner shall be deemed to be a designated partner.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: If a designated partner leaves, the LLP has 30 days to appoint a replacement. If they fail to do so, every single regular partner is legally treated as a designated partner (meaning everyone shares the compliance liability).

title: Punishment for contravention of sections 7 and 9
text: (1) If the limited liability partnership contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 7, the limited liability partnership and its every partner shall be liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees and in case of continuing contravention, with a further penalty of one hundred rupees for each day after the first... subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees for the limited liability partnership and fifty thousand rupees for every partner of such limited liability partnership.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.3: (3) If the limited liability partnership contravenes the provisions of sub-section (5) of section 7 or section 9, such limited liability partnership and its every partner shall be liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees... subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees for the limited liability partnership and fifty thousand rupees for its every partner.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: Failing to maintain the minimum number of designated partners, or failing to appoint a replacement within 30 days, results in a base penalty of ₹10,000 plus daily fines up to ₹1 Lakh for the LLP and ₹50,000 for every partner.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Incorporation document
text: (1) For a limited liability partnership to be incorporated, - (a) two or more persons associated for carrying on a lawful business with a view to profit shall subscribe their names to an incorporation document;[cite: 11]

sub_structure.1_c: (c) there shall be filed along with the incorporation document, a statement in the prescribed form, made by either an advocate, or a Company Secretary or a Chartered Accountant or a Cost Accountant... that all the requirements of this Act and the rules made thereunder have been complied with...[cite: 11]
sub_structure.3: (3) If a person makes a statement under clause (c) of sub-section (1) which he- (a) knows to be false; or (b) does not believe to be true, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: To register an LLP, partners must file an incorporation document backed by a professional (like a CA or CS). Making a false statement during this incorporation process is a severe crime punishable by up to 2 years in prison and a fine up to ₹5 Lakh.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Incorporation by registration
text: (1) When the requirements imposed by clauses (b) and (c) of sub-section (1) of section 11 have been complied with, the Registrar shall retain the incorporation document and... he shall, within a period of fourteen days- (a) register the incorporation document; and (b) give a certificate that the limited liability partnership is incorporated by the name specified therein.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.4: (4) The certificate shall be conclusive evidence that the limited liability partnership is incorporated by the name specified therein.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: Once the Registrar accepts the incorporation documents, they will issue a formal certificate within 14 days, which serves as conclusive legal proof that the LLP exists.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Registered office of limited liability partnership and change therein
text: (1) Every limited liability partnership shall have a registered office to which all communications and notices may be addressed and where they shall be received.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.3: (3) A limited liability partnership may change the place of its registered office and file the notice of such change with the Registrar... and any such change shall take effect only upon such filing.[cite: 11]
sub_structure.4: (4) If any default is made in complying with the requirements of this section, the limited liability partnership and its every partner shall be liable to a penalty of five hundred rupees for each day during which the default continues, subject to a maximum of fifty thousand rupees for the limited liability partnership and its every partner.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: Every LLP must maintain a registered office where legal notices can be sent. Failing to have one or failing to notify the Registrar of an address change triggers a daily penalty of ₹500, up to ₹50,000 for both the LLP and its partners.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Effect of registration
text: On registration, a limited liability partnership shall, by its name, be capable of- (a) suing and being sued; (b) acquiring, owning, holding and developing or disposing of property, whether movable or immovable, tangible or intangible; (c) having a common seal, if it decides to have one; and (d) doing and suffering such other acts and things as bodies corporate may lawfully do and suffer.[cite: 11]
plain_english_summary: Once registered, the LLP becomes a legal entity that can sue, be sued, buy property, and have a common seal in its own name.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Name
text: (1) Every limited liability partnership shall have either the words "limited liability partnership" or the acronym "LLP" as the last words of its name.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.2: (2) No limited liability partnership shall be registered by a name which, in the opinion of the Central Government is- (a) undesirable; or (b) identical or too nearly resembles to that of any other limited liability partnership or a company or a registered trade mark of any other person...[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: An LLP's name must legally end with the words 'limited liability partnership' or the acronym 'LLP'. The government will reject names that are undesirable or too similar to existing companies or trademarks.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Reservation of name
text: (1) A person may apply in such form and manner and accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed to the Registrar for the reservation of a name set out in the application as- (a) the name of a proposed limited liability partnership; or (b) the name to which a limited liability partnership proposes to change its name.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.2: (2) Upon receipt of an application under sub-section (1) and on payment of the prescribed fee, the Registrar may... reserve the name for a period of three months from the date of intimation by the Registrar.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: Founders can apply to the Registrar to reserve a proposed name for their new LLP or a name change. If approved, the name is reserved for three months.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Rectification of name of limited liability partnership
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in sections 15 and 16, if through inadvertence or otherwise, a limited liability partnership, on its first registration or on its registration by a new name, is registered by a name which is identical with or too nearly resembles to-- (a) that of any other limited liability partnership or a company; or (b) a registered trade mark... the Central Government may direct that such limited liability partnership to change its name or new name within a period of three months...[cite: 11]

sub_structure.3: (3) If the limited liability partnership is in default in complying with any direction given under sub-section (1), the Central Government shall allot a new name to the limited liability partnership in such manner as may be prescribed and the Registrar shall enter the new name in the register...[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: If an LLP accidentally registers a name that infringes on an existing trademark or company name, the government will order them to change it within 3 months. If they ignore the order, the government will forcefully assign them a new name.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Change of registered name
text: Any limited liability partnership may change its name registered with the Registrar by filing with him a notice of such change in such form and manner and on payment of such fees as may be prescribed.[cite: 11]
plain_english_summary: An LLP can officially change its name by filing a notice of the change with the Registrar and paying the prescribed fee.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Penalty for improper use of words "limited liability partnership" or "LLP"
text: If any person or persons carry on business under any name or title of which the words "Limited Liability Partnership" or "LLP" or any contraction or imitation thereof is or are the last word or words, that person or each of those persons shall, unless duly incorporated as limited liability partnership, be punishable with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.[cite: 11]
plain_english_summary: It is illegal for any business to use the words 'Limited Liability Partnership' or 'LLP' in their name if they are not officially registered as one. Doing so carries a fine between ₹50,000 and ₹5 Lakh.

chapter_title: INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
title: Publication of name and limited liability
text: (1) Every limited liability partnership shall ensure that its invoices, official correspondence and publications bear the following, namely:- (a) the name, address of its registered office and registration number of the limited liability partnership; and (b) a statement that it is registered with limited liability.[cite: 11]

sub_structure.2: (2) If the limited liability partnership contravenes the provisions of this section, the limited liability partnership shall be liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees.[cite: 11]

plain_english_summary: An LLP must clearly print its name, registered office address, registration number, and a statement that it has limited liability on all its invoices and official letters. Violating this rule carries a ₹10,000 penalty.

title: Eligibility to be partners
text: On the incorporation of a limited liability partnership, the persons who subscribed their names to the incorporation document shall be its partners and any other person may become a partner of the limited liability partnership by and in accordance with the limited liability partnership agreement.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: The original founders who sign the incorporation documents automatically become the first partners. Anyone else can join as a partner later, but only according to the rules set out in the LLP Agreement.

title: Relationship of partners
text: (1) Save as otherwise provided by this Act, the mutual rights and duties of the partners of a limited liability partnership, and the mutual rights and duties of a limited liability partnership and its partners, shall be governed by the limited liability partnership agreement between the partners, or between the limited liability partnership and its partners.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) The limited liability partnership agreement and any changes, if any, made therein shall be filed with the Registrar in such form, manner and accompanied by such fees as may be prescribed.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.4: (4) In the absence of agreement as to any matter, the mutual rights and duties of the partners and the mutual rights and duties of the limited liability partnership and the partners shall be determined by the provisions relating to that matter as are set-out in the First Schedule.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The LLP Agreement acts as the constitution for the partners, defining all their rights and duties. It must be officially filed with the Registrar. If the agreement is silent on a specific issue, the default rules in the First Schedule of the LLP Act will apply.

title: Cessation of partnership interest
text: (1) A person may cease to be a partner of a limited liability partnership in accordance with an agreement with the other partners or, in the absence of agreement with the other partners as to cessation of being a partner, by giving a notice in writing of not less than thirty days to the other partners of his intention to resign as partner.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) A person shall cease to be a partner of a limited liability partnership- (a) on his death or dissolution of the limited liability partnership; or (b) if he is declared to be of unsound mind by a competent court; or (c) if he has applied to be adjudged as an insolvent or declared as an insolvent.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.5: (5) Where a partner of a limited liability partnership ceases to be a partner, unless otherwise provided in the limited liability partnership agreement, the former partner or a person entitled to his share... shall be entitled to receive... (a) an amount equal to the capital contribution of the former partner... and (b) his right to share in the accumulated profits... after the deduction of accumulated losses...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: A partner can resign by following the LLP agreement or by giving 30 days' written notice. When a partner leaves (or dies), they or their heirs are entitled to get back their capital contribution and their share of the accumulated profits, minus any losses, unless the agreement says otherwise.

title: Registration of changes in partners
text: (1) Every partner shall inform the limited liability partnership of any change in his name or address within a period of fifteen days of such change.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) A limited liability partnership shall- (a) where a person becomes or ceases to be a partner, file a notice with the Registrar within thirty days from the date he becomes or ceases to be a partner; and (b) where there is any change in the name or address of a partner, file a notice with the Registrar within thirty days...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.4: (4) If the limited liability partnership contravenes the provisions of sub-section (2), the limited liability partnership and its every designated partner shall be liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.5: (5) If the contravention referred to in sub-section (1) is made by any partner of the limited liability partnership, such partner shall be liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If a partner changes their name or address, they must tell the LLP within 15 days (or face a ₹10,000 fine). If a partner joins, leaves, or changes their details, the LLP must inform the Registrar within 30 days (or face a ₹10,000 fine).

chapter_title: EXTENT AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND PARTNERS
title: Partner as agent
text: Every partner of a limited liability partnership is, for the purpose of the business of the limited liability partnership, the agent of the limited liability partnership, but not of other partners.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: In an LLP, a partner acts as an agent for the company itself, meaning their business actions bind the LLP. However, unlike a traditional partnership, they do not act as agents for the other partners, shielding the other partners from personal liability for their actions.

chapter_title: EXTENT AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND PARTNERS
title: Extent of liability of limited liability partnership
text: (1) A limited liability partnership is not bound by anything done by a partner in dealing with a person if- (a) the partner in fact has no authority to act for the limited liability partnership in doing a particular act; and (b) the person knows that he has no authority or does not know or believe him to be a partner of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) The limited liability partnership is liable if a partner of a limited liability partnership is liable to any person as a result of a wrongful act or omission on his part in the course of the business of the limited liability partnership or with its authority.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: (3) An obligation of the limited liability partnership whether arising in contract or otherwise, shall be solely the obligation of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.4: (4) The liabilities of the limited liability partnership shall be met out of the property of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: An LLP's debts are its own; creditors can only go after the LLP's assets, not the partners' personal assets. The LLP is responsible for a partner's wrongful actions if done during official business, but it isn't responsible if a partner secretly goes rogue and makes deals they had no authority to make.

chapter_title: EXTENT AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND PARTNERS
title: Extent of liability of partner
text: (1) A partner is not personally liable, directly or indirectly for an obligation referred to in sub-section (3) of section 27 solely by reason of being a partner of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) The provisions of sub-section (3) of section 27 and sub-section (1) of this section shall not affect the personal liability of a partner for his own wrongful act or omission, but a partner shall not be personally liable for the wrongful act or omission of any other partner of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: This is the core 'Limited Liability' protection. A partner is never personally responsible for the LLP's debts or for the mistakes and wrongful acts of other co-founders. They are only personally liable for their *own* wrongful acts or fraud.

chapter_title: EXTENT AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND PARTNERS
title: Holding out
text: (1) Any person, who by words spoken or written or by conduct, represents himself, or knowingly permits himself to be represented to be a partner in a limited liability partnership is liable to any person who has on the faith of any such representation given credit to the limited liability partnership...[cite: 6]

sub_structure.1_proviso: Provided that where any credit is received by the limited liability partnership as a result of such representation, the limited liability partnership shall, without prejudice to the liability of the person so representing himself or represented to be a partner, be liable to the extent of credit received by it or any financial benefit derived thereon.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If you fake being a partner in an LLP (or let someone else claim you are) to trick a bank or supplier into giving the LLP a loan or credit, you can be held personally liable to repay that debt.

chapter_title: EXTENT AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND PARTNERS
title: Unlimited liability in case of fraud
text: (1) In the event of an act carried out by a limited liability partnership, or any of its partners, with intent to defraud creditors of the limited liability partnership or any other person, or for any fraudulent purpose, the liability of the limited liability partnership and partners who acted with intent to defraud creditors or for any fraudulent purpose shall be unlimited for all or any of the debts or other liabilities of the limited liability partnership:[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) Where any business is carried on with such intent or for such purpose as mentioned in sub-section (1), every person who was knowingly a party to the carrying on of the business in the manner aforesaid shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The 'Limited Liability' shield is instantly destroyed if the LLP or its partners commit fraud. Any partner involved in defrauding creditors faces unlimited personal liability for those debts, plus up to 5 years in prison and heavy fines.

chapter_title: EXTENT AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND PARTNERS
title: Whistle blowing
text: (1) The Court or Tribunal may reduce or waive any penalty leviable against any partner or employee of a limited liability partnership, if it is satisfied that- (a) such partner or employee of a limited liability partnership has provided useful information during investigation of such limited liability partnership; or (b) when any information given by any partner or employee... leads to limited liability partnership or any partner or employee of such limited liability partnership being convicted under this Act or any other Act.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) No partner or employee of any limited liability partnership may be discharged, demoted, suspended, threatened, harassed or in any other manner discriminated against the terms and conditions of his limited liability partnership or employment merely because of his providing information or causing information to be provided pursuant to sub-section (1).[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Protects whistleblowers. If a partner or employee exposes fraud or illegal activity within the LLP to the authorities, the court can reduce or waive their personal penalties. It is strictly illegal for the LLP to fire, demote, or harass an employee for whistleblowing.

title: Form of contribution
text: (1) A contribution of a partner may consist of tangible, movable or immovable or intangible property or other benefit to the limited liability partnership, including money, promissory notes, other agreements to contribute cash or property, and contracts for services performed or to be performed.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) The monetary value of contribution of each partner shall be accounted for and disclosed in the accounts of the limited liability partnership in the manner as may be prescribed.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: A founder's 'buy-in' to an LLP doesn't just have to be cash. They can contribute property, software (intangible property), or even a contract to perform future services (sweat equity). However, a clear monetary value must be assigned to these contributions in the official accounts.

title: Obligation to contribute
text: (1) The obligation of a partner to contribute money or other property or other benefit or to perform services for a limited liability partnership shall be as per the limited liability partnership agreement.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) A creditor of a limited liability partnership, which extends credit or otherwise acts in reliance on an obligation described in that agreement, without notice of any compromise between partners, may enforce the original obligation against such partner.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If the LLP agreement states a partner must contribute ₹10 Lakhs, they are legally bound to do so. If the LLP takes a loan from a bank based on the promise of that ₹10 Lakhs coming in, the bank can force the partner to pay up even if the partners later secretly agreed to cancel the contribution.

title: Maintenance of books of account, other records and audit, etc.
text: (1) The limited liability partnership shall maintain such proper books of account as may be prescribed relating to its affairs for each year of its existence on cash basis or accrual basis and according to double entry system of accounting and shall maintain the same at its registered office for such period as may be prescribed.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) Every limited liability partnership shall, within a period of six months from the end of each financial year, prepare a Statement of Account and Solvency for the said financial year as at the last day of the said financial year in such form as may be prescribed, and such statement shall be signed by the designated partners...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: (3) Every limited liability partnership shall file within the prescribed time, the Statement of Account and Solvency prepared pursuant to sub-section (2) with the Registrar every year...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.4: (4) The accounts of limited liability partnerships shall be audited in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed: Provided that the Central Government may... exempt any class or classes of limited liability partnerships from the requirements of this sub-section.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.5: (5) Any limited liability partnership which fails to comply with the provisions of sub-section (3), such limited liability partnership and its designated partners shall be liable to a penalty of one hundred rupees for each day during which such failure continues...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.6: (6) Any limited liability partnership which fails to comply with the provisions of sub-section (1), sub-section (2) and sub-section (4), such limited liability partnership shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees, but may extend to five lakh rupees...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: LLPs must maintain proper double-entry accounting records. Every year, within 6 months of the financial year-end, they must prepare and file a 'Statement of Account and Solvency' with the ROC. Failure to maintain records, get audited, or file on time triggers severe fines and daily penalties.

title: Accounting and auditing standards
text: The Central Government may, in consultation with the National Financial Reporting Authority constituted under section 132 of the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013),-- (a) prescribe the standards of accounting; and (b) prescribe the standards of auditing, as recommended by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India... for a class or classes of limited liability partnerships.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: The government, working with the NFRA and ICAI, has the power to set the specific official accounting and auditing standards that LLPs must follow when preparing their finances.

title: Annual return
text: (1) Every limited liability partnership shall file an annual return duly authenticated with the Registrar within sixty days of closure of its financial year in such form and manner and accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) If any limited liability partnership fails to file its annual return under sub-section (1) before the expiry of the period specified therein, such limited liability partnership and its designated partners shall be liable to a penalty of one hundred rupees for each day during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees for the limited liability partnership and fifty thousand rupees for designated partners.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Every LLP must file an Annual Return (Form 11) with the ROC within 60 days of the end of the financial year. Missing this deadline results in an automatic daily penalty of ₹100 for both the LLP and the designated partners.

title: Inspection of documents kept by Registrar
text: The incorporation document, names of partners and changes, if any, made therein, Statement of Account and Solvency and annual return filed by each limited liability partnership with the Registrar shall be available for inspection by any person in such manner and on payment of such fee as may be prescribed.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: LLP filings are public records. Anyone (like an investor, competitor, or creditor) can pay a small fee to the government to inspect an LLP's incorporation details, list of partners, and financial statements.

title: Penalty for false statement
text: If in any return, statement or other document required by or for the purposes of any of the provisions of this Act, any person makes a statement- (a) which is false in any material particular, knowing it to be false; or (b) which omits any material fact knowing it to be material, he shall, save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five lakh rupees but which shall not be less than one lakh rupees.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: Lying or hiding important facts on any official LLP document (like an annual return or financial statement) is a serious crime. The person responsible can be sent to prison for up to 2 years and fined up to ₹5 Lakh.

title: Power of Registrar to obtain information
text: (1) In order to obtain such information as the Registrar may consider necessary for the purposes of carrying out the provisions of this Act, the Registrar may require any person including any present or former partner or designated partner or employee of a limited liability partnership to answer any question or make any declaration or supply any details or particulars in writing to him within a reasonable period.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) In case any person referred to in sub-section (1) does not answer such question or make such declaration... the Registrar shall have power to summon that person to appear before him or an inspector...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: (3) Any person who, without lawful excuse, fails to comply with any summons or requisition of the Registrar under this section shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than two thousand rupees but which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The ROC has the power to demand information or issue a legal summons requiring any current or former partner, or employee, to answer questions about the LLP. Ignoring this summons results in a fine.

title: Compounding of offences
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), the Regional Director or any other officer... authorised by the Central Government may compound any offence under this Act which is punishable with fine only, by collecting from a person reasonably suspected of having committed the offence, a sum which may extend to the amount of the maximum fine provided for the offence but shall not be lower than the minimum amount provided for the offence.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) Nothing contained in sub-section (1) shall apply to an offence committed by a limited liability partnership or its partner or its designated partner within a period of three years from the date on which similar offence committed by it or him was compounded under this section.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If an LLP commits a minor offense (one punishable only by a fine, not prison), they can admit the mistake and 'compound' it by paying a settlement fee to the Regional Director to avoid prosecution. However, repeat offenses within a 3-year window cannot be compounded.

title: Destruction of old records
text: The Registrar may destroy any document filed or registered with him in physical form or in electronic form in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: The Registrar is legally authorized to permanently delete or destroy old LLP filings and records based on the timelines set by government rules.

title: Enforcement of duty to make returns, etc.
text: (1) If any limited liability partnership is in default in complying with- (a) any provisions of this Act or of any other law which requires the filing in any manner with the Registrar of any return, account or other document... and fails to make good the default within fourteen days after the service on the limited liability partnership of a notice... the Tribunal may, on application by the Registrar, make an order directing that limited liability partnership or its designated partners or its partners to make good the default within such time as specified in the order.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) Any such order may provide that all the costs of and incidental to the application shall be borne by that limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If an LLP ignores notices to file its required returns, the Registrar can take them to the Tribunal. The Tribunal can legally force the partners to file the documents and make the LLP pay all the legal costs of the court application.

chapter_title: ASSIGNMENT AND TRANSFER OF PARTNERSHIP RIGHTS
title: Partner's transferable interest
text: (1) The rights of a partner to a share of the profits and losses of the limited liability partnership and to receive distributions in accordance with the limited liability partnership agreement are transferable either wholly or in part.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) The transfer of any right by any partner pursuant to sub-section (1) does not by itself cause the disassociation of the partner or a dissolution and winding up of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: (3) The transfer of right pursuant to this section does not, by itself, entitle the transferee or assignee to participate in the management or conduct of the activities of the limited liability partnership, or access information concerning the transactions of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: A partner can transfer or sell their right to receive profits from the LLP to someone else. However, this buyer only gets the money—they do not officially become a partner, they cannot vote, and they cannot interfere in the management of the startup.

title: Investigation of the affairs of limited liability partnership
text: (1) The Central Government shall appoint one or more competent persons as inspectors to investigate the affairs of a limited liability partnership and to report thereon in such manner as it may direct if- (a) the Tribunal... declares that the affairs of the limited liability partnership ought to be investigated; or (b) any Court... declares that the affairs of a limited liability partnership ought to be investigated.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.3_a: (a) if not less than one-fifth of the total number of partners of the limited liability partnership make an application along with supporting evidence and security amount as may be prescribed;[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3_c_i: (i) that the business of the limited liability partnership is being or has been conducted with an intent to defraud its creditors, partners or any other person, or otherwise for a fraudulent or unlawful purpose...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The Central Government will appoint official inspectors to investigate an LLP if ordered by a court or Tribunal. The government can also launch an investigation if 20% of the partners request it, or if there is suspicion that the LLP is defrauding creditors or operating illegally.

title: Application by partners for investigation
text: An application by partners of the limited liability partnership under clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 43 shall be supported by such evidence as the Tribunal may require for the purpose of showing that the applicants have good reason for requiring the investigation and the Central Government may, before appointing an inspector, require the applicants to give security, of such amount as may be prescribed, for payment of costs of the investigation.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: If partners want the government to investigate their own LLP, they must provide solid evidence justifying the request. The government can also force them to deposit a security amount to cover the costs of the investigation.

title: Firm, body corporate or association not to be appointed as inspector
text: No firm, body corporate or other association shall be appointed as an inspector.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: Only individuals (natural persons) can be appointed as official inspectors to investigate an LLP. A company or an accounting firm cannot be appointed as the inspector.

title: Power of inspectors to carry out investigation into affairs of related entities, etc.
text: (1) If an inspector appointed by the Central Government to investigate the affairs of a limited liability partnership thinks it necessary for the purposes of his investigation to investigate also the affairs of an entity which has been associated in the past or is presently associated with the limited liability partnership or any present or former partner or designated partner... the inspector shall have the power to do so...[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) In the case of any entity or partner or designated partner referred to in sub-section (1), the inspector shall not exercise his power of investigating into, and reporting on, its or his affairs without obtaining the prior approval of the Central Government thereto:[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: An inspector investigating an LLP has the power to expand their investigation to look into related companies, parent entities, or the personal affairs of past/present partners, provided they get prior approval from the Central Government.

title: Production of documents and evidence
text: (1) It shall be the duty of the designated partner and partners of the limited liability partnership- (a) to preserve and to produce before an inspector... all books and papers of, or relating to, the limited liability partnership... and (b) otherwise to give to the inspector all assistance in connection with the investigation which they are reasonably able to give.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.4: (4) An inspector may examine on oath- (a) any of the persons referred to in sub-section (1); (b) with the previous approval of the Central Government, any other person in relation to the affairs of the limited liability partnership...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.5: (5) If any person fails without reasonable cause or refuses- (a) to produce before an inspector... any book or paper... or (b) to furnish any information... or (c) to appear before the inspector personally... he shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than two thousand rupees but which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Partners are legally obligated to hand over all books, records, and documents to the inspector and must answer questions under oath. Refusing to cooperate or hiding documents carries a minimum fine of ₹2,000.

title: Seizure of documents by inspector
text: (1) Where in the course of investigation, the inspector has reasonable ground to believe that the books and papers of, or relating to, the limited liability partnership or other entity or partner or designated partner of such limited liability partnership may be destroyed, mutilated, altered, falsified or secreted, the inspector may make an application to the Judicial Magistrate of the first class... for an order for the seizure of such books and papers.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2_a: (2) After considering the application and hearing the inspector... the Magistrate may, by order, authorise the inspector- (a) to enter, with such assistance, as may be required, the place or places where such books and papers are kept;[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: (3) The inspector shall keep in his custody the books and papers seized under this section for such period not later than the conclusion of the investigation... Provided that the books and papers shall not be kept seized for a continuous period of more than six months:[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If an inspector suspects that partners might destroy or alter financial records, they can get a Magistrate's warrant to raid the office, search the premises, and physically seize the documents for up to 6 months.

title: Inspector's report
text: (1) The Inspector may, and if so directed by the Central Government, shall make interim reports to that Government, and on the conclusion of the investigation, shall make a final report to the Central Government and any such report shall be written or printed, as the Central Government may direct.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) The Central Government- (a) shall forward a copy of any report (other than an interim report) made by the inspectors to the limited liability partnership at its registered office, and also to any other entity or person dealt with or related to the report;[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: After finishing the investigation, the inspector must submit a final, formal report to the Central Government. The government will then send a copy of this final report to the LLP's registered office.

title: Prosecution
text: If, from the report under section 49, it appears to the Central Government that any person in relation to the limited liability partnership or in relation to any other entity whose affairs have been investigated, has been guilty of any offence for which he is liable, the Central Government may prosecute such person for the offence; and it shall be the duty of all partners, designated partners and and other employees and agents... to give the Central Government all assistance in connection with the prosecution...[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: If the inspector's report uncovers criminal activity, the Central Government will initiate prosecution against the guilty individuals. All other partners and employees are legally obligated to help the government with the prosecution.

title: Application for winding up of limited liability partnership
text: If any such limited liability partnership is liable to be wound up under this Act or any other law for the time being in force, and it appears to the Central Government from any such report under section 49 that it is expedient to do so by reason of any such circumstances as are referred to in sub-clause (i) or sub-clause (ii) of clause (c) of sub-section (3) of section 43, the Central Government may... cause to be presented to the Tribunal by any person authorised by the Central Government in this behalf, a petition for the winding up of the limited liability partnership on the ground that it is just and equitable that it should be wound up.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: If the investigation reveals that the LLP was built for fraud or is operating illegally, the Central Government can step in and petition the Tribunal to immediately shut down (wind up) the LLP in the public interest.

title: Proceedings for recovery of damages or property
text: If, from any report under section 49, it appears to the Central Government that proceedings ought, in the public interest, to be brought by the limited liability partnership or any entity whose affairs have been investigated,- (a) for the recovery of damages in respect of any fraud, misfeasance or other misconduct in connection with the promotion or formation, or the management of the affairs, of such limited liability partnership... or (b) for the recovery of any property of such limited liability partnership... which has been misapplied or wrongfully retained, the Central Government may itself bring proceedings for that purpose.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: If founders or partners stole money or property from the LLP, the Central Government has the authority to sue them on behalf of the LLP to recover the stolen assets or claim damages for fraud.

title: Expenses of investigation
text: (1) The expenses of, and incidental to, an investigation by an inspector appointed by the Central Government under this Act shall be defrayed in the first instance by the Central Government; but the following persons shall, to the extent mentioned below, be liable to reimburse the Central Government in respect of such expenses, namely:- (a) any person who is convicted on a prosecution, or who is ordered to pay damages or restore any property in proceedings brought by virtue of section 52...[cite: 6]

sub_structure.1_b: (b) any entity in whose name proceedings are brought as aforesaid shall be liable, to the extent of the amount or value of any sums or property recovered by it as a result of the proceedings;[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The government will initially pay for the investigation. However, if a partner is convicted of fraud, or if the LLP recovers stolen money thanks to the investigation, they will be forced to reimburse the government for the costs of the investigation.

title: Inspector's report to be evidence
text: A copy of any report of any inspector or inspectors appointed under the provisions of this Act, authenticated in such manner, if any, as may be prescribed, shall be admissible in any legal proceeding as evidence in relation to any matter contained in the report.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: The official report generated by the government inspector is legally admissible as direct evidence in any court case against the LLP or its partners.

title: Conversion from firm into limited liability partnership
text: A firm may convert into a limited liability partnership in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter and the Second Schedule.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: A traditional partnership firm can legally upgrade and convert into an LLP by following the rules laid out in the Second Schedule of this Act.

title: Conversion from private company into limited liability partnership
text: A private company may convert into a limited liability partnership in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter and the Third Schedule.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: A private limited company can legally restructure and convert itself into an LLP by following the rules laid out in the Third Schedule of this Act.

title: Conversion from unlisted public company into limited liability partnership
text: An unlisted public company may convert into a limited liability partnership in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter and the Fourth Schedule.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: An unlisted public company can legally convert itself into an LLP by following the rules laid out in the Fourth Schedule of this Act.

title: Registration and effect of conversion
text: (1) The Registrar, on satisfying that a firm, private company or an unlisted public company, as the case may be, has complied with the provisions of the Second Schedule, the Third Schedule or the Fourth Schedule... shall... register the documents submitted under such Schedule and issue a certificate of registration...[cite: 6]

sub_structure.1_proviso: Provided that the limited liability partnership shall, within fifteen days of the date of registration, inform the concerned Registrar of Firms or Registrar of Companies... about the conversion...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.4_b: (b) all tangible (movable or immovable) and intangible property vested in the firm or the company... and the whole of the undertaking of the firm or the company... shall be transferred to and shall vest in the limited liability partnership without further assurance, act or deed;[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: When a startup converts into an LLP, the Registrar issues a new certificate. Automatically, all assets, properties, IP, and liabilities of the old company transfer seamlessly to the new LLP without the founders needing to sign separate transfer deeds.

title: Foreign limited liability partnerships
text: The Central Government may make rules for provisions in relation to establishment of place of business by foreign limited liability partnerships within India and carrying on their business therein by applying or incorporating, with such modifications, as appear appropriate, the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013...[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: The Central Government has the authority to create specific rules that dictate how foreign LLPs can legally set up an office and conduct business inside India.

chapter_title: COMPROMISE, ARRANGEMENT OR RECONSTRUCTION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIPS
title: Compromise, or arrangement of limited liability partnerships
text: (1) Where a compromise or arrangement is proposed- (a) between a limited liability partnership and its creditors; or (b) between a limited liability partnership and its partners, the Tribunal may, on the application of the limited liability partnership or of any creditor or partner... order a meeting of the creditors or of the partners...[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) If a majority representing three-fourths in value of the creditors, or partners... agree to any compromise or arrangement, the compromise or arrangement shall, if sanctioned by the Tribunal, by order be binding on all the creditors or all the partners...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.4: (4) If default is made in complying with the provisions of sub-section (3), the limited liability partnership and its every designated partner shall be liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees, and in case of continuing default, with a further penalty of one hundred rupees for each day...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If an LLP needs to restructure its debts with creditors or reorganize its partners, it needs a 75% majority vote from the affected group and approval from the Tribunal. The final approved plan must be filed with the Registrar; failing to file it triggers a ₹10,000 fine.

chapter_title: COMPROMISE, ARRANGEMENT OR RECONSTRUCTION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIPS
title: Power of Tribunal to enforce compromise or arrangement
text: (1) Where the Tribunal makes an order under section 60 sanctioning a compromise or an arrangement in respect of a limited liability partnership, it- (a) shall have power to supervise the carrying out of the compromise or an arrangement; and (b) may... give such directions in regard to any matter or make such modifications in the compromise or arrangement as it may consider necessary...[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) If the Tribunal aforesaid is satisfied that a compromise or an arrangement sanctioned under section 60 cannot be worked satisfactorily with or without modifications, it may... make an order for winding up the limited liability partnership...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The Tribunal has the authority to supervise and modify any approved debt restructuring or compromise plan. If the plan fails and the LLP cannot be saved, the Tribunal can order the LLP to be forcefully wound up and shut down.

chapter_title: COMPROMISE, ARRANGEMENT OR RECONSTRUCTION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIPS
title: Provisions for facilitating reconstruction or amalgamation of limited liability partnerships
text: (1) Where an application is made to the Tribunal under section 60 for sanctioning of a compromise or arrangement... for the purposes of, or in connection with, a scheme for the reconstruction of any limited liability partnership... or the amalgamation of any two or more limited liability partnerships... the Tribunal may... make provisions for all or any of the following matters, namely:- (i) the transfer to the transferee limited liability partnership of the whole or any part of the undertaking, property or liabilities...[cite: 6]

sub_structure.3: (3) Within thirty days after the making of an order under this section, every limited liability partnership in relation to which the order is made shall cause a certified copy thereof to be filed with the Registrar for registration.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.4: (4) If default is made in complying with the provisions of sub-section (3), the limited liability partnership and its every designated partner shall be liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees, and in case of the continuing default, with a further penalty of one hundred rupees for each day...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.explanation_ii: Explanation. For the purposes of this section,- ... (ii) a "limited liability partnership" shall not be amalgamated with a company.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Covers mergers and acquisitions (M&A) of LLPs. If an LLP merges with another, the Tribunal can order the seamless transfer of all properties and liabilities to the new entity. Failing to register this order with the ROC carries a ₹10,000 fine. Importantly, an LLP cannot legally merge with a traditional Company.

title: Winding up and dissolution
text: The winding up of a limited liability partnership may be either voluntary or by the Tribunal and limited liability partnership, so wound up may be dissolved.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: An LLP can be shut down (wound up) either voluntarily by its partners or forcefully by an order of the Tribunal.

title: Circumstances in which limited liability partnership may be wound up by Tribunal
text: A limited liability partnership may be wound up by the Tribunal,- (a) if the limited liability partnership decides that limited liability partnership be wound up by the Tribunal; (b) if, for a period of more than six months, the number of partners of the limited liability partnership is reduced below two;[cite: 6]

sub_structure.d: (d) if the limited liability partnership has acted against the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the State or public order;[cite: 6]
sub_structure.e: (e) if the limited liability partnership has made a default in filing with the Registrar the Statement of Account and Solvency or annual return for any five consecutive financial years; or[cite: 6]
sub_structure.f: (f) if the Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and equitable that the limited liability partnership be wound up.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Lists the specific reasons the Tribunal can forcefully shut down an LLP, including: operating with less than 2 partners for over 6 months, acting against national security, failing to file financial returns for 5 consecutive years, or if the Tribunal simply decides it is 'just and equitable' to do so.

title: Rules for winding up and dissolution
text: The Central Government may make rules for the provisions in relation to winding up and dissolution of limited liability partnerships.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: Grants the Central Government the power to create the specific rules and procedures governing how an LLP is wound up and dissolved.

title: Business transactions of partner with limited liability partnership
text: A partner may lend money to and transact other business with the limited liability partnership and has the same rights and obligations with respect to the loan or other transactions as a person who is not a partner.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: A founder/partner can legally lend money to their own LLP or do business with it. When they do, they are treated legally just like any other outside creditor or vendor.

title: Application of the provisions of the Companies Act
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that any of the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 specified in the notification- (a) shall apply to any limited liability partnership; or (b) shall apply to any limited liability partnership with such exception, modification and adaptation, as may be specified, in the notification.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: The government has the power to take specific sections of the Companies Act and apply them directly to LLPs, with or without modifications.

title: Establishment of Special Courts
text: (1) The Central Government may, for the purpose of providing speedy trial of offences under this Act, by notification, establish or designate as many Special Courts as may be necessary for such area or areas, as may be specified in the notification.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) The Special Court shall consist of- (a) a single Judge holding office as Sessions Judge or Additional Sessions Judge, in case of offences punishable under this Act with imprisonment of three years or more; and (b) a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class, in the case of other offences...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The government can set up 'Special Courts' specifically designed to provide speedy trials for criminal offenses committed under the LLP Act.

title: Procedure and powers of Special Court
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), all offences specified under sub-section (1) of section 67A shall be triable only by the Special Court established or designated for the area in which the registered office of the limited liability partnership is situated...[cite: 6]

sub_structure.3: (3) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), the Special Court may, if it thinks fit, try in a summary way any offence under this Act which is punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years:[cite: 6]
