plain_english_summary: Special Courts have the exclusive jurisdiction to try major LLP offenses in their assigned area, and they have the power to conduct summary (fast-track) trials for offenses carrying less than 3 years of imprisonment.

title: Appeal and revision
text: The High Court may exercise, so far as may be applicable, all the powers conferred by Chapters XXIX and XXX of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) on a High Court, as if a Special Court within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the High Court were a Court of Sessions trying cases within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the High Court.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: If an LLP or partner wants to appeal a criminal decision or sentence handed down by a Special Court, that appeal goes directly to the High Court.

title: Electronic filing of documents
text: (1) Any document required to be filed, recorded or registered under this Act may be filed, recorded or registered in such manner and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) A copy of or an extract from any document electronically filed with or submitted to the Registrar which is supplied or issued by the Registrar and certified through affixing digital signature as per the Information Technology Act, 2000 (21 of 2000) to be a true copy... shall, in any proceedings, be admissible in evidence as of equal validity with the original document.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: LLPs are legally allowed to file all their official documents, returns, and registrations electronically. Documents downloaded from the Registrar bearing an official digital signature hold the exact same legal weight in court as the physical originals.

title: Registration offices
text: (1) For the purpose of exercising such powers and discharging such functions as are conferred on the Central Government by or under this Act or under rules made thereunder and for the purpose of registration of limited liability partnerships under this Act, the Central Government shall, by notification, establish such number of registration offices at such places as it thinks fit, specifying their jurisdiction.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) The Central Government may appoint such Registrars, Additional Registrars, Joint Registrars, Deputy Registrars and Assistant Registrars as it considers necessary...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The Central Government has the authority to set up official registration offices across the country and appoint Registrars to handle LLP registrations and compliance enforcement.

title: Payment of additional fee
text: Any document or return required to be registered or filed under this Act with Registrar, if, is not registered or filed in time provided therein, may be registered or filed after that time, on payment of such additional fee as may be prescribed in addition to any fee as is payable for filing of such document or return:[cite: 6]

sub_structure.proviso_1: Provided that such document or return shall be filed after the due date of filing, without prejudice to any other action or liability under this Act:[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If an LLP misses a filing deadline, it can still file the document later by paying an additional late fee. However, paying the late fee does not protect the LLP from facing other legal penalties for missing the deadline in the first place.

title: Enhanced punishment
text: In case a limited liability partnership or any partner or designated partner of such limited liability partnership commits any offence, the limited liability partnership or any partner or designated partner shall, for the second or subsequent offence, be punishable with imprisonment as provided, but in case of offences for which fine is prescribed either along with or exclusive of imprisonment, with fine which shall be twice the amount of fine for such offence.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: Repeat offenders face strict consequences. If an LLP or its partners commit the exact same offense a second time, the standard financial fines prescribed in the Act are automatically doubled.

title: Application of other laws not barred
text: The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of, the provisions of any other law for the time being in force.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: The LLP Act does not cancel out other laws. LLPs still have to comply with all other applicable Indian laws, such as tax codes, labor laws, and the Contract Act.

title: Jurisdiction of Tribunal and Appellate Tribunal
text: (1) The Tribunal shall exercise such powers and perform such functions as are, or may be, conferred on it by or under this Act or any other law for the time being in force.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) Any person aggrieved by an order of Tribunal may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal: Provided that no appeal shall lie to the Appellate Tribunal from an order made by the Tribunal with the consent of parties.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: (3) Every appeal preferred under sub-section (2) shall be filed within a period of sixty days from the date on which the copy of the order of the Tribunal is made available...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) handles LLP disputes and corporate actions. If an LLP or partner disagrees with an NCLT order, they have exactly 60 days to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT).

title: General penalties
text: If a limited liability partnership or any partner or any designated partner or any other person contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder... and for which no penalty or punishment is provided elsewhere in this Act, the limited liability partnership or any partner or any designated partner... shall be liable to a penalty of five thousand rupees and in case of a continuing contravention with a further penalty of one hundred rupees for each day after the first... subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: This is the catch-all penalty. If an LLP or partner breaks any rule in this Act that doesn't already have a specific fine attached to it, they are slapped with a base penalty of ₹5,000, plus ₹100 for every single day the violation continues (capped at ₹1 Lakh).

title: Power of Registrar to strike defunct limited liability partnership off register
text: Where the Registrar has reasonable cause to believe that a limited liability partnership is not carrying on business or its operation, in accordance with the provisions of this Act, the name of limited liability partnership may be struck off the register of limited liability partnerships in such manner as may be prescribed:[cite: 6]

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that the Registrar shall, before striking off the name of any limited liability partnership under this section, give such limited liability partnership a reasonable opportunity of being heard.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: If an LLP completely stops doing business and becomes inactive, the Registrar has the legal power to formally strike its name off the public register and shut it down. However, the Registrar must give the partners a chance to explain themselves before pulling the plug.

title: Offences to limited liability partnerships
text: Where an offence under this Act committed by a limited liability partnership is proved- (a) to have been committed with the consent or connivance of a partner or partners or designated partner or designated partners of the limited liability partnership; or (b) to be attributable to any neglect on the part of the partner or partners or designated partner... the partner or partners... as well as that limited liability partnership shall be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: If an LLP commits a corporate crime, the 'limited liability' veil does not protect the guilty individuals. Any partner who actively consented to the crime, or whose extreme negligence allowed the crime to happen, will be held personally guilty and punished alongside the LLP.

title: Adjudication of penalties
text: (1) For the purposes of adjudging penalties under this Act, the Central Government may, by an order published in the Official Gazette, appoint as many officers of the Central Government, not below the rank of Registrar, as adjudicating officers in such manner as may be prescribed.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.3_a_proviso_2: Provided further that notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, if penalty is payable for non-compliance of any of the provisions of this Act by a small limited liability partnership or a start-up limited liability partnership or by its partner... then such limited liability partnership or its partner... shall be liable to a penalty which shall be one-half of the penalty specified in such provisions subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.explanation: Explanation.--For the purposes of this proviso, the expression "start-up limited liability partnership" means a limited liability partnership incorporated under this Act and recognised as such in accordance with the notifications issued by the Central Government...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: The government appoints specific Adjudicating Officers to hand out penalties to LLPs. Crucially for founders, if a business is officially recognized as a 'start-up LLP' or a 'small LLP', they receive a 50% discount on standard penalties, capped at a maximum of ₹1 Lakh.

title: Jurisdiction of Court
text: Subject to the provisions contained in section 67A and section 67B, on and from the date of establishment or designation of Special Courts under this Act,-- (i) the Special Court referred to in clause (a) of sub-section (2) of section 67A shall have jurisdiction and power to impose punishment under section 30 of the Act; and (ii) the criminal cases... shall be transferred to the Special Court...[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: Clarifies that once Special Courts are established, they have the exclusive power to handle severe criminal cases (like fraud under Section 30) and any pending cases will be transferred to them.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: No court, other than the Special Courts referred to in section 67A, shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act or the rules made thereunder save on a complaint in writing made by the Registrar or by any officer not below the rank of Registrar duly authorised by the Central Government for this purpose.[cite: 6]
plain_english_summary: A court will only hear a criminal case against an LLP if the official complaint is filed in writing by the Registrar or an authorized government officer. Private individuals cannot directly launch criminal prosecutions under this Act.

title: Power to alter Schedules
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, alter any of the provisions contained in any of the Schedules to this Act.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) Any alteration notified under sub-section (1) shall have effect as if enacted in the Act and shall come into force on the date of the notification...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: (3) Every alteration made by the Central Government under sub-section (1) shall be laid... before each House of Parliament...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government the power to update or change the Schedules attached to the LLP Act without passing a whole new law, subject to Parliament's review.

title: Power to make rules
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: (2) In particular, and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters...[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: (3) Every rule made under this Act by the Central Government shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament...[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to create detailed operational rules (like specific forms, fees, and procedures) required to actually enforce the LLP Act.

title: Power to remove difficulties
text: (1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act as may appear to it to be necessary for removing the difficulty: Provided that no such order shall be made under this section after the expiry of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.1A: (1A) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), if any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act as amended by the Limited Liability Partnership (Amendment) Act, 2021, the Central Government may... make such provisions... for removing the difficulty:[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: A transitional provision that allows the government to issue quick fixes if practical problems arise when the LLP Act (or its amendments) are first launched, valid only for a short window of time.

title: PROVISIONS REGARDING MATTERS RELATING TO MUTUAL RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF PARTNERS AND LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND ITS PARTNERS APPLICABLE IN THE ABSENCE OF ANY AGREEMENT ON SUCH MATTERS
text: 1. The mutual rights and duties of the partners and the mutual rights and duties of the limited liability partnership and its partners shall be determined, subject to the terms of any limited liability partnership agreement or in the absence of any such agreement on any matter, by the provisions in this Schedule.[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: 2. All the partners of a limited liability partnership are entitled to share equally in the capital, profits and losses of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.5: 5. Every partner may take part in the management of the limited liability partnership.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.7: 7. No person may be introduced as a partner without the consent of all the existing partners.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.14: 14. All disputes between the partners arising out of the limited liability partnership agreement which cannot be resolved in terms of such agreement shall be referred for arbitration as per the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (26 of 1996).[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: This is the default 'LLP Agreement'. If founders start an LLP but fail to write their own custom agreement, these standard legal rules automatically apply: profits are shared equally, all partners get a say in management, new partners require 100% consent, and disputes must go to arbitration.

title: CONVERSION FROM FIRM INTO LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP
text: 1. Interpretation. In this Schedule, unless the context otherwise requires,- (a) "firm" means a firm as defined in section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (9 of 1932);[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: 2. Conversion from firm into limited liability partnership. -(1) A firm may convert into a limited liability partnership by complying with the requirements as to the conversion set out in this Schedule.[cite: 6]
sub_structure.3: 3. Eligibility for conversion. A firm may apply to convert into a limited liability partnership in accordance with this Schedule if and only if the partners of the limited liability partnership into which the firm is to be converted, comprise, all the partners of the firm and no one else.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Provides the exact step-by-step legal procedure and requirements for converting an old-school traditional partnership firm into a modern LLP. Crucially, the partners in the new LLP must be the exact same people as the partners in the old firm.

title: CONVERSION FROM PRIVATE COMPANY INTO LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP
text: 1. Interpretation. In this Schedule, unless the context otherwise requires,- (a) "company" means a private company as defined in clause (iii) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013(18 of 2013);[cite: 6]

sub_structure.2: 2. Eligibility for conversion of private companies into limited liability partnership. (1) A company may convert into a limited liability partnership by complying with the requirements... (2) A company may apply to convert... if and only if- (a) there is no security interest in its assets subsisting or in force at the time of application; and (b) the partners of the limited liability partnership to which it converts comprise all the shareholders of the company and no one else.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Outlines the specific legal process for a Private Limited Company to convert itself into an LLP. A company can only do this if it has no existing loans/liens secured against its assets, and the partners of the new LLP must be the exact same people as the shareholders of the old company.

title: CONVERSION FROM UNLISTED PUBLIC COMPANY INTO LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP
text: 1. Interpretation.- (1) In this Schedule, unless the context otherwise requires,- (a) "company" means an unlisted public company;[cite: 6]

sub_structure.3: 3. Eligibility for conversion. A company may apply to convert into a limited liability partnership in accordance with the provisions of this Schedule if and only if- (a) there is no security interest in its assets subsisting or in force at the time of application; and (b) the partners of the limited liability partnership to which it converts comprise all the shareholders of the company and no one else.[cite: 6]

plain_english_summary: Details the legal procedure for converting an Unlisted Public Company into an LLP. Just like private companies, they must clear all asset security interests (secured loans) before applying, and the ownership structure cannot change during the conversion.

title: Short title, extent, commencement
text: This Act may be called the Indian Contract Act, 1872. It extends to the whole of India... And it shall come into force on the first day of September, 1872.
plain_english_summary: Establishes the name of the Act, confirms it applies across the whole of India, and states its commencement date of September 1, 1872.

title: Interpretation-clause
text: In this Act the following words and expressions are used in the following senses, unless a contrary intention appears from the context:-

sub_structure.a: (a) When one person signifies to another his willingness to do or to abstain from doing anything, with a view to obtaining the assent of that other to such act or abstinence, he is said to make a proposal;
sub_structure.b: (b) When the person to whom the proposal is made signifies his assent thereto, the proposal is said to be accepted. A proposal, when accepted, becomes a promise;
sub_structure.c: (c) The person making the proposal is called the "promisor", and the person accepting the proposal is called the "promisee";
sub_structure.d: (d) When, at the desire of the promisor, the promisee or any other person has done or abstained from doing, or does or abstains from doing, or promises to do or to abstain from doing, something, such act or abstinence or promise is called a consideration for the promise;
sub_structure.e: (e) Every promise and every set of promises, forming the consideration for each other, is an agreement;
sub_structure.h: (h) An agreement enforceable by law is a contract;
sub_structure.i: (i) An agreement which is enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties thereto, but not at the option of the other or others, is a voidable contract;
sub_structure.j: (j) A contract which ceases to be enforceable by law becomes void when it ceases to be enforceable.

plain_english_summary: Defines foundational contract terminology for founders: a proposal + acceptance = a promise; promises with a 'consideration' (value exchanged) = an agreement; and an agreement enforceable by law = a contract. It also distinguishes between valid, voidable, and void contracts.

chapter_title: OF THE COMMUNICATION, ACCEPTANCE AND REVOCATION OF PROPOSALS
title: Communication, acceptance and revocation of proposals
text: The communication of proposals, the acceptance of proposals, and the revocation of proposals and acceptances, respectively, are deemed to be made by any act or omission of the party proposing, accepting or revoking, by which he intends to communicate such proposal, acceptance or revocation, or which has the effect of communicating it.
plain_english_summary: Explains that making an offer, accepting it, or canceling it can be communicated through any action, conduct, or omission by a party that effectively conveys their intent.

chapter_title: OF THE COMMUNICATION, ACCEPTANCE AND REVOCATION OF PROPOSALS
title: Communication when complete
text: The communication of a proposal is complete when it comes to the knowledge of the person to whom it is made. The communication of an acceptance is complete,- as against the proposer, when it is put in a course of transmission to him... and as against the acceptor, when it comes to the knowledge of the proposer.
plain_english_summary: Sets the timeline for legal communication: an offer is complete when the other person receives it. An acceptance is complete the moment it is sent (like mailing a letter or hitting send on an email), binding the person who made the offer.

chapter_title: OF THE COMMUNICATION, ACCEPTANCE AND REVOCATION OF PROPOSALS
title: Revocation of proposals and acceptances
text: A proposal may be revoked at any time before the communication of its acceptance is complete as against the proposer, but not afterwards. An acceptance may be revoked at any time before the communication of the acceptance is complete as against the acceptor, but not afterwards.
plain_english_summary: An offer can be canceled (revoked) at any time before the other person finishes communicating their acceptance. Once acceptance is officially transmitted, the deal is locked in and cannot be unilaterally canceled.

chapter_title: OF THE COMMUNICATION, ACCEPTANCE AND REVOCATION OF PROPOSALS
title: Revocation how made
text: A proposal is revoked- (1) by the communication of notice of revocation by the proposer to the other party; (2) by the lapse of time prescribed in such proposal for its acceptance... (3) by the failure of the acceptor to fulfill a condition precedent to acceptance; or (4) by the death or insanity of the proposer...
plain_english_summary: An offer dies and can no longer be accepted if: the person who made it cancels it, the stated deadline expires, the other party fails a pre-condition, or the person making the offer dies or becomes insane before acceptance.

chapter_title: OF THE COMMUNICATION, ACCEPTANCE AND REVOCATION OF PROPOSALS
title: Acceptance must be absolute
text: In order to convert a proposal into a promise, the acceptance must— (1) be absolute and unqualified; (2) be expressed in some usual and reasonable manner, unless the proposal prescribes the manner in which it is to be accepted.
plain_english_summary: For an agreement to form, an acceptance must be total and unconditional. If someone says 'I accept, but with these new changes', that counts as a counter-offer, not an acceptance.

chapter_title: OF THE COMMUNICATION, ACCEPTANCE AND REVOCATION OF PROPOSALS
title: Acceptance by performing conditions, or receiving consideration
text: Performance of the conditions of a proposal, or the acceptance of any consideration of a reciprocal promise which may be offered with a proposal, is an acceptance of the proposal.
plain_english_summary: You don't always have to sign a paper to accept an offer. Fulfilling the conditions of an offer (like completing a requested task or accepting payment/goods) legally counts as full acceptance.

chapter_title: OF THE COMMUNICATION, ACCEPTANCE AND REVOCATION OF PROPOSALS
title: Promises, express and implied
text: Insofar as the proposal or acceptance of any promise is made in words, the promise is said to be express. Insofar as such proposal or acceptance is made otherwise than in words, the promise is said to be implied.
plain_english_summary: Contracts can be 'express' (spoken or written explicitly in words) or 'implied' (created through actions and conduct, like boarding a public bus). Both are legally binding.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: What agreements are contracts
text: All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.
plain_english_summary: This is the master checklist for a legally binding contract. An agreement is only a valid contract if it has: 1) Free consent of both parties, 2) Competent parties (sane adults), 3) Lawful consideration (legal value exchanged), and 4) A lawful objective.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Who are competent to contract
text: Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.
plain_english_summary: To sign a valid contract in India, a person must be an adult (majority age), of sound mind, and not legally disqualified (such as being an undischarged insolvent or convicted felon). Contracts signed by minors are entirely void.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: What is a sound mind for the purposes of contracting
text: A person is said to be of sound mind for the purpose of making a contract if, at the time when he makes it, he is capable of understanding it and of forming a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interests.
plain_english_summary: Defines sound mind: a person is competent if they can understand the terms of the contract and rationally judge how it impacts their financial or personal interests at the exact moment they sign it.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: "Consent" defined
text: Two or more persons are said to consent when they agree upon the same thing in the same sense.
plain_english_summary: True 'consent' means both parties are thinking about the exact same thing in the exact same way (Meeting of the Minds / Consensus ad idem).

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: "Free consent" defined
text: Consent is said to be free when it is not caused by— (1) coercion, as defined in section 15; or (2) undue influence, as defined in section 16; or (3) fraud, as defined in section 17; or (4) misrepresentation, as defined in section 18; or (5) mistake, subject to the provisions of sections 20, 21 and 22.
plain_english_summary: Consent is only 'free' if it is given willingly. If a contract is signed under physical force, psychological manipulation, fraud, false statements, or mutual factual error, consent is legally defective.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: "Coercion" defined
text: "Coercion" is the committing, or threatening to commit, any act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code, or the unlawful detaining, or threatening to detain, any property, to the prejudice of any person whatever, with the intention of causing any person to enter into an agreement.
plain_english_summary: Coercion means forcing someone to sign a contract by using physical violence, criminal threats, or unlawfully holding their property hostage.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: "Undue influence" defined
text: (1) A contract is said to be induced by "undue influence" where the relations subsisting between the parties are such that one of the parties is in a position to dominate the will of the other and uses that position to obtain an unfair advantage over the other.

sub_structure.2: (2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing principle, a person is deemed to be in a position to dominate the will of another— (a) where he holds a real or apparent authority over the other... or (b) where he stands in a fiduciary relation to the other... or (c) where he makes a contract with a person whose mental capacity is temporarily or permanently affected...

plain_english_summary: Undue influence happens when someone in a position of power or trust (like a boss over an employee, a doctor over a patient, or a parent over a child) abuses that relationship to force or manipulate the weaker party into an unfair contract.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: "Fraud" defined
text: "Fraud" means and includes any of the following acts committed by a party to a contract... with intent to deceive another party or his agent or to induce him to enter into the contract:- (1) the suggestion, as a fact, of that which is not true, by one who does not believe it to be true; (2) the active concealment of a fact by one having knowledge or belief of the fact; (3) a promise made without any intention of performing it...
plain_english_summary: Defines legal fraud in contracts: telling intentional lies, actively hiding crucial facts, making promises you never intend to keep, or any other act designed to trick someone into signing an agreement.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: "Misrepresentation" defined
text: "Misrepresentation" means and includes— (1) the positive assertion, in a manner not warranted by the information of the person making it, of that which is not true, though he believes it to be true; (2) any breach of duty which, without an intent to deceive, gains an advantage to the person committing it... (3) causing, however innocently, a party to an agreement to make a mistake as to the substance of the thing which is the subject of the agreement.
plain_english_summary: Misrepresentation occurs when someone states something false as a fact, but *without* the deliberate intent to cheat (unlike fraud). Even if it was an honest mistake or careless error, it misleads the other party.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Voidability of agreements without free consent
text: When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that, if such consent was caused by misrepresentation or by fraud... the contract, nevertheless, is not voidable, if the party whose consent was so caused had the means of discovering the truth with ordinary diligence.

plain_english_summary: If you are tricked by fraud, misrepresentation, or forced by coercion into signing a contract, that contract is 'voidable'—meaning the victim can choose to cancel it. However, if the victim could easily have discovered the truth with basic common sense and ordinary diligence, they may lose the right to cancel.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Agreement void where both parties are under mistake as to matter of fact
text: Where both the parties to an agreement are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement, the agreement is void.
plain_english_summary: If both parties sign a contract while laboring under a fundamental mutual misunderstanding about a core fact (e.g., selling a car that was secretly destroyed in a fire before the deal was made), the agreement is completely void from day one.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Effect of mistake as to law
text: A contract is not voidable because it was caused by a mistake as to any law in force in India; but a mistake as to a law not in force in India has the same effect as a mistake of fact.
plain_english_summary: Ignorance of Indian law is no excuse. You cannot cancel a contract just because you misunderstood or made a mistake regarding an Indian law. However, a mistake regarding foreign law is treated like a mistake of fact (making it voidable).

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Contract caused by mistake of one party as to matter of fact
text: A contract is not voidable merely because it was caused by one of the parties to it being under a mistake as to a matter of fact.
plain_english_summary: If only *one* party makes a unilateral mistake about a fact (while the other party knew nothing about it), the contract cannot be canceled. Both parties must be mistaken for it to be void under Section 20.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not
text: The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless- it is forbidden by law; or is of such a nature that, if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law; or is fraudulent; or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another; or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.
plain_english_summary: An agreement is completely illegal and void if its purpose or money exchanged involves breaking the law, committing fraud, harming someone else, or violating public policy (e.g., an agreement to commit a crime or take a bribe).

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Agreements void, if considerations and objects unlawful in part
text: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one or any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, the agreement is void.
plain_english_summary: If a contract involves multiple parts, but even a small part of the core consideration or object is illegal, the entire contract is tainted and rendered completely void.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Agreement without consideration, void, unless it is in writing and registered or is a promise to compensate for something done or is a promise to pay a debt barred by limitation law
text: An agreement made without consideration is void, unless— (1) it is expressed in writing and registered under the law for the time being in force for the registration of documents and is made on account of natural love and affection between parties standing in a near relation to each other; or (2) it is a promise to compensate, wholly or in part, a person who has already voluntarily done something for the promisor... or (3) it is a promise, made in writing and signed by the person to be charged therewith... to pay wholly or in part a debt of which the creditor might have enforced payment but for the law for the limitation of suits.
plain_english_summary: As a rule, a promise without 'consideration' (value given in return) is a gift and legally unenforceable. However, key exceptions exist: written agreements made out of natural love and affection between close family members, promises to compensate someone for past voluntary help, or signed promises to pay off time-barred debts.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Agreement in restraint of marriage, void
text: Every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person, other than a minor, is void.
plain_english_summary: Any contract that restricts an adult from getting married (e.g., an agreement stating 'if you marry X, I will sue you') is completely void and legally unenforceable.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
text: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. Exception 1.—Saving of agreement not to carry on business of which goodwill is sold.—One who sells the goodwill of a business may agree with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business, within specified local limits...
plain_english_summary: Crucial for founders and employment contracts: Any clause that completely stops someone from practicing their trade or profession is legally void. However, a narrow exception allows non-compete clauses when selling the goodwill of a business or during active employment.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void
text: Every agreement,— (a) by which any party is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals... or (b) which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights... is void to that extent.
plain_english_summary: You cannot draft a contract that completely bans a party from going to court to resolve a dispute, nor can you arbitrarily shorten the legal statute of limitations to sue (such as stating 'you must sue us within 10 days or lose all rights'). Such clauses are void.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Agreements void for uncertainty
text: Agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void.
plain_english_summary: Contracts must be clear. If an agreement is so vague, ambiguous, or incomplete that its true meaning cannot be figured out (e.g., agreeing to sell 'oil' without specifying which kind, quantity, or price), the agreement is void for uncertainty.

chapter_title: OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
title: Agreements by way of wager, void
text: Agreements by way of wager are void; and no suit shall be brought for recovering anything alleged to be won on any wager, or entrusted to any person to abide the result of any game or other uncertain event on which any wager is made.
plain_english_summary: Wagering (gambling or betting) agreements are completely void in India. You cannot file a lawsuit in an Indian court to recover money won on a bet or lottery.

title: "Contingent contract" defined
text: A "contingent contract" is a contract to do or not to do something, if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen.
plain_english_summary: A contingent contract is an 'if-then' agreement—a contract where performance depends on whether a specific uncertain future event happens or doesn't happen (like an insurance policy payout triggered only if a house catches fire).

title: Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening
text: Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened. If the event becomes impossible, such contracts become void.
plain_english_summary: You cannot sue to enforce a conditional contract until the required future event actually happens. If it becomes mathematically or legally impossible for that event to happen, the contract automatically dies and becomes void.

title: Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event not happening
text: Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event does not happen can be enforced when the time fixed for such event has expired and has not happened, or, before it has expired, if it becomes certain that such event will not happen.
plain_english_summary: If a contract states something will happen *if an event does not happen*, you can enforce it once the deadline passes without the event occurring, or as soon as it becomes certain the event cannot possibly happen.

title: When event on which contract is contingent to be deemed impossible, if it is the future conduct of a living person
text: If the future event on which a contract is contingent is the way in which a person will act at an unspecified time, the event shall be considered to become impossible when such person does anything which renders it impossible that he should so act within any definite time...
plain_english_summary: If a contract depends on someone's future behavior or choice, that condition becomes 'impossible' if that person takes an action that makes their original behavior permanently undoable.

title: When contracts become void which are contingent on happening of specified event within fixed time
text: Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if a specified uncertain future event happens within a fixed time become void if, at the expiration of the time fixed, such event has not happened, or if, before the time fixed, such event becomes impossible.
plain_english_summary: If a contract says 'we will do X if event Y happens within 6 months', and the 6 months pass without event Y happening, the contract becomes void.

title: Agreement contingent on impossible events, void
text: Contingent agreements to do or not to do anything, if an impossible event happens, are void, whether the impossibility of the event is known or not to the parties to the agreement at the time when it is made.
plain_english_summary: An agreement based on a physically or legally impossible condition (e.g., 'I will pay you ₹10 Lakhs if you touch the sun') is entirely void, whether the parties knew it was impossible or not.

title: Obligation of parties to contracts
text: The parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless such performance is dispensed with or excused under the provisions of this Act, or of any other law.
plain_english_summary: Both parties are strictly obligated to fulfill their promises under a contract, unless excused by law or released by the other party.

title: Effect of refusal to accept offer of performance
text: Where a promisor has made an offer of performance to the promisee, and the offer has not been accepted, the promisor is not responsible for non-performance, nor does he thereby lose his rights under the contract.
plain_english_summary: If you try to deliver on your contractual promise (an 'tender of performance'), but the other person unreasonably refuses to accept it, you are legally off the hook and do not lose your rights under the contract.

title: Effect of refusal of party to perform promise wholly
text: When a party to a contract has refused to perform, or disabled himself from performing, his promise in its entirety, the promisee may put an end to the contract, unless he has signified, by words or conduct, his acquiescence in its continuance.
plain_english_summary: If one party completely breaches or refuses to perform their side of a contract, the innocent party has the right to terminate (put an end to) the contract and sue for damages.

title: Person by whom promise is to be performed
text: If it appears from the nature of the case that it was the intention of the parties to any contract that any promise contained in it should be performed by the promisor himself, such promise must be performed by the promisor. In other cases, the promisor or his representatives may employ competent persons to perform it.
plain_english_summary: If a contract relies on personal skills or art (e.g., hiring a specific artist to paint a portrait), the person must perform it themselves. For general business contracts, the party or their legal representatives can hire competent agents or employees to fulfill the duty.

title: Effect of accepting performance from third person
text: When a promisee accepts performance of the promise from a third person, he cannot afterwards enforce it against the promisor.
plain_english_summary: If someone owes you a performance or payment, and a third party steps in and fulfills it for them, and you accept it, you cannot later turn around and sue the original person for it.

title: Devolution of joint liabilities
text: When two or more persons have made a joint promise, then, unless a contrary intention appears by the contract, all such persons, during their joint lives, and after the death of any of them, his representative jointly with the survivor or survivors, and after the death of the last survivor, the representatives of all jointly, must fulfill the promise.
plain_english_summary: When multiple people make a joint promise to fulfill a contract, they are jointly liable while alive. If one dies, their legal representative steps in alongside the surviving partners to fulfill the obligation.

title: Any one of joint promisors may be compelled to perform
text: When two or more persons make a joint promise, the promisee may, in the absence of express agreement to the contrary, compel any one or more of such joint promisors to perform the whole of the promise.

sub_structure.recovery: Each of two or more joint promisors may compel every other joint promisor to contribute equally with himself to the performance of the promise...
sub_structure.release: If any one of two or more joint promisors is released from such liability... such release does not discharge any other joint promisor...

plain_english_summary: If people make a joint promise, the person owed can choose to force *any single one* of them to perform the entire contract. However, the partner forced to pay can legally sue the other co-promisors to get them to pay their fair share.

title: Effect of release of one joint promisor
text: Where two or more persons have made a joint promise, a release of one of such joint promisors by the promisee does not discharge the other joint promisor or promisors; neither does it free the joint promisor so released from responsibility to the other joint promisor or promisors.
plain_english_summary: If you release one person from a joint contract, it does not automatically let the other joint participants off the hook; they remain responsible for the remaining obligations.

title: Devolution of joint rights
text: When a person has made a promise to two or more persons jointly, then, unless a contrary intention appears from the contract, the right to claim performance rests, during their joint lives, with them, and, after the death of any of them, with the representative of such deceased person jointly with the survivor or survivors, and, after the death of the last survivor, with the representatives of all jointly.
plain_english_summary: When a promise is made to multiple people jointly, all of them together have the right to demand performance. If one dies, their legal heirs step in alongside the survivors to claim performance.

title: Time for performance of promise, where no application is to be made and no time is specified
text: Where, by a contract, a promisor is to perform his promise without application by the promisee, and no time for performance is specified, the engagement must be performed within a reasonable time.
plain_english_summary: If a contract doesn't explicitly state a deadline for when a task must be done, the law implies it must be completed within a 'reasonable time' depending on the nature of the business.

title: Time and place for performance of promise where time is specified and no application to be made
text: When a promise is to be performed on a certain day, and the promisor has undertaken to perform it without application by the promisee, the promisor may perform it at any time during the usual business hours on such day, at the place at which the promise ought to be performed.
plain_english_summary: If a contract specifies a date for performance, the task must be carried out during normal business hours on that exact day at the designated location.

title: Application for performance on certain day to be at proper time and place
text: When a promise is to be performed on a certain day, and the promisor has not undertaken to perform it without application by the promisee, it is the duty of the promisee to apply for performance at a proper place and within the usual business hours.
plain_english_summary: If performance requires the other party to request it first, that request must be made at a proper location and during normal business hours.

title: Place for performance of promise, where no application to be made and no place fixed for performance
text: When a promise is to be performed without application by the promisee, and no place is fixed for the performance of it, it is the duty of the promisor to apply to the promisee to appoint a reasonable place for the performance of the promise, and to perform it at such place.
plain_english_summary: If a contract doesn't state *where* a task must be performed, the person doing the work must ask the other party to designate a reasonable location.

title: Performance in manner or at time prescribed or sanctioned by promisee
text: The performance of any promise may be made in any manner, or at any time which the promisee prescribes or sanctions.
plain_english_summary: A contract can be performed in any manner or timeline explicitly prescribed, requested, or approved by the party receiving the performance.

title: Promisor not bound to perform, unless reciprocal promisee ready and willing to perform
text: When a contract consists of reciprocal promises to be simultaneously performed, no promisor need perform his promise unless the promisee is ready and willing to perform his reciprocal promise.
plain_english_summary: In a simultaneous exchange contract (like a cash-and-carry sale), you aren't legally required to deliver your side of the bargain unless the other party is ready and willing to deliver theirs at the same time.

title: Order of performance of reciprocal promises
text: Where the order in which reciprocal promises are to be performed is expressly fixed by contract, they shall be performed in that order; and where the order is not expressly fixed, they shall be performed in that order which the nature of the transaction requires.
plain_english_summary: If a contract specifies the sequence of steps, they must be done in that exact order. If no order is specified, they must be performed in the sequence required by the nature of the business transaction.

title: Liability of party preventing event on which the contract is to take effect
text: When a contract contains reciprocal promises, and one party to the contract prevents the other from performing his promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party so prevented; and he is entitled to compensation from the other party for any loss which he may sustain in consequence of the non-performance.
plain_english_summary: If Party A blocks or prevents Party B from fulfilling their side of a contract, Party B has the right to cancel the contract and sue Party A for any financial losses suffered.

title: Effect of default as to that promise which should be first performed, in contract consisting of reciprocal promises
text: When a contract consists of reciprocal promises, such that one of them cannot be performed, or that its performance cannot be claimed till the other has been performed, and the promisor of the promise last to be performed fails in performance, such promisor cannot claim the performance of the reciprocal promise, and must make compensation... for any loss which the other party may sustain... pleadings.
plain_english_summary: If a contract requires Step A to happen before Step B, and the person responsible for Step A fails to do it, they cannot force the other party to complete Step B and must pay compensation for any resulting losses.

title: Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential
text: When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract.

sub_structure.non_essential: If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure.

plain_english_summary: If 'time is of the essence' in a contract (explicitly stated or implied by urgency), missing a deadline makes the contract voidable, allowing the innocent party to cancel it. If time wasn't critical, the contract stays valid, but the delayed party must pay compensation for any losses.

title: Agreement to do impossible act
text: An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.

sub_structure.compensation: Where one person has promised to do something which he knew, or, with reasonable diligence, might have known, and which the promisee did not know, to be impossible or unlawful, such promisor must make compensation to such promisee for any loss which such promisee sustains...

plain_english_summary: The Doctrine of Frustration: An agreement to do an impossible act is void. If a contract is signed, but unforeseen events later make performance legally or physically impossible (or unlawful), the contract automatically becomes void.

title: Reciprocal promise to do things legal, and also other things illegal
text: Where persons reciprocally promise, firstly, to do certain things which are legal, and, secondly, under specified circumstances, to do certain other things which are illegal, the first set of promises is a contract, but the second set is a void agreement.
plain_english_summary: If a contract contains a mix of legal promises and illegal promises, the legal parts can be enforced as a valid contract, while the illegal parts are severed and treated as void.

title: Alternative promise, one branch being illegal
text: In the case of an alternative promise of which one branch is legal and the other illegal, the legal branch alone can be enforced.
plain_english_summary: If a contract gives an alternative choice between two actions, where one option is legal and the other is illegal, only the legal alternative can be enforced.

title: Application of payment where debt to be discharged is indicated
text: Where a debtor, owing several distinct debts to one person, makes a payment to him, either with express intimation, or under circumstances implying that the payment is to be applied to the discharge of some particular debt, the payment, if accepted, must be applied accordingly.
plain_english_summary: If a debtor owes multiple distinct debts to a creditor and makes a payment explicitly designating it for a specific debt, the creditor must apply the money to that exact debt.

title: Application of payment where debt to be discharged is not indicated
text: Where the debtor has omitted to intimate, and there are no other circumstances indicating to which debt the payment is to be applied, the creditor may apply it at his discretion to any lawful debt actually due and payable to him from the debtor, whether its recovery is or is not barred by the law in the limitation of suits.
plain_english_summary: If a debtor makes a payment without specifying which debt it is for, the creditor has the legal right to apply that money toward any lawful debt owed by that debtor at their own discretion (even debts that are technically time-barred).

title: Application of payment where neither party appropriates
text: Where neither party makes any appropriation, the payment shall be applied in discharge of the debts in order of time, whether they are or are not barred by the law in force for the limitation of suits. If the debts are of equal standing, the payment shall be applied in discharge of each proportionally.
plain_english_summary: If neither the debtor nor the creditor specifies which debt a payment is meant for, the law automatically applies the money to pay off the debts in chronological order (oldest debts first). If debts are of equal standing, it pays them off proportionally.

title: Effect of novation, rescission, and alteration of contract
text: If the parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, the original contract need not be performed.
plain_english_summary: If both parties mutually agree to replace an old contract with a brand new one (novation), cancel it entirely (rescission), or modify its terms (alteration), the original contract is wiped out and does not need to be fulfilled.

title: Promisee may dispense with or remit performance of promise
text: Every promisee may dispense with or remit, whole or in part, the performance of the promise made to him, or may extend the time for such performance, or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit.
plain_english_summary: The person owed a performance can choose to let the other party off the hook entirely, forgive a part of the debt, grant a deadline extension, or accept any alternative form of payment or satisfaction they choose.

title: Consequences of rescission of voidable contract
text: When a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he have received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.
plain_english_summary: If you choose to cancel (rescind) a voidable contract (like a contract signed under fraud or coercion), you are released from your duties, but you must also return any money, property, or benefits you already received under that contract.

title: Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void
text: When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it, to the person from whom he received it.
plain_english_summary: If a contract turns out to be void from the start or becomes void later due to unforeseen impossibility, anyone who received money, goods, or benefits under it must return them or pay financial compensation to the other party.

title: Mode of communicating or revoking rescission of voidable contract
text: The rescission of a voidable contract may be communicated or revoked in the same manner, and subject to the same rules, as apply to the communication or revocation of a proposal.
plain_english_summary: The rules for canceling (rescinding) a voidable contract follow the exact same communication and revocation guidelines as making a standard offer or proposal.

title: Effect of neglect of promisee to afford promisor reasonable facilities for performance
text: If any promisee neglects or refuses to afford the promisor reasonable facilities for the performance of his promise, the promisor is excused by such neglect or refusal as to any non-performance caused thereby.
plain_english_summary: If you fail to provide reasonable cooperation or facilities required for the other party to do their job (e.g., refusing to give them access to the building), you cannot later sue them for failing to perform.

chapter_title: OF CERTAIN RELATIONS RESEMBLING THOSE CREATED BY CONTRACT
title: Claim for necessaries supplied to person incapable of contracting, or on his account
text: If a person, incapable of entering into a contract, or any one whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who has furnished such supplies is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of such incapable person.
plain_english_summary: Quasi-Contract: If someone supplies life's 'necessaries' (food, medical care, shelter) to a person who is legally incapable of contracting (like a minor or a person of unsound mind) or their dependents, the supplier has a legal right to be reimbursed out of that person's personal property.

chapter_title: OF CERTAIN RELATIONS RESEMBLING THOSE CREATED BY CONTRACT
title: Reimbursement of person paying money due by another, in payment of which he is interested
text: A person who is interested in the payment of money which another is bound by law to pay, and who therefore pays it, is entitled to be reimbursed by the other.
plain_english_summary: If you pay off a financial obligation that another person was legally bound to pay because you had a financial stake in it (e.g., paying property taxes to prevent your leased building from being seized), you have a legal right to get reimbursed by that person.

chapter_title: OF CERTAIN RELATIONS RESEMBLING THOSE CREATED BY CONTRACT
title: Obligation of person enjoying benefit of non-gratuitous act
text: Where a person lawfully does anything for another person, or delivers anything to him, not intending to do so gratuitously, and such other person enjoys the benefit thereof, the latter is bound to make compensation to the former in respect of, or to restore, the thing so done or delivered.
plain_english_summary: If you deliver goods or perform a service for someone without intending it as a free gift, and they knowingly accept and enjoy the benefit of it, they are legally obligated to pay you compensation for it.

chapter_title: OF CERTAIN RELATIONS RESEMBLING THOSE CREATED BY CONTRACT
title: Responsibility of finder of goods
text: A person who finds goods belonging to another, and takes them into his custody, is subject to the same responsibility as a bailee.
plain_english_summary: If you find lost property belonging to someone else and take possession of it, you take on the legal duties of a 'bailee'—meaning you must take reasonable care of the goods and make a genuine effort to find the true owner rather than keeping or stealing them.

chapter_title: OF CERTAIN RELATIONS RESEMBLING THOSE CREATED BY CONTRACT
title: Liability of person to whom money is paid, or thing delivered, by mistake or under coercion
text: A person to whom money has been paid, or anything delivered, by mistake or under coercion, must repay or return it.
plain_english_summary: If money or goods are handed to someone by accident (mistake) or under duress (coercion), that person is legally bound to refund or return them.

chapter_title: OF THE CONSEQUENCES OF BREACH OF CONTRACT
title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
text: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach.

sub_structure.remoteness: Such compensation is not to be given for any remote and indirect loss or damage sustained by reason of the breach.

plain_english_summary: The foundational rule for breach of contract damages: The injured party can sue for financial compensation for direct losses that naturally flow from the breach, or losses the parties anticipated when signing. Remote or indirect losses cannot be recovered.

chapter_title: OF THE CONSEQUENCES OF BREACH OF CONTRACT
title: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for
text: When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for.
plain_english_summary: If a contract includes a pre-agreed penalty clause for a breach, Indian courts will not automatically award the full penalty amount. Instead, the court will award 'reasonable compensation' up to that maximum penalty limit, provided actual loss or a genuine pre-estimate of damage is shown.

chapter_title: OF THE CONSEQUENCES OF BREACH OF CONTRACT
title: Party rightfully rescinding contract, entitled to compensation
text: A person who rightfully rescinds a contract is entitled to compensation for any damage which he has sustained through the non-fulfillment of the contract.
plain_english_summary: If you lawfully cancel a contract because the other party breached it, you retain the legal right to sue them for compensation to cover any damages you suffered due to their failure to perform.

title: Sections 76 to 123 repealed
text: [Repealed by the Indian Sale of Goods Act, 1930 (3 of 1930), section 65.]
plain_english_summary: Sections 76 through 123 of the original 1872 Act (which dealt with the sale of goods) were officially repealed and moved to the independent Sale of Goods Act, 1930.

title: Repealed sections 77 to 123
text: [Repealed by the Indian Sale of Goods Act, 1930 (3 of 1930), section 65.]
