title: "Contract of indemnity" defined
text: A contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to him by the conduct of the promisor himself, or by the conduct of any other person, is called a "contract of indemnity".
plain_english_summary: Defines a contract of indemnity: an agreement where one party formally promises to protect or compensate another party for any financial losses caused by the actions of the promisor or any other person.

title: Rights of indemnity-holder when sued
text: The promisee in a contract of indemnity, acting within the scope of his authority, is entitled to recover from the promisor— (1) all damages which he may be compelled to pay in any suit in respect of any matter to which the promise to indemnify applies; (2) all costs which he may be compelled to pay in such suit... (3) all sums which he may have paid under the terms of any compromise of any such suit...
plain_english_summary: Outlines the legal rights of an indemnity holder (the person protected). When sued, they have the right to recover all court damages, legal costs, and settlement amounts paid out, provided they acted prudently or under the indemnifier's authorization.

title: "Contract of guarantee", "surety", "principal debtor" and "creditor"
text: A "contract of guarantee" is a contract to perform the promise, or discharge the liability, of a third person in case of his default. The person who gives the guarantee is called the "surety"; the person in respect of whose default the guarantee is given is called the "principal debtor", and the person to whom the guarantee is given is called the "creditor". A guarantee may be either oral or written.
plain_english_summary: Defines a contract of guarantee (often used in startup debt or bank loans): a three-party arrangement where a 'surety' promises to pay a 'creditor' if the 'principal debtor' defaults. Guarantees can be either written or oral.

title: Consideration for guarantee
text: Anything done, or any promise made, for the benefit of the principal debtor, may be a sufficient consideration to the surety for giving the guarantee.
plain_english_summary: Any benefit given to the principal debtor (such as advancing a loan) serves as valid legal consideration to bind the surety to their guarantee, even if the surety themselves didn't receive direct money.

title: Surety's liability
text: The liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless it is otherwise provided by contract.
plain_english_summary: Unless specified otherwise in the contract, a surety's financial liability matches the principal debtor's liability dollar-for-dollar. The creditor can chase the surety for payment immediately upon default without needing to sue the debtor first.

title: "Continuing guarantee"
text: A guarantee which extends to a series of transactions is called a "continuing guarantee".
plain_english_summary: A continuing guarantee covers a continuous series of ongoing transactions or lines of credit rather than a single, isolated isolated debt transaction.

title: Revocation of continuing guarantee
text: A continuing guarantee may at any time be revoked by the surety as to future transactions by notice to the creditor.
plain_english_summary: A surety can cancel a continuing guarantee at any time for all *future* transactions by giving formal written notice to the creditor. (Note: They remain liable for past transactions that already occurred before the notice).

title: Revocation of continuing guarantee by surety's death
text: The death of the surety operates, in the absence of contract to the pertinent effect, as a revocation of a continuing guarantee, so far as regards future transactions.
plain_english_summary: Unless the contract states otherwise, the death of a surety automatically revokes a continuing guarantee regarding any future transactions or lines of credit extended after their death.

title: Discharge of surety by variance in terms of contract
text: Any variance, made without the surety's consent, in the terms of the contract between the principal debtor and the creditor, discharges the surety as to transactions subsequent to the variance.
plain_english_summary: If a creditor and debtor secretly alter the terms of their underlying contract without the surety's consent, the surety is automatically released from liability for any transactions occurring after that alteration.

title: Discharge of surety by release or discharge of principal debtor
text: The surety is discharged by any contract between the creditor and the principal debtor, by which the principal debtor is released, or by any act or omission of the creditor, the legal consequence of which is the discharge of the principal debtor.
plain_english_summary: If the creditor releases the primary debtor from their debt, or takes an action that legally discharges the debtor, the surety is also completely released and discharged from liability.

title: Discharge of surety when creditor compounds with, gives time to, or agrees not to sue, principal debtor
text: A contract between the creditor and the principal debtor, by which the creditor makes a composition with, or promises to give time to, or not to sue, the principal debtor, discharges the surety, unless the surety assents to such contract.
plain_english_summary: If a creditor cuts a secret side-deal with the debtor to give them more time to pay, or promises not to sue them without consulting the surety, the surety is discharged from their guarantee.

title: Surety not discharged when agreement made with third person to give time to principal debtor
text: Not being the principal debtor, a contract entered into by the creditor with a third person to give time to the principal debtor does not discharge the surety.
plain_english_summary: If the creditor makes an agreement with an *outside third party* (not the principal debtor) to give the debtor extra time to pay, the surety is not discharged.

title: Creditor's forbearance to sue does not discharge surety
text: Mere forbearance on the part of the creditor to sue the principal debtor or to enforce any other remedy against him does not, in the absence of any provision in the guarantee to the contrary, discharge the surety.
plain_english_summary: If a creditor simply delays filing a lawsuit against a defaulting debtor, the surety is not automatically discharged. The creditor's passive delay or forbearance does not free the surety.

title: Release of one co-surety does not discharge others
text: Where there are co-sureties, a release by the creditor of one of them does not discharge the others; neither does it free the surety so released from his responsibility to the other sureties.
plain_english_summary: If there are multiple guarantors (co-sureties) backing a loan, releasing one of them does not let the remaining co-sureties off the hook.

title: Discharge of surety by creditor's act or omission implying negligence
text: If the creditor does any act which is inconsistent with the rights of the surety, or omits to do any act which his duty to the surety requires him to do, and the eventual remedy of the surety himself against the principal debtor is thereby impaired, the surety is discharged.
plain_english_summary: If the creditor acts negligently or does something that destroys or impairs the surety's legal right to recover money from the debtor later, the surety is discharged from their guarantee.

title: Rights of surety on payment or performance
text: Where a guaranteed debt has become due, or default of the principal debtor to perform a guaranteed duty has taken place, the surety, upon payment or performance of all that he is liable for, is invested with all the rights which the creditor had against the principal debtor.
plain_english_summary: Doctrine of Subrogation: The moment the surety steps in and pays off the defaulting debtor's loan, the surety automatically steps into the shoes of the creditor, acquiring all the legal rights the creditor had to recover that money from the debtor.

title: Surety's right to benefit of creditor's securities
text: A surety is entitled to the benefit of every security which the creditor has against the principal debtor at the time when the contract of suretyship is entered into, whether the surety knows of the existence of such security or not...
plain_english_summary: A surety is legally entitled to share in or benefit from any collateral or security the creditor holds against the debtor for that loan, whether the surety knew about that collateral when signing the guarantee or not.

title: Guarantee obtained by misrepresentation invalid
text: Any guarantee which has been obtained by means of misrepresentation made by the creditor, or with his knowledge and assent, concerning a material part of the transaction, is invalid.
plain_english_summary: If a creditor misleads a surety or hides material facts to trick them into guaranteeing a loan, that guarantee is legally invalid and unenforceable.

title: Guarantee obtained by concealment invalid
text: Any guarantee which the creditor has obtained by means of keeping silence as to material circumstances is invalid.
plain_english_summary: If a creditor intentionally stays silent about crucial, material risks when a surety asks to sign a guarantee, that concealment renders the guarantee invalid.

title: Guarantee on contract that creditor shall not act on it until co-surety signs
text: Where a person gives a guarantee upon a contract that the creditor shall not act upon it until another person has joined in it as co-surety, the guarantee is not valid if that other person does not join.
plain_english_summary: If a surety agrees to back a loan on the explicit condition that another co-surety also signs the agreement, but that second person fails to sign, the first person's guarantee is completely invalid.

title: Implied promise to indemnify surety
text: In every contract of guarantee there is an implied promise by the principal debtor to indemnify the surety; and the surety is entitled to recover from the principal debtor whatever sum he has rightfully paid under the guarantee...
plain_english_summary: Even if not written explicitly, the law assumes an implied promise that the principal debtor will indemnify the surety. If the surety is forced to pay off the debtor's default, the surety has the absolute legal right to recover that exact money from the debtor.

title: Co-sureties liable to contribute equally
text: Where two or more persons are co-sureties for the same debt or duty, either jointly or severally, and whether under the same or different contracts, and whether with or without the knowledge of each other, the co-sureties, in the absence of any contract to the contrary, match and contribute equally... to pay each of such debt or any part thereof.
plain_english_summary: If multiple people guarantee the same debt (co-sureties), they must share the burden equally if the debtor defaults, unless their contract specifies a different unequal proportion.

title: Liability to co-sureties bound in different sums
text: Co-sureties who are bound for co-sureties bound in different sums are liable to pay equally as far as the limits of their respective obligations permit.
plain_english_summary: If co-sureties guarantee different maximum limits/sums, they share the loss equally up to the limit of the smallest guarantee, with any remainder split among the higher limits.

title: "Bailment", "bailor" and "bailee" defined
text: A "bailment" is the delivery of goods by one person to another for some purpose, upon a contract that they shall, when the purpose is accomplished, be returned or otherwise disposed of according to the directions of the person delivering them. The person delivering the goods is called the "bailor". The person to whom they are delivered is called the "bailee".
plain_english_summary: Defines bailment: when someone (bailor) hands over goods to another person (bailee) for a specific purpose under an agreement that the goods will be returned or handled as instructed once the purpose is achieved (e.g., leaving a laptop at a repair shop).

title: Delivery to bailee how made
text: The delivery to the bailee may be made by doing anything which has the effect of putting goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorized to hold them on his behalf.
plain_english_summary: Delivery of goods for bailment can happen physically or through any action that transfers control and possession of the goods to the bailee or their authorized agent.

title: Bailor's duty to disclose faults in goods bailed
text: The bailor is bound to disclose to the bailee faults in the goods bailed, of which the bailor is aware, and which materially interfere with the use of them, or expose the bailee to extraordinary risks; and if he does not make such disclosure, he is responsible for damage arising to the bailee directly from such faults.
plain_english_summary: A bailor must warn the bailee about any known dangerous flaws or faults in the goods. If they stay silent and the bailee gets hurt or suffers damage directly because of those hidden flaws, the bailor is financially responsible.

title: Repayment by bailor of necessary expenses
text: Where, by the conditions of the bailment, the goods are to be kept or carried, or to have work done upon them by the bailee for the bailor, the bailor shall repay to the bailee all necessary expenses incurred by him for the purpose of the bailment.
plain_english_summary: The bailor must reimburse the bailee for any necessary or extraordinary expenses the bailee had to incur to safely store, transport, or work on the bailed goods.

title: Care to be taken by bailee
text: In all cases of bailment, the bailee is bound to take as much care of the goods bailed to him as a man of ordinary prudence would, under similar circumstances, take of his own goods of the same bulk, quality and value.
plain_english_summary: A bailee has a legal duty of care: they must look after the bailed goods with the same level of caution and prudence that a sensible, ordinary person would apply to their own personal property of similar value.

title: Bailee when not liable for loss, etc., of thing bailed
text: The bailee, in the absence of any special contract, is not responsible for the loss, destruction or deterioration of the thing bailed, if he has taken the amount of care of it described in section 151.
plain_english_summary: If a bailee exercises the required standard of ordinary care (Section 151), they are not legally liable if the goods are accidentally damaged, destroyed, or stolen, unless a special contract states otherwise.

title: Termination of bailment by bailee's act inconsistent with conditions
text: A contract of bailment is terminable at the option of the bailor if the bailee does any act with regard to the goods bailed, inconsistent with the conditions of the bailment.
plain_english_summary: If a bailee violates the terms of the bailment agreement (e.g., using a rented car for illegal racing when it was rented for commuting), the bailor has the right to immediately terminate the bailment contract.

title: Liability of bailee making unauthorized use of goods bailed
text: If the bailee makes any use of the goods bailed which is not according to the conditions of the bailment, he is liable to make compensation to the bailor for any damage arising to the goods from or during such use of them.
plain_english_summary: If a bailee uses bailed goods in a way that violates the agreement, they are strictly liable to compensate the bailor for any damage that happens to the goods during that unauthorized use, even if it was accidental.

title: Effect of mixture, with bailor's consent, of his goods with bailee's
text: If the bailee, with the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods, the bailor and the bailee shall have an interest, in proportion to their respective shares, in the mixture thus produced.
plain_english_summary: If the bailor gives permission to mix their goods with the bailee's goods (e.g., mixing bulk grain), both parties own a proportional share of the combined mixture.

title: Effect of mixture, without bailor's consent, when the goods can be separated
text: If the bailee, without the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods, and the goods can be separated or divided, the property in the goods remains in the parties respectively; but the bailee is bound to bear the expense of separation or division, and any damage arising from the mixture.
plain_english_summary: If a bailee mixes the bailor's goods with their own without permission, but the goods can easily be sorted out, each party keeps their own goods, but the bailee must pay 100% of the sorting costs and any damage caused.

title: Effect of mixture, without bailor's consent, when the goods cannot be separated
text: If the bailee, without the consent of the bailee, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods, in such a manner that it is impossible to separate the goods bailed from the other goods and deliver them back, the bailor is entitled to be compensated by the bailee for the loss of the goods.
plain_english_summary: If a bailee mixes goods without permission and they cannot possibly be separated (e.g., mixing different chemicals or liquids), the bailee must fully compensate the bailor for the total loss of their goods.

title: Repayment by bailor of necessary expenses
text: Where, by the conditions of the bailment, the goods are to be kept or carried, or to have work done upon them by the bailee for the bailor, the bailor shall repay to the bailee all necessary expenses incurred by him for the purpose of the bailment.
plain_english_summary: Reiterates that the bailor must cover all necessary expenses incurred by the bailee while storing, transporting, or servicing the bailed goods.

title: Restoration of goods lent gratis
text: The lender of a thing for use may at times require its return, even though the loan was specified for a specified time or purpose: Provided that, if on the faith of such loan made for a specified time or purpose the borrower has acted in such a manner that the return of the thing lent before the time specified would cause him loss greater than the benefit actually derived by him from the loan, the lender shall, if he compels such return, indemnify the borrower for the resulting loss.
plain_english_summary: If you lend an item for free (gratis), you can generally demand it back whenever you want. However, if the borrower relied on a promised timeline and would suffer financial loss by returning it early, you must indemnify them for that loss.

title: Return of goods bailed, on expiration of time or accomplishment of purpose
text: It is the duty of the bailee to return, or deliver them according to the bailor's directions, the goods bailed, without demand, as soon as the time for which they were bailed has expired, or the purpose for which they were bailed has been accomplished.
plain_english_summary: Once the loan period expires or the purpose of the bailment is finished, the bailee has a strict duty to return the goods to the bailor as directed, without even needing the bailor to ask for them.

title: Bailee's responsibility when goods are not duly returned
text: If, by the default of the bailee, the goods are not returned, delivered or tendered at the proper time, he is responsible to the bailor for any loss, destruction or deterioration of the goods from that time.
plain_english_summary: If a bailee fails to return goods on time due to their own fault, they become strictly responsible for any subsequent loss, damage, or destruction of those goods, even if caused by an accident.

title: Termination of bailment by gratuitous death
text: A gratuitous bailment is terminated by the death either of the bailor or of the bailee.
plain_english_summary: A free (gratuitous) loan or bailment of goods is automatically terminated upon the death of either the bailor or the bailee.

title: Bailor entitled to increase or profit from goods bailed
text: In the absence of any contract to the contrary, the bailor is entitled to any increase or profit which may have accrued from the goods bailed.
plain_english_summary: Any natural profit, increase, or offspring born from bailed goods (such as a calf born from a bailed cow) belongs to the bailor, unless a contract states otherwise.

title: Bailor's responsibility to bailee
text: The bailor is responsible to the bailee for any loss which the bailee may sustain by reason that the bailor was not entitled to make the bailment, or to receive back the goods, or to give directions respecting them.
plain_english_summary: If a bailor hands over goods they don't actually have the legal right to possess or bail, and the bailee suffers a loss because of it (such as the true owner seizing the goods), the bailor is legally responsible to compensate the bailee.

title: Custody of goods where several joint owners bail them
text: If goods are bailed jointly by several joint owners, the bailee may deliver them back to, or according to the directions of, one joint owner in the absence of any agreement to the contrary.
plain_english_summary: If multiple people jointly own an item and bail it together, the bailee is legally safe returning the item to just *one* of those joint owners, unless they have a prior agreement stating otherwise.

title: Right of third person claiming goods bailed
text: If a person other than the bailor claims goods bailed, he may apply to the Court to stop the delivery of the goods to the bailor, and to decide the title to the goods.
plain_english_summary: If an outside third party claims ownership of goods currently held in bailment, they can apply to a court to block the bailee from returning the goods to the bailor until ownership is legally determined.

title: Right of finder of goods; may sue for specific reward offered
text: The finder of goods has no right to sue the owner for compensation for trouble and expense voluntarily incurred by him to find the owner and preserve the goods found; but he may retain the goods against the owner until he receives such compensation; and, where the owner has offered a specific reward for the return of goods found, the finder may sue for such reward, and may retain the goods until he receives it.
plain_english_summary: A person who finds lost goods cannot sue the owner for reimbursement of voluntary expenses, but they have the right to hold onto the goods (lien) until they are paid. If the owner publicly offered a reward, the finder can sue to collect it.

title: When finder of thing commonly on sale may sell it
text: When a thing which is commonly the subject of sale is lost, if the owner cannot with reasonable diligence be found, or if he refuses, upon demand, to pay the lawful charges of the finder, the finder may sell it... when the thing is in danger of perishing or of losing the greater part of its value, or when the lawful charges of the finder... amount to two-thirds of its value.
plain_english_summary: If someone finds lost goods that are perishable or losing value fast, and the owner cannot be tracked down or refuses to pay storage costs, the finder has the legal right to sell the items.

title: Bailee's particular lien
text: Where the bailee has, in accordance with the purpose of the bailment, rendered any service involving the exercise of labour or skill in respect of the goods bailed, he has, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, a right to retain such goods until he receives due remuneration for the services he has rendered in respect of them.
plain_english_summary: Bailee's Particular Lien: If a bailee applies skill or labor to improve or repair bailed goods (like a watchmaker repairing a watch), they have the legal right to keep holding the item until the owner pays them for their services.

title: General lien of bankers, factors, wharfingers, attorneys and policy-brokers
text: Bankers, factors, wharfingers, attorneys of a High Court and policy-brokers may, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, retain, as a security for a general balance of account, any goods bailed to them; but no other persons have a right to retain, as a security for such balance, goods bailed to them, unless there is an express contract to the effect.
plain_english_summary: General Lien: Specific professionals like bankers, stockbrokers, attorneys, and wharfingers have a 'general lien', meaning they can hold onto *any* of your goods or money in their possession to cover any general unpaid balance or past debt you owe them.

title: "Pledge", "pawnor" and "pawnee" defined
text: The bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise is called "pledge". The bailor is in this case called the "pawnor". The bailee is called the "pawnee".
plain_english_summary: Defines a pledge (pawn): a special type of bailment where goods are handed over as security collateral for a loan or debt performance. The person giving the goods is the 'pawnor', and the lender holding them is the 'pawnee'.

title: Pawnee's right of retainer
text: The pawnee may retain the goods pledged, not only for payment of the debt or the performance of the promise, for the interest of the debt, and all necessary expenses incurred by him in respect of the possession or for the preservation of the goods pledged.
plain_english_summary: A pawnee (lender) has the right to hold onto the pledged goods until the full debt is repaid, alongside interest and any expenses they incurred while storing or protecting the goods.

title: Pawnee not to retain for debt or promise other than that for which goods pledged. Presumption in case of subsequent advances
text: The pawnee shall not, in the absence of a contract to that effect, retain the goods pledged for any debt or promise other than the debt or promise for which they are pledged; but such contract, in the absence of anything to the contrary, shall be presumed in regard to subsequent advances made by the pawnee.
plain_english_summary: A lender cannot hold onto pledged goods for a *different* old debt unless a contract specifically allows it. However, if the lender gives subsequent loans later down the line, the law presumes the collateral applies to those as well.

title: Pawnee's right as to extraordinary expenses incurred
text: The pawnee is entitled to receive from the pawnor extraordinary expenses incurred by him for the preservation of the goods pledged.
plain_english_summary: The borrower (pawnor) must reimburse the lender (pawnee) for any extraordinary expenses the lender had to pay to keep the pledged goods safe and preserved.

title: Pawnee's right where pawnor makes default
text: If the pawnor makes default in payment of the debt, or performance, at the stipulated time, the pawnee may bring a suit against the pawnor upon the debt or promise, and retain the goods pledged as a collateral security; or he may sell the thing pledged, on giving the pawnor reasonable notice of the sale.
plain_english_summary: If a borrower defaults on a loan, the lender has two options: sue the borrower for the money while holding the collateral, OR sell the pledged goods after giving the borrower reasonable advance notice of the sale.

title: Defaulting pawnor's right to redeem
text: If a time is stipulated for the payment of the debt, and the pawnor makes default in payment of the debt at the stipulated time, he may redeem the goods pledged at any subsequent time before the actual sale of them; but he must, in that case, pay, in addition, any expenses which have arisen from his default.
plain_english_summary: Even if a borrower defaults, they have the right to redeem (buy back) their pledged goods at any time *before* the lender actually sells them, as long as they pay off the debt plus any extra expenses caused by the delay.

title: Pledge by mercantile agent
text: Where a mercantile agent is, with the consent of the owner, in possession of goods or the documents of title to goods, any pledge made by him, when acting in the ordinary course of business of a mercantile agent, shall be as valid as if he were expressly authorized by the owner of the goods to make it...
plain_english_summary: If a commercial agent is holding goods with the owner's permission, any pledge of those goods made by the agent during normal business operations is legally valid and binding on the owner.

title: Pledge by person in possession under voidable contract
text: When the pawnor has obtained possession of the goods pledged by him under a contract voidable under section 19 or section 19A, but the contract has not been rescinded at the time of the pledge, the pawnee acquires a good title to the goods, provided he acts in good faith and without notice of the pawnor's defect of title.
plain_english_summary: If someone obtains goods via a voidable contract (like fraud) and pledges them to a lender *before* the original owner cancels that contract, the lender gets valid legal title to the goods, provided they acted in good faith.

title: Pledge where pawnor has only a limited interest
text: Where a person pledges goods in which he has only a limited interest, the pledge is valid to the extent of that interest.
plain_english_summary: If a person only owns a partial or limited legal interest in an item (such as being a part-owner or having a lien), they can still pledge it, but the pledge is only legally valid up to the value of their limited interest.

title: Suit by bailor or bailee against wrong-doers
text: If a third person wrongfully deprives the bailee of the use or possession of goods bailed, or does them any injury, the bailee is entitled to use such remedies as the owner might have used in the like case if no bailment had been made, and either the bailor or the bailee may bring a suit against a third person for such injury.
plain_english_summary: If a third party damages or steals bailed goods from a bailee, both the bailor and the bailee have the independent right to file a lawsuit against that wrongdoer for damages.

title: Apportionment of relief or compensation obtained by such suits
text: Whatever is obtained by way of relief or compensation in any such suit shall, as between the bailor and the bailee, be dealt with according to their respective interests.
plain_english_summary: Any financial compensation or damages recovered from a lawsuit against a wrongdoer must be split and shared between the bailor and bailee based on their respective ownership interests.

title: "Agent" and "principal" defined
text: An "agent" is a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in dealings with third persons. The person for whom such act is done, or who is so represented, is called the "principal".
plain_english_summary: Defines agency: an 'agent' is someone hired to act on behalf of someone else or represent them in business deals with third parties. The person being represented is the 'principal'.

title: Who may employ agent
text: Any person who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, may employ an agent.
plain_english_summary: Anyone who is a competent adult of sound mind has the legal right to hire and appoint an agent to act on their behalf.

title: Who may be an agent
text: As between the principal and third persons, any person may become an agent, but no person who is not of the age of majority and of sound mind can become an agent, so as to be responsible to his principal according to the provisions in that behalf herein contained.
plain_english_summary: In dealings with third parties, anyone can act as an agent (even a minor). However, to be legally responsible and accountable to your principal as an agent, you must be of the age of majority and of sound mind.

title: Consideration not necessary
text: No consideration is necessary to create an agency.
plain_english_summary: Unlike regular contracts which require financial value (consideration) to be valid, a legal agency relationship can be created purely gratuitously without any payment or consideration.

title: Agent's authority may be expressed or implied
text: The authority of an agent may be expressed or implied.
plain_english_summary: An agent's power to act for a principal can be explicitly stated in writing or spoken words (expressed), or it can be inferred from the circumstances, conduct, or course of dealing (implied).

title: Definitions of express and implied authority
text: An authority is said to be express when it is given by words spoken or written. An authority is said to be implied when it is to be inferred from the circumstances of the case; and things spoken or written, or the ordinary course of dealing, may be accounted circumstances of the case.
plain_english_summary: Defines express authority (explicitly written or spoken instructions) and implied authority (powers deduced logically from the situation, ordinary business practices, or conduct).

title: Extent of agent's authority
text: An agent, having an authority to do an act, has authority to do every lawful thing which is necessary in order to do such act. An agent having an authority to carry on a business has authority to do every lawful thing necessary for the purpose, or usually done in the course, of conducting such business.
plain_english_summary: An agent authorized to complete a task automatically has the legal power to perform any lawful, necessary steps required to finish it, including anything customary in that specific type of business.

title: Agent's authority in an emergency
text: An agent has authority, in an emergency, to do all such acts for the purpose of protecting his principal from loss as would be done by a person of ordinary prudence, in his own case, under similar circumstances.
plain_english_summary: Agency of Necessity: In an emergency, an agent has the expanded legal power to take whatever reasonable, prudent steps are necessary to protect their principal from financial loss, even if it goes beyond their usual written instructions.

title: When agent cannot delegate
text: An agent cannot lawfully employ another to perform acts which he has expressly or impliedly undertaken to perform personally, unless by the ordinary custom of trade a sub-agent may, from the nature of the agency, be employed.
plain_english_summary: Delegatus non potest delegare: An agent cannot delegate their core duties to a sub-agent if they were hired to perform those tasks personally, unless trade custom explicitly allows it.

title: "Sub-agent" defined
text: A "sub-agent" is a person employed by, and acting under the control of, the original agent in the business of the agency.
plain_english_summary: Defines a sub-agent: someone hired by the primary agent to assist in handling the principal's business, operating under the primary agent's direct control.

title: Representation of principal by sub-agent properly appointed
text: Where a sub-agent is properly appointed, the principal is, so far as regards third persons, represented by the sub-agent, and is bound by and responsible for his acts, as if he were an agent originally appointed by the principal.

sub_structure.agent_responsibility: The agent is responsible to the principal for the acts of the sub-agent.

plain_english_summary: If a sub-agent is lawfully appointed, they represent the principal to third parties just like a normal agent. The primary agent remains fully responsible to the principal for the sub-agent's actions.

title: Agent's responsibility for sub-agent appointed without authority
text: Where an agent is not authorized to employ a sub-agent has appointed a sub-agent, the agent is responsible for the acts of the sub-agent to both the principal and to third persons.
plain_english_summary: If an agent hires a sub-agent without proper authorization, the primary agent takes 100% personal responsibility for the sub-agent's mistakes or frauds, answering to both the principal and third parties.

title: Relation between principal and person duly appointed by agent to act in business of agency
text: Where an agent, holding an express or implied authority to name another person to act for the principal in the business of the agency, has named another person accordingly, such person is not a sub-agent, but an agent of the principal for such part of the business of the agency as is entrusted to him.
plain_english_summary: If an agent has authority to name a substitute, and names someone else, that person is not a sub-agent; they become a direct, independent agent of the principal for that specific task.

title: Agent's duty in naming such person
text: In selecting such person for the principal, an agent is bound to exercise the same amount of discretion as a man of ordinary prudence would exercise in his own case; and, if he does so, he is not responsible to the principal for the acts or negligence of the person so selected.
plain_english_summary: When an agent picks a substitute or replacement agent for the principal, they must exercise ordinary care and prudence in choosing them. If they do, the original agent is not liable for any future mistakes made by that substitute.

title: Right of person as to acts done for him without his authority. Ratification
text: Where acts are done by one person on behalf of another, but without his knowledge or authority, he may elect to ratify or to disown such acts. If he ratify them, the same effects will follow as if they had been performed by his authority.
plain_english_summary: If someone acts on your behalf without your permission, you can choose to accept (ratify) or reject their actions. If you ratify them, it has the exact same legal effect as if you had authorized them from the very beginning.

title: Ratification may be expressed or implied
text: Ratification may be expressed or implied in conduct.
plain_english_summary: Approval of an unauthorized act (ratification) doesn't have to be in writing; it can be expressed explicitly through words or implied implicitly through the principal's behavior and conduct.

title: Knowledge requisite for valid ratification
text: Valid ratification can be made only by a person whose knowledge of the facts of the case is material.
plain_english_summary: For a ratification to be legally binding, the principal must have full knowledge of all the material facts and circumstances surrounding the transaction at the time they approve it.

title: Effect of ratifying unauthorized act forming part of a transaction
text: A person ratifying any unauthorized act done on his behalf ratifies the whole of the transaction in which such act was done.
plain_english_summary: You cannot cherry-pick parts of an unauthorized deal. If you ratify an unauthorized act, you automatically ratify the entire transaction and all associated terms.

title: Ratification of unauthorized act cannot injure third person
text: An act done by one person on behalf of another, without his authority, which, if done with authority, would have had the effect of subjecting a third person to damages, or of terminating any right or interest of a third person, cannot, by ratification, be made to have such effect.
plain_english_summary: You cannot use retroactive ratification to harm a third party or strip away third-party rights that were established before the ratification took place.

title: Termination of agency
text: An agency is terminated by the principal revoking his authority; or by the agent renouncing the business of the agency; or by the business of the agency being completed; or by either the principal or agent dying or becoming of unsound mind; or by the principal being adjudicated an insolvent under the provisions of any Act for the time being in force for the relief of insolvent debtors.
plain_english_summary: Lists the standard ways an agency relationship ends: when the principal revokes it, the agent resigns, the task is completed, either party dies or becomes of unsound mind, or the principal goes bankrupt (insolvent).

title: Termination of agency where agent has an interest in subject-matter
text: Where the agent has himself an interest in the property which forms the subject-matter of the agency, the agency cannot, in the absence of an express contract, be terminated to the prejudice of such interest.
plain_english_summary: Agency Coupled with an Interest: If an agent holds a personal financial stake or interest in the property they are managing for the principal, the principal cannot unilaterally terminate the agency to harm that interest.

title: When principal may revoke agent's authority
text: The principal may, save as otherwise provided by section 202, revoke the authority given to his agent at any time before the authority has been exercised so as to bind the principal.
plain_english_summary: Except when the agent has a financial interest in the project (Section 202), a principal has the right to revoke an agent's authority at any time before the agent binds the principal in a deal.

title: Revocation where authority has been partly exercised
text: The principal cannot revoke the authority given to his agent after the authority has been exercised so far as regards such acts and obligations as arise from acts already done in the agency.
plain_english_summary: A principal cannot revoke an agent's authority regarding actions and obligations that have already been executed or partly exercised. Once an agent binds the principal in a transaction, that past act cannot be undone by a late revocation.

title: Compensation for revocation by principal, or renunciation by agent
text: Where there is an express or implied contract that the agency should continue for any period of time, the principal must make compensation to the agent, or the agent to the principal, for any revocation or renunciation of the agency without sufficient cause, vorher the period of time specified.
plain_english_summary: If an agency agreement was contracted to last for a specific timeframe, and either party breaks it and cancels early without a valid legal cause, they must pay financial compensation to the other party for the premature termination.

title: Notice of revocation or renunciation
text: Reasonable notice must be given of such revocation or renunciation; otherwise the damage thereby resulting to the principal or the agent, as the case may be, must be made good to the one by the other.
plain_english_summary: Canceling or resigning from an agency requires giving reasonable advance notice. If proper notice is not given and damages result, the party responsible for the sudden termination must pay for the resulting losses.

title: Revocation and renunciation may be expressed or implied
text: Revocation and renunciation may be expressed or implied in conduct.
plain_english_summary: The cancellation of an agency by a principal or resignation by an agent doesn't have to be formal; it can be communicated explicitly through words or implied implicitly through their behavior and conduct.

title: When termination of agent's authority takes effect as to agent, and as to third persons
text: The termination of the authority of an agent does not, so far as regards the agent, before it becomes known to him, and, so far as regards third persons, before it becomes known to them, take effect.
plain_english_summary: An agent's termination doesn't officially take effect for them until they are notified of it, and it doesn't take effect for third-party partners until they receive notice, protecting people who deal with the agent in good faith.

title: Agent's duty on termination of agency by principal's death or insanity
text: When an agency is terminated by the principal dying or becoming of unsound mind, the agent is bound to take, on behalf of the representatives of his late principal, all reasonable steps for the protection and preservation of the interests entrusted to him.
plain_english_summary: If an agency ends because the principal dies or goes insane, the agent has a legal duty to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the principal's assets on behalf of their legal heirs or representatives.

title: Termination of sub-agent's authority
text: The termination of an authority of an agent causes the termination (subject to the rules herein contained regarding the termination of an agent's authority) of the authority of all sub-agents appointed by him.
plain_english_summary: When a primary agent's authority is terminated, it automatically triggers the termination of all sub-agents appointed under them.

title: Agent's duty in conducting principal's business
text: An agent is bound to conduct the business of his principal according to the directions given by the principal, or, in the absence of any such directions, according to the custom which prevails in doing business of the same kind at the place where the agent conducts such business... When any loss is sustained, the agent must make it good to his principal, and if any profit accrues, he must account for it.
plain_english_summary: An agent must conduct business strictly following the principal's instructions or local business customs. If they deviate and cause a loss, they must compensate the principal; if they make an extra profit, they must hand it over.

title: Skill and diligence required from agent
text: An agent is bound to conduct the business of the agency with as much skill as is generally possessed for persons engaged in similar business... and he is always bound to act with reasonable diligence, and to use such skill as he possesses... and he is responsible to his principal in respect of the direct consequence of his neglect, want of skill or misconduct...
plain_english_summary: An agent must exercise reasonable skill and professional diligence. They are personally responsible to compensate the principal for any direct financial losses caused by their professional negligence, lack of skill, or misconduct.

title: Agent's accounts
text: An agent is bound to render proper accounts to his principal on demand.
plain_english_summary: An agent has a strict legal obligation to maintain accurate financial records and present proper accounts to their principal whenever requested.

title: Agent's duty to communicate with principal
text: It is the duty of an agent, in cases of difficulty, to use all reasonable diligence in communicating with his principal, in order to seek his instructions.
plain_english_summary: If an agent runs into unexpected difficulties or complications while handling business, they must make a diligent effort to contact the principal and ask for instructions before taking independent actions.

title: Right of principal when agent deals, on his own account, in business of agency without principal's consent
text: If an agent deals on his own account in the business of the agency, without first obtaining the consent of his principal and acquainting him with all material circumstances which have come to his own knowledge on the subject, the principal may repudiate the transaction...
plain_english_summary: If an agent secretly buys from or sells to the principal on their own account without full disclosure and consent, the principal has the legal right to cancel (repudiate) the deal and claim any secret profits made by the agent.

title: Principal's right to benefit gained by agent dealing on his own account in business of agency
text: If an agent, without the knowledge of his principal, deals in the business of the agency on his own account, the principal is entitled to claim from the agent any benefit which may have resulted to him from the transaction.
plain_english_summary: If an agent engages in business on their own account behind the principal's back, the principal is legally entitled to seize and claim all profits or financial benefits the agent made from that transaction.

title: Agent's right of retention out of sums received on principal's account
text: An agent may retain, out of any sums received on account of the principal in the business of the agency, all moneys due to himself in respect of advances made or expenses properly incurred by him in conducting such business, and also such remuneration as may be payable to him for acting as agent.
plain_english_summary: An agent has the right to deduct and retain their owed commissions, proper business expenses, and cash advances out of any money they collect on behalf of the principal before handing over the balance.

title: Agent's duty to pay sums received for principal
text: Subject to such deductions, the agent is bound to pay to his principal all sums received on his account.
plain_english_summary: After deducting authorized commissions and expenses, an agent is strictly bound to hand over and account for all remaining money collected on behalf of the principal.

title: When agent's remuneration becomes due
text: In the absence of any special contract to the contrary, an agent's remuneration does not become due until the completion of the stated act; but an agent may retain moneys received by a account of goods still unsold, in respect of advances made or expenses properly incurred.
plain_english_summary: Unless agreed otherwise, an agent's commission or pay does not officially become due until they fully complete the specific task they were hired to perform.

title: Agent not entitled to remuneration for business misconducted
text: An agent who is guilty of misconduct in the business of the agency is not entitled to any remuneration in respect of that part of the business which he has misconducted.
plain_english_summary: If an agent commits fraud, gross negligence, or misconduct while handling a task, they entirely forfeit their right to claim any commission or pay for that specific portion of work.

title: Agent's lien on principal's property
text: In the absence of any contract to the contrary, an agent is entitled to retain goods, papers and other property, whether movable or immovable, of the principal received by him, until the amount due to himself for commission, disbursements and services in respect of the same has been paid or accounted for to him.
plain_english_summary: Agent's Lien: An agent has the legal right to hold onto the principal's goods, documents, or property until they are fully paid their due commissions, expenses, and service fees.

title: Agent to be indemnified against consequences of lawful acts
text: The employer of a duly appointed agent is bound to indemnify him against the consequences of all lawful acts done by such agent in exercise of the authority conferred upon him.
plain_english_summary: The principal is legally obligated to protect and indemnify the agent against any financial losses or liabilities resulting from lawful acts performed while following the principal's instructions.

title: Agent to be indemnified against consequences of acts done in good faith
text: Where one person employs another to do an act, and the agent does the act in good faith, the employer is liable to indemnification to the agent for any loss or damage which he may sustain from it, notwithstanding the fact that the act causes an injury to the rights of third persons.
plain_english_summary: If an agent carries out an instruction in good faith, believing it to be lawful, the principal must indemnify them for any damages or losses sustained, even if that act inadvertently violates the rights of a third party.

title: Non-liability of employer of agent to do a criminal act
text: Where one person employs another to do an act which is criminal, the employer is not liable to the agent, either upon an express or an implied promise, to indemnify him against the consequences of that act.
plain_english_summary: If a principal hires an agent to commit a criminal offense, the principal is not legally obligated to indemnify or protect the agent from the criminal consequences, even if they promised to do so.

title: Compensation to agent for injury caused by principal's neglect
text: The principal must make compensation to his agent in respect of injury caused to such agent by the principal's neglect or want of skill.
plain_english_summary: A principal must pay financial compensation to an agent if the agent suffers physical or financial injury due to the principal's own negligence, lack of skill, or unsafe directions.

title: Enforcement and consequences of agent's contracts
text: Contracts entered into through an agent, and obligations arising from acts done by an agent, may be enforced in the same manner, and will have the same legal consequences, as if the contracts had been entered into and the acts done by the principal in person.
plain_english_summary: Deals done by an authorized agent legally bind the principal. They carry the exact same legal force and consequences as if the principal had handled the transaction personally.

title: Principal how far bound, when agent exceeds authority
text: When an agent does more than he is authorized to do, and when the part of what he does, which is within his authority, can be separated from the part which is beyond his authority, so much only of what he does as is within his authority is binding as between him and his principal.
plain_english_summary: If an agent oversteps their authority, the principal is only bound by the portion of the actions that fell *within* their authorized limits, provided that authorized part can be cleanly separated from the unauthorized part.

title: Principal not bound when excess of agent's authority is not separable
text: Where an agent does more than he is authorized to do, and what he does beyond the scope of his authority cannot be separated from what is within it, the principal is not bound to recognize the transaction.
plain_english_summary: If an agent exceeds their authority and the authorized and unauthorized parts are hopelessly mixed together and cannot be separated, the principal has the right to reject the entire transaction completely.

title: Consequence of notice given to agent
text: Any notice given to or information obtained by the agent, in the course of the business transacted by him for the principal, shall have the same legal consequence as if it had been given to or obtained by the principal.
plain_english_summary: Notice given to an agent while they are working on company business is legally treated as notice given directly to the principal. The principal is legally assumed to know whatever their agent knows.

title: Agent cannot personally enforce, nor be bound by, contracts on behalf of principal
text: In the absence of any contract to that effect, an agent cannot personally enforce contracts entered into by him on behalf of his principal, nor is he personally bound by them. Such a contract shall be presumed to exist in the following cases:— (1) where the contract is made by an agent for the sale or purchase of goods for a merchant resident abroad; (2) where the agent does not disclose the name of his principal; (3) where the principal, though disclosed, cannot be sued.
plain_english_summary: Normally, an agent cannot personally sue or be sued on contracts they sign on behalf of their principal. However, the agent *is* personally presumed liable if: they buy/sell for an overseas merchant, they hide the principal's identity, or the principal cannot legally be sued.

title: Rights of parties to a contract made by agent not disclosed
text: If an agent makes a contract with a person who neither knows, nor has reason to suspect, that he is an agent, his principal may require the performance of the contract; but the other party to the contract has, as against the principal, the same rights as he would have had as against the agent if the agent had been principal.
plain_english_summary: If an agent signs a deal without revealing they are an agent, the hidden principal can step forward to enforce it. However, the third party can raise any defense or claim against the principal that they could have used against the agent.

title: Performance of contract with agent supposed to be principal
text: Where one man makes a contract with another, neither knowing nor having reasonable ground to suspect that the other is an agent, the principal, if he requires the performance of the contract, can only obtain such performance subject to the rights and obligations subsisting between the agent and the other party to the contract.
plain_english_summary: If a third party deals with someone believing they are the primary owner, but they turn out to be a hidden agent, the principal must take the contract subject to any existing rights, credits, or offsets the third party had with the agent.

title: Right of person dealing with agent personally liable
text: In cases where the agent is personally liable, a person dealing with him may hold either the principal or his agent, or both of them, liable.
plain_english_summary: If an agent is legally subject to personal liability on a deal, the third party has the option to sue either the principal, the agent, or both of them simultaneously.

title: Consequence of inducing agent or principal to act on belief that principal or agent will be held exclusively liable
text: When a person who has made a contract with an agent induces the agent to act upon the belief that the principal only will be held liable, or induces the principal to act upon the belief that the agent only will be held liable, he cannot afterwards hold liable the agent or principal, respectively.
plain_english_summary: If a third party tricks an agent or principal into believing only one of them will be held responsible, and they rely on that belief, the third party cannot later turn around and sue the other party.

title: Liability of pretended agent
text: A person who falsely represents himself to be the authorized agent of another, and thereby induces a third person to deal with him as such agent, is liable, if his alleged employer does not ratify his acts, to make compensation to the other for any loss or damage which he has incurred by so dealing.
plain_english_summary: If someone pretends to be an authorized agent when they are not, and tricks a third party into a deal, that fake agent is personally liable to pay compensation for any losses if the actual principal refuses to ratify the act.

title: Person falsely contracting as agent not entitled to performance
text: A person with whom a contract has been entered into in the character of agent, is not entitled to require the performance of it, if he was in reality acting, not as agent, but on his own account.
plain_english_summary: If someone signs a contract pretending to be an agent for a principal, but they were actually acting secretly on their own behalf, they cannot legally enforce or demand performance of that contract.

title: Liability of principal inducing belief that agent's unauthorized acts were authorized
text: When a principal has, by his conduct, induced a third person to believe that certain unauthorized acts of an agent were authorized, the principal is bound by such acts, even though they were beyond his actual authority.
plain_english_summary: Apparent / Ostensible Authority: If a principal's behavior or words lead a third party to reasonably believe an agent had authority to do something (even if they didn't), the principal is legally bound by those acts.

title: Effect, on agreement, of misrepresentation or fraud, by agent
text: Misrepresentation made, or frauds committed, by agents acting in the course of their business for their principals, have the same effect on agreements made by such agents as if such misrepresentation or frauds had been made or committed by the principals...
plain_english_summary: If an agent commits fraud or misrepresentation while acting within the scope of their employment for a principal, it has the exact same legal effect as if the principal committed the fraud personally, making the contract voidable.

plain_english_summary: Sections 239 through 266 of the original 1872 Act (which dealt with the law of partnership) were officially repealed and replaced by the independent Indian Partnership Act, 1932.

title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
text: (1) This Act may be called the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may... appoint... (4) Save as otherwise expressly provided otherwise, it shall apply to all goods and services.
plain_english_summary: Establishes the name of the Act, confirms it applies across the whole of India to all goods and services, and defines its implementation scope.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,— (7) "consumer" means any person who— (i) buys any goods for a consideration... or (ii) hires or avails of any service... and includes any user of such goods... but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose...

sub_structure.7_explanation: Explanation.—For the purposes of this clause, the expression "buys any goods" and "hires or avails of any services" includes offline or online transactions through electronic means or teleshopping or direct selling or multi-level marketing;
sub_structure.16: (16) "e-commerce" means buying or selling of goods or services including digital products over digital or electronic network;
sub_structure.17: (17) "electronic service provider" means a person who provides technologies or processes to enable a product seller to engage in advertising or selling goods or services to a consumer...;
sub_structure.34: (34) "product liability" means the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product for any harm, caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto;

plain_english_summary: Crucial definitions for modern businesses: explicitly expands the definition of a 'consumer' to cover e-commerce, online marketplaces, teleshopping, and direct selling. It defines 'electronic service provider' (platforms) and introduces strict 'product liability' rules.

title: Central Consumer Protection Council
text: (1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish to be known as the Central Consumer Protection Council.
plain_english_summary: Requires the Central Government to establish an advisory body known as the Central Consumer Protection Council to advise on promoting and protecting consumer rights.

title: Procedure for meetings of Central Council
text: (1) The Central Council shall meet as and when necessary, but at least one meeting of the council shall be held every year. (2) The Central Council shall meet at such time and place as the Chairman may think fit...
plain_english_summary: Mandates that the Central Consumer Protection Council must hold at least one meeting every year at a time and place chosen by its Chairman.

title: Objects of Central Council
text: The objects of the Central Council shall be to render advice on the promotion and protection of the rights of the consumer under this Act, such as— (a) the right to be protected against the marketing of goods, products or services which are hazardous to life and property...
plain_english_summary: Outlines the core mission of the Central Council: advising the government on safeguarding consumer rights, such as protection from hazardous goods, access to accurate product information, and fair pricing.

title: State Consumer Protection Councils
text: (1) Each State Government shall, by notification, establish a State Consumer Protection Council to be known as the State Consumer Protection Council...
plain_english_summary: Mandates every State Government to establish a State Consumer Protection Council to promote and protect consumer interests at the state level.

title: Objects of State Council
text: The objects of every State Council shall be to render advice on the promotion and protection of the rights of the consumer within the State under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Defines the purpose of the State Council as advising state authorities on the enforcement and protection of consumer rights within that specific state.

title: District Consumer Protection Council
text: (1) The State Government shall, by notification, establish for every district, a district consumer protection council to be known as the District Consumer Protection Council.
plain_english_summary: Requires state governments to establish a District Consumer Protection Council for every individual district to promote and protect consumer rights at the grassroots level.

title: Objects of District Council
text: The objects of every District Council shall be to render advice on the promotion and protection of the rights of the consumer under this Act within the district.
plain_english_summary: The objective of the District Council is to advise local authorities on protecting consumer rights and resolving consumer grievances within the district boundaries.

title: Establishment of Central Consumer Protection Authority
text: (1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish a central authority to be known as the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements...
plain_english_summary: Establishes the **Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)**, a powerful new regulatory body tasked with cracking down on consumer rights violations, unfair trade practices, and misleading ads.

title: Qualifications, method of recruitment, etc., of Chief Commissioner and Commissioners
text: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules in relation to the qualifications, method of recruitment, terms of office, salaries and allowances of the Chief Commissioner and Commissioners of the Central Authority.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to set the official qualifications, recruitment methods, and salary guidelines for the Chief Commissioner and Commissioners leading the CCPA.

title: Vacancy, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of Central Authority
text: No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be questioned or shall be invalid on the mere ground of the existence of any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Central Authority.
plain_english_summary: Ensures that if there is an empty seat (vacancy) or a minor procedural defect in the CCPA's makeup, any official decisions or investigations it conducts remain legally valid.

title: Appointment of Officers, Experts, Professionals and Other Employees of Central Authority
text: (1) The Central Government may provide the Central Authority such officers, experts, professionals and other employees as it may think necessary.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Central Government to staff the CCPA with technical experts, legal professionals, and support employees to assist in its regulatory duties.

title: Procedure of Central Authority
text: (1) The Central Authority shall meet at such times and places and shall observe such rules of procedure in regard to the transaction of business at its meetings as may be specified by regulations.
plain_english_summary: Gives the CCPA the power to set its own internal rules, meeting schedules, and procedural guidelines for conducting regulatory business.

title: Investigation Wing
text: (1) The Central Authority shall have an Investigation Wing, headed by a Director-General, for the purpose of conducting inquiry or investigation under this Act as the Central Authority may direct.
plain_english_summary: Establishes a dedicated Investigation Wing within the CCPA, headed by a Director-General, to launch inquiries and investigate consumer rights violations and misleading ads.

title: Power of District Collector
text: (1) The District Collector may, on a complaint or a reference made to him by the Central Authority or the Commissioner, inquire into or investigate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers or unfair trade practices...
plain_english_summary: Empowers local District Collectors to conduct inquiries and local investigations into consumer rights violations or unfair trade practices when directed by the CCPA.

title: Complaints to Authorities
text: A complaint relating to violation of consumer rights or unfair trade practices or false or misleading advertisements may be forwarded in writing or through electronic mode to the District Collector or to the Commissioner or to the Central Authority.
plain_english_summary: Allows consumers to file complaints regarding unfair trade practices or misleading ads either physically in writing or electronically to local authorities, regional commissioners, or the CCPA.

title: Powers and Functions of Central Authority
text: (1) The Central Authority shall protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class, and prevent violation of consumers' rights under this Act... (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions... the Central Authority may— (a) inquire or investigate into violations... (b) file complaints before the District, State or National Commission...
plain_english_summary: Outlines the sweeping powers and functions of the CCPA: to protect consumer rights as a class, launch investigations, recall hazardous goods, order refunds, and file formal complaints before Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions.

title: Power of Central Authority to refer matter for investigation or to other Regulator
text: The Central Authority may, compound or refer any matter under investigation to any other regulator or statutory authority if it considers that the matter falls within their jurisdiction.
plain_english_summary: Allows the CCPA to transfer or refer a matter under investigation to another specialized regulator (such as FSSAI or RBI) if the issue falls under their specific legal jurisdiction.

title: Power of Central Authority to issue directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements
text: (1) Where the Central Authority is satisfied after investigation that any advertisement is false or misleading and is prejudicial to the interest of any consumer or is in contravention of consumer rights, it may, by order, issue directions to the manufacturer or the endorser or the publisher or the advertiser to discontinue such advertisement or to modify the same...

sub_structure.2: (2) The Central Authority may impose a penalty which may extend to ten lakh rupees on a manufacturer or an endorser for a false or misleading advertisement...
sub_structure.3: (3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (2), the Central Authority may... prohibit the endorser of a false or misleading advertisement from making any endorsement of any product or service for a period which may extend to one year...

plain_english_summary: Empowers the CCPA to ban or modify misleading ads. It can levy fines up to ₹10 Lakhs on manufacturers and celebrity endorsers for false ads, and ban celebrity endorsers from endorsing any product or service for up to 1 year (and up to 3 years for repeat offenses).

title: Search and seizure
text: (1) The Director-General or any other officer authorised in this behalf by the Central Authority... shall have power to- (a) enter and search any place... (b) seize any document or record...
plain_english_summary: Grants the CCPA's Investigation Wing the power to conduct search and seizure operations, enter premises, and confiscate documents or fake products relevant to an investigation.

title: Application of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to searches and seizures
text: The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 relating to searches and seizures shall, so far as may be, apply to every search and seizure made under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Requires the CCPA's search and seizure operations to follow standard criminal procedure rules to protect legal rights and due process.

title: Appeals against orders of Central Authority
text: (1) Any person aggrieved by any order relating to a false or misleading advertisement made by the Central Authority... may prefer an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order.
plain_english_summary: If a company or endorser is penalized or ordered by the CCPA regarding a misleading ad, they have 30 days to file an official appeal with the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

title: Establishment of Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
text: (1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission to be known as the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission...
plain_english_summary: Mandates the government to establish District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions across districts to handle consumer complaints.

title: Qualifications, etc., of President and members of District Commission
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification, make rules to provide for the qualifications, method of recruitment, term of office, resignation and removal of the President and members of the District Commission.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to set qualification requirements, recruitment standards, and terms of office for the Presidents and members of District Consumer Commissions.

title: Salaries, allowances and other terms and conditions of service of President and members of District Commission
text: The salaries and allowances payable to, and the other terms and conditions of service of, the President and members of the District Commission shall be such as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Sets the rule that salary, allowances, and working conditions for District Commission members are prescribed by the Central Government.

title: Vacancy, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of District Commission
text: No act or proceeding of the District Commission shall be called in question on the ground merely of the existence of any vacancy in or any defect in the constitution of the District Commission.
plain_english_summary: Protects District Commission rulings from being overturned solely because there was an empty seat or a minor procedural error in its composition.

title: Officers and other employees of District Commission
text: (1) The State Government shall provide the District Commission with such officers and other employees as may be necessary...
plain_english_summary: Requires State Governments to provide necessary administrative staff and officers to support the functioning of District Commissions.

title: Jurisdiction of District Commission
text: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees: Provided that the Central Government may prescribe such pecuniary jurisdiction from time to time.
plain_english_summary: Sets the pecuniary jurisdiction limit for District Commissions: they can handle consumer complaints where the value of goods or services paid does not exceed ₹50 Lakhs. (Note: Central rules later revised these thresholds upward across tiers).

title: Manner in which complaint shall be made
text: (1) A complaint relating to any product or goods or services may be made in writing or through electronic mode, by— (a) any consumer... (b) any recognized consumer association... (c) the Central Government or the State Government...
plain_english_summary: Allows consumers, consumer associations, or governments to file a complaint either in writing or electronically before a Consumer Commission.

title: Review by District Commission in certain cases
text: The District Commission shall have power to review any of the order passed by it if there is an error apparent on the face of the record, either of its own motion or on an application made by any of the parties within thirty days of such order.
plain_english_summary: Gives District Commissions the power to review and correct their own past orders within 30 days if there is an obvious, glaring error on the face of the record.

title: Manner of filling up vacancies
text: If the office of the President of the District Commission gets vacant or if he is unable to perform his functions... such vacancy shall be filled... by the State Government.
plain_english_summary: Outlines that if the President's post at a District Commission becomes vacant, the State Government must step in to fill the vacancy.

title: Vacation of office by member
text: The President or a member of the District Commission may resign his office in writing under his hand addressed to the State Government...
plain_english_summary: Sets out the resignation process and rules under which members or Presidents of a District Commission vacate their office.

title: Establishment of State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
text: (1) The State Government shall, by notification, establish a State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission to be known as the State Commission...
plain_english_summary: Requires every State Government to establish a State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (State Commission) to handle mid-tier consumer disputes and hear appeals from District Commissions.

title: Jurisdiction of State Commission
text: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the State Commission shall have jurisdiction to— (a) entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds fifty lakh rupees, but does not exceed two crore rupees... and (b) appeals against the orders of any District Commission within the State...
plain_english_summary: Sets State Commission jurisdiction: handles original complaints where consideration is between ₹50 Lakhs and ₹2 Crores, and hears appeals against District Commission orders.

title: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
text: (1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish a National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission to be known as the National Commission.
plain_english_summary: Requires the Central Government to establish the **National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (National Commission)** at the apex level.

title: Jurisdiction of National Commission
text: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the National Commission shall have jurisdiction to— (a) entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds two crore rupees... and (b) appeals against the orders of any State Commission...
plain_english_summary: Sets National Commission jurisdiction: handles high-value consumer complaints where consideration exceeds ₹2 Crores, and hears appeals against orders passed by State Commissions.

title: Procedure on admission of complaint
text: (1) The District Commission shall, on admission of a complaint, refer a copy of the admitted complaint, directing the opposite party to give his version of the case within a period of thirty days or such extended period not exceeding fifteen days as may be granted by the District Commission.
plain_english_summary: Outlines trial procedures: once a complaint is accepted, the opposing company has 30 days (extendable by up to 15 days) to file their defense reply.

title: Findings of the District Commission
