text: (1) Where the District Commission is satisfied that the goods complained against suffer from any of the defects specified in the complaint or that any of the allegations contained in the complaint about services are proved, it shall issue an order to the opposite party directing him to do one or more of the following things, namely:— (a) to remove the defect... (b) to replace the goods... (c) to return to the consumer the price paid...
plain_english_summary: Empowers the District Commission to issue binding orders when a complaint is proven, such as forcing a company to repair defects, replace goods, refund money, or pay compensation for damages and unfair trade practices.

title: Review by District Commission in certain cases
text: The District Commission shall have the power to review any of the order passed by it if there is an error apparent on the face of the record, either of its own motion or on an application made by any of the parties within thirty days of such order.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the District Commission to review and fix any of its own orders if there is an obvious, glaring error on the face of the record, either independently or upon a request filed within 30 days.

title: Appeal against order of District Commission
text: Any person aggrieved by an order made by the District Commission may prefer an appeal against such order to the State Commission on the grounds of facts or law within a period of forty-five days from Knox the date of the order, in such form and manner as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: If a party is unhappy with a ruling from a District Commission, they have the right to file an appeal with the State Commission within 45 days of the order.

title: Qualifications, etc., of President and members of State Commission
text: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules to provide for the qualifications, method of recruitment, term of office, resignation and removal of the President and members of the State Commission.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to establish standard rules regarding the qualifications, recruitment procedures, and tenure of the President and members serving on State Commissions.

title: Salaries, allowances and other terms and conditions of service of President and members of State Commission
text: The salaries and allowances payable to, and the other terms and conditions of service of, the President and members of the State Commission shall be such as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Specifies that the salaries, allowances, and working terms of the President and members of State Commissions are regulated by rules made by the Central Government.

title: Transitional provision
text: The President and members of the State Commission holding office immediately before the commencement of this Act shall hold office as such for such period as remaining under their terms.
plain_english_summary: Transitional clause ensuring that existing State Commission members holding office prior to the 2019 Act are allowed to finish out the remainder of their terms.

title: Vacancy, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of State Commission
text: No act or proceeding of the State Commission shall be called in question on the ground merely of the existence of any vacancy in or any defect in the constitution of the State Commission.
plain_english_summary: Protects State Commission orders and proceedings from being challenged or invalidated purely due to an empty seat or minor structural vacancy.

title: Officers and other employees of State Commission
text: (1) The State Government shall provide the State Commission with such officers and other employees as may be necessary for assisting the State Commission in its work.
plain_english_summary: Requires each State Government to supply necessary administrative staff and employees to help the State Commission perform its duties.

title: Jurisdiction of State Commission
text: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the State Commission shall have jurisdiction to— (a) entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds fifty lakh rupees, but does not exceed two crore rupees... and (b) appeals against the orders of any District Commission within the State...
plain_english_summary: Defines the dual role of the State Commission: handling original mid-tier complaints valued between ₹50 Lakhs and ₹2 Crores, and hearing appeals filed against District Commission rulings.

title: Transfer of cases
text: The State Commission may, on application of any of the parties and after notice to the parties, and after hearing such of them as may desire to be heard, or of its own motion, transfer any pending complaint before any District Commission within the State to any other District Commission within the State.
plain_english_summary: Grants the State Commission the authority to transfer an active consumer complaint from one District Commission to another within the same state, either on request or on its own initiative.

title: Procedure applicable to State Commission
text: (1) The provisions relating to complaints under section 35 shall, with such modifications as may be necessary, apply to complaints preferred before the State Commission.
plain_english_summary: Applies standard complaint filing, documentation, and hearing procedures (similar to those used in District Commissions) to proceedings before the State Commission.

title: Review by State Commission in certain cases
text: The State Commission shall have power to review any of the order passed by it if there is an error apparent on the face of the record, either of its own motion or on an application made by any of the parties within thirty days of such order.
plain_english_summary: Allows the State Commission to review and modify its own previous orders within 30 days if there is a glaring, obvious error apparent on the face of the record.

title: Appeal to National Commission
text: (1) Any person aggrieved by an order made by the State Commission under sub-clause (i) or sub-clause (ii) of clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 47 may prefer an appeal against such order to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of the order.
plain_english_summary: Provides a right of appeal: any party dissatisfied with a final order or decision issued by a State Commission can appeal to the National Commission within 30 days.

title: Hearing of appeal
text: An appeal filed before the State Commission or the National Commission shall be heard as expeditiously as possible and endeavor shall be made to dispose of the appeal within a period of ninety days from the date of its admission.
plain_english_summary: Establishes a fast-track goal for appellate reviews: State and National Commissions should endeavor to hear and dispose of appeals within 90 days of admission.

title: Establishment of National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
text: (1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission to be known as the National Commission.
plain_english_summary: Mandates the Central Government to officially set up the apex National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

title: Composition of National Commission
text: The National Commission shall consist of— (a) a President; and (b) not less than four and not more than such number of members as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Specifies that the National Commission is composed of a President and a prescribed number of members (at least four members alongside the President).

title: Qualifications, etc., of President and members of National Commission
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification, make rules to provide for qualifications, method of recruitment, term of office, resignation and removal of the President and members of the National Commission.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to set qualification criteria, recruitment methods, terms of office, and removal rules for the President and members of the National Commission.

title: Transitional provision
text: The President and members of the National Commission holding office immediately before the commencement of this Act shall hold office as such for such period as remaining under their terms.
plain_english_summary: Transitional clause protecting the tenure of existing members and President of the National Commission when the 2019 Act came into force.

title: Other officers and employees of National Commission
text: (1) The Central Government shall provide the National Commission with such officers and other employees as may be necessary for assisting the National Commission in its work.
plain_english_summary: Requires the Central Government to provide the National Commission with necessary administrative officers and support staff.

title: Jurisdiction of National Commission
text: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the National Commission shall have jurisdiction to— (a) entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds two crore rupees... and (b) appeals against the orders of any State Commission.
plain_english_summary: Sets the high-end jurisdictional limits of the National Commission: original complaints where consideration exceeds ₹2 Crores, and appellate reviews against orders passed by any State Commission.

title: Jurisdiction of National Commission to review and set aside ex parte orders
text: The National Commission shall have the power to review its own orders or set aside ex parte orders passed by it in appropriate circumstances.
plain_english_summary: Gives the National Commission explicit power to review its previous decisions and set aside ex parte orders (rulings made when one party failed to show up) under appropriate circumstances.

title: Review by National Commission in certain cases
text: The National Commission shall have the power to review any of the order passed by it if there is an error apparent on the face of the record, either of its own motion or on an application made by any of the parties within thirty days of such order.
plain_english_summary: Grants the National Commission the authority to review and modify its own previous orders within 30 days if there is an obvious, glaring error apparent on the face of the record.

title: Power to set aside ex parte orders
text: Where an order is passed ex parte against the opposite party, he may apply to the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, to set aside such order if he satisfies the Commission that there was sufficient cause for his absence.
plain_english_summary: Allows any of the Consumer Commissions to set aside an ex parte order (a ruling made when the opposing party failed to show up) if that party can prove they had a valid, sufficient reason for missing the hearing.

title: Transfer of cases
text: On the application of any of the parties and after notice to the parties, and after hearing such of them as may desire to be heard, the Supreme Court may, at any stage, if it is expedient so to do for the ends of justice, direct that any complaint pending before the National Commission be transferred to any other State Commission or from one State Commission to another State Commission.
plain_english_summary: Grants the Supreme Court of India the ultimate power to transfer a pending consumer complaint from one State Commission to another or out of the National Commission to ensure absolute fairness and justice.

title: Vacancy in office of President of National Commission
text: When the office of President of the National Commission is vacant or when the President is, by reason of absence or otherwise, unable to perform the duties of his office, then such of the members of the National Commission as the Central Government may authorize in this behalf shall perform the duties of the President...
plain_english_summary: Outlines that if the President's post at the National Commission is vacant or the President is absent, the Central Government can authorize another senior member to temporarily step in and perform those presidential duties.

title: Vacancies or defects in appointment not to invalidate orders
text: No act or proceeding of the National Commission shall be called in question on the ground merely of the existence of any vacancy in or any defect in the constitution of the National Commission.
plain_english_summary: Ensures that rulings issued by the National Commission remain completely legal and valid, even if a vacancy or technical appointment defect existed during the proceedings.
keywords: vacancies or defects do not invalidate

title: Service of notice, etc.
text: (1) All notices, required by this Act to be served, shall be served by delivering in person or by registered post or by speed post or by such electronic mode as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Defines the legally valid methods for delivering court notices and summonses under the Act, including hand delivery, registered post, speed post, or approved electronic channels (like email).

title: Experts to assist National Commission or State Commission
text: The National Commission or the State Commission may, for the purposes of any proceedings under this Act, appoint any person having special knowledge or experience as an expert to assist the Commission.
plain_english_summary: Allows State and National Commissions to bring in independent technical experts or specialists to assist them in evaluating complex engineering, medical, or commercial product evidence during a case.

title: Appeal against order of National Commission
text: Any person aggrieved by an order made by the National Commission on a complaint under clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 58 may prefer an appeal against such order to the Supreme Court within a period of thirty days from the date of the order.
plain_english_summary: Provides the final route of judicial appeal: any party dissatisfied with an original order passed by the National Commission can appeal directly to the Supreme Court of India within 30 days.

title: Finality of orders
text: Every order of a District Commission, State Commission or the National Commission if no appeal has been preferred against such order under the provisions of this Act shall be final.
plain_english_summary: Establishes that orders passed by any Consumer Commission become legally final and binding if no timely appeal is filed against them.

title: Limitation period
text: (1) The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.
plain_english_summary: Statute of Limitations: Consumer Commissions are barred from accepting any complaint unless it is officially filed within 2 years from the date the cause of action (defect, injury, or breach) occurred.

title: Administrative control
text: (1) The State Commission shall have administrative control over all the District Commissions within its jurisdiction in such manner as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Gives State Commissions supervisory and administrative oversight over all District Commissions operating within their state boundaries.

title: Enforcement of orders of District Commission, State Commission and National Commission
text: Every order made by a District Commission, State Commission or the National Commission shall be enforced by the Commission in the same manner as if it were a decree made by a Court in a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
plain_english_summary: Consumer Commission orders carry the exact legal weight of a civil court decree and can be enforced directly through civil execution powers (such as attaching property or bank accounts).

title: Penalty for non-compliance of order
text: (1) Where a {@opposing party@} fails to comply with any order made by a District Commission or a State Commission or the National Commission, such Commission may punish him with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month, but which may extend to three years, or with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees, but which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Penalties for Contempt/Non-Compliance: If a business or individual ignores or refuses to obey a Consumer Commission order, the Commission can punish them with imprisonment ranging from 1 month up to 3 years, fines from ₹25,000 to ₹1 Lakh, or both.

title: Appeal against order passed under section 72
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, an appeal shall lie from any order passed under section 72 (whether punishing for non-compliance or refusing to punish) — (a) where the order has been passed by the District Commission, to the State Commission... and (b) where the order has been passed by the State Commission, to the National Commission...
plain_english_summary: Allows a party punished or aggrieved by a non-compliance penalty order under Section 72 to appeal that specific enforcement penalty to the next higher Commission tier.

title: Establishment of consumer mediation cell
text: (1) Every State Government shall establish, by notification, a consumer mediation cell to be attached to each of the District Commissions and the State Commissions.
plain_english_summary: Establishes formal Consumer Mediation Cells attached to every District and State Commission across the country to facilitate out-of-court settlements.

title: Empanelment of mediators
text: (1) Every Commission shall prepare a panel of the mediators to be maintained by the consumer mediation cell attached to it.
plain_english_summary: Requires every Consumer Commission to maintain an official panel of certified, qualified mediators through its attached mediation cell.

title: Nomination of mediators from panel
text: (1) The Commission shall, while nominating any person from the panel of mediators... consider the suitability of the person for resolving the consumer dispute.
plain_english_summary: Directs Commissions to carefully evaluate the suitability, background, and expertise of mediators when nominating them from the panel to handle a specific consumer dispute.

title: Duty of mediator to disclose certain facts
text: (1) Where a person is approached in connection with his possible appointment as a mediator, he shall disclose in writing to the Commission any circumstances likely to give rise to justifiable doubt as to his independence or impartiality.
plain_english_summary: Requires any prospective mediator to make full written disclosures regarding any potential conflicts of interest that could compromise their independence or impartiality.

title: Replacement of mediator in certain cases
text: (1) Where the Commission is satisfied... that the circumstances disclosed by a mediator under section 77 give rise to justifiable doubt as to his independence or impartiality, the Commission shall replace him with another mediator.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Commission to replace a mediator if a conflict of interest arises or if their impartiality is called into question.

title: Procedure for mediation
text: (1) The mediation shall be conducted in such manner and procedure as may be specified by regulations.
plain_english_summary: Mandates that court-annexed consumer mediations must follow the established procedural guidelines and regulations set out under the Act.

title: Settlement through mediation
text: (1) Where a settlement agreement is reached between the parties in consumer mediation, the same shall be reduced to writing and signed by the parties or their-authorized representatives.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Commission shall pass an order in terms of such settlement, thereby disposing of the consumer dispute.

plain_english_summary: If a consumer dispute successfully settles through mediation, the agreement must be put in writing and signed. The Commission will then issue a formal order based on that settlement, officially closing the case.

title: Sharing of mediation fee and cost
text: The mediator's fee and other incidental costs of mediation shall be shared equally by the parties or as may be agreed upon between them in the settlement agreement.
plain_english_summary: Unless the parties agree otherwise in their settlement, the fees and costs of the mediator are shared equally between the consumer and the opposing business.

title: Confidentiality
text: (1) The mediator shall maintain utmost confidentiality in respect of all proceedings conducted through mediation.
plain_english_summary: Mediators must maintain strict confidentiality regarding all statements, discussions, and documents shared during the mediation proceedings.

title: Application of Chapter
text: This Chapter shall apply to every claim for product liability brought by a consumer against a product manufacturer, product service provider or product seller, as the case may be.
plain_english_summary: Establishes that Chapter VI governs all product liability lawsuits brought by consumers against product manufacturers, service providers, or commercial sellers.

title: Liability of product manufacturer
text: (1) A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the product contains a manufacturing defect; or (b) the product is defective in design; or (c) there is deviation from manufacturing specifications; or (d) the product does not conform to the express warranty; or (e) the product fails to contain adequate instructions of correct usage to prevent any harm...
plain_english_summary: A product manufacturer is legally liable for damages if their product has manufacturing or design defects, deviates from specs, breaches an express warranty, or fails to include adequate safety and usage instructions.

title: Liability of product service provider
text: (1) A product service provider shall be liable in a product liability action, if the service provided by him was faulty, imperfect or deficient or inadequate in quality, nature or manner of performance...
plain_english_summary: A product service provider is liable for product-related services if they are performed in a faulty, imperfect, or deficient manner, or fail to meet the required quality standards.

title: Liability of product sellers
text: (1) A product seller who is not a product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) he has exercised substantial control over the design, testing, manufacturing, packaging or labeling of the product... (b) he has altered or modified the product... (c) he has made an express warranty of a product independent of any express warranty made by a manufacturer...
plain_english_summary: A product seller (retailer/distributor) can be held liable if they exercised control over manufacturing, altered the product, made independent warranties, or failed to identify the actual manufacturer when requested.

title: Exceptions to liability of product manufacturer
text: (1) A product manufacturer shall not be liable in a product liability action if he proves that the product was misused, altered, or modified by the consumer, or that the defect was due to obeying mandatory government regulations.
plain_english_summary: Provides safe harbors for manufacturers: they are not liable if the consumer misused or altered the product, or if the defect was caused strictly by complying with mandatory government standards.

title: Punishment for non-compliance of direction of Central Authority
text: Whoever fails to comply with any order or direction issued by the Central Authority under section 20 or section 21 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to twenty lakh rupees, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Penalizes defying CCPA orders: anyone who ignores CCPA directions regarding misleading ads or investigations faces up to 6 months in prison, a fine up to ₹20 Lakhs, or both.

title: Punishment for false or misleading advertisement
text: Any manufacturer or service provider who causes an advertisement which is false or misleading to be made shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees; and for every subsequent offence, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to fifty lakh rupees.
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalties for misleading ads: manufacturers or service providers publishing false ads face up to 2 years in prison and a ₹10 Lakh fine, scaling up to 5 years in prison and a ₹50 Lakh fine for repeat offenses.

title: Punishment for manufacturing for sale or storing, selling or distributing or importing products containing adulterants
text: (1) Whoever, by himself or by any other person on his behalf, manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any product containing adulterant shall be punished, if such act— (a) results in non-injury... (b) results in injury... (c) results in death...
plain_english_summary: Severe criminal punishments for selling adulterated products: prison terms and fines scale depending on the harm caused, ranging from minor fines up to life imprisonment if adulteration results in a consumer's death.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: No court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act except on a complaint made by the Central Authority or any officer authorized by it in this behalf.
plain_english_summary: Criminal courts cannot take up or prosecute offenses under this Act unless the formal complaint is filed by the CCPA or an authorized government officer.

title: Compounding of offences
text: (1) Any offence punishable under section 88 or section 89, whether committed by a manufacturer or endorser, may, either before or after the institution of any prosecution, be compounded by the National Commission or a court...
plain_english_summary: Allows certain non-violent offenses (like ad violations under sections 88 and 89) to be compounded (settled out of court via financial payments) through the Commission or a court.

title: Measures to prevent unfair trade practices in e-commerce, etc.
text: The Central Government may take such measures as may be prescribed to prevent unfair trade practices in e-commerce, direct selling and electronic service providers.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to issue regulatory guidelines and rules specifically targeting unfair trade practices across e-commerce platforms and direct selling networks.
keywords: Measures to prevent unfair trade practices

title: President, members, etc., to be public servants
text: The President and members of the District Commission, State Commission and National Commission, and officers and employees of the Central Authority and Commissions shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
plain_english_summary: Designates all members, Presidents, and officers of Consumer Commissions and the CCPA as official 'public servants' under Indian law.

title: Protection of action taken in good faith
text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Central Government, the Central Authority, the President, any member, officer or person acting under the direction of the Central Authority for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act...
plain_english_summary: Provides legal immunity from lawsuits and personal prosecution to government officials, CCPA members, and Commission judges for actions taken in good faith while executing their duties under the Act.
keywords: Protection of action taken in good faith

title: Power to make rules by Central Government
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Grants the Central Government general rulemaking powers via official notifications to properly administer and enforce the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act.

title: Power of State Government to make rules
text: (1) The State Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act relating to State and District Commissions.
plain_english_summary: Grants State Governments the authority to formulate state-level rules regarding the operation of State and District Commissions.
keywords: Power of State Government to make rules

title: Power of National Commission to make regulations
text: (1) The National Commission may, with the previous approval of the Central Government, make regulations not inconsistent with this Act to provide for all matters for which provision is necessary or expedient for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the National Commission, with central approval, to draft internal regulations governing its case management and procedural practices.
keywords: Power of National Commission to make regulations

title: Power of Central Authority to make regulations
text: (1) The Central Authority may, with the previous approval of the Central Government, make regulations not inconsistent with this Act for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the CCPA, with central approval, to formulate operational regulations to enforce its consumer protection mandates and investigation standards.
keywords: Power of Central Authority to make regulations

title: Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament
text: (1) Every rule and regulation made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament... while it is in session...
plain_english_summary: Requires all rules and regulations framed under this Act to be officially laid before both Houses of Parliament for review.

title: Power of Central Government to remove difficulties
text: (1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may, by order, published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, as appear to it to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty: Provided that no such order shall be made under this section after the expiry of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Transitional power enabling the Central Government to issue orders to remove any practical administrative difficulties during the first two years of the Act's rollout.

title: Amendment of certain enactments
text: The enactments specified in the Schedule are hereby amended in the manner specified therein.
plain_english_summary: Provides for consequential amendments to other legacy statutes as outlined in the schedule attached to the Act.

title: Repeal and savings
text: (1) The Consumer Protection Act, 1986 is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Act shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Formally repeals the old Consumer Protection Act of 1986, while containing 'savings' language ensuring that past actions, ongoing cases, and orders under the 1986 Act remain legally valid under the new 2019 framework.

title: Power of State Government to make rules in certain cases
text: (1) The State Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act relating to State and District Commissions.
plain_english_summary: Reiterates the state-level rulemaking powers regarding local commission setups and administrative operations.

title: Power of Central Government to make rules
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Confirms the central government's overarching authority to issue rules and notifications for effective national enforcement.

title: Power of National Commission to make regulations
text: (1) The National Commission may, with the previous approval of the Central Government, make regulations consistent with this Act.
plain_english_summary: Authorizes the National Commission to draft procedural regulations for its tribunals with central government approval.

title: Power of Central Authority to make regulations
text: (1) The Central Authority may, with the previous approval of the Central Government, make regulations consistent with this Act.
plain_english_summary: Concludes the Act by granting the CCPA the power to issue internal regulations for managing its investigations and regulatory functions.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Appointment and tenure of interim resolution professional
text: (1) The Adjudicating Authority shall appoint an interim resolution professional on the insolvency commencement date. (2) The term of the interim resolution professional shall not exceed thirty days from date of his appointment.
plain_english_summary: The NCLT appoints an Interim Resolution Professional (IRP) immediately upon admitting an insolvency case. The IRP's short-term tenure lasts for a maximum of 30 days while claims are collated.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Management of affairs of corporate debtor by interim resolution professional
text: (1) From the insolvency commencement date,— (a) the management of the affairs of the corporate debtor shall vest in the interim resolution professional; (b) the powers of the board of directors... of the corporate debtor shall stand suspended and be exercised by the interim resolution professional...
plain_english_summary: Management Takeover: The moment the IRP is appointed, the company's Board of Directors is instantly suspended. All management powers, control of assets, and operations shift entirely to the IRP.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Duties of interim resolution professional
text: The interim resolution professional shall perform the following duties, namely:— (a) collect all information relating to the assets, finances and operations of the corporate debtor... (b) receive and collate all the claims submitted by creditors... (c) constitute a committee of creditors...
plain_english_summary: Outlines the core duties of the IRP: gathering financial records, collating all creditor claims, taking control of company assets, and officially forming the Committee of Creditors (CoC).

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Personnel to extend cooperation to interim resolution professional
text: (1) The personnel, promoters and any other person associated with the corporate debtor shall extend all assistance and cooperation to the interim resolution professional as may be required by him in managing the affairs of the corporate debtor.
plain_english_summary: Founders, promoters, and company employees are legally mandated to fully cooperate with the IRP, hand over passwords/records, and provide unhindered access to company data.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Management of operations of corporate debtor as going concern
text: (1) The interim resolution professional shall make every endeavour to protect and preserve the value of the property of the corporate debtor and manage the operations of the corporate debtor as a going concern.
plain_english_summary: The IRP must make every effort to keep the distressed company running as a 'going concern' rather than shutting it down immediately, preserving its business value for a potential turnaround.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Committee of creditors
text: (1) The interim resolution professional shall after collation of all claims received against the corporate debtor and determination of the financial position of the corporate debtor, constitute a committee of creditors.

sub_structure.2: (2) The committee of creditors shall comprise all financial creditors of the corporate debtor...
sub_structure.2_proviso: Provided that a financial creditor or the authorised representative of the financial creditor... if it is a related party of the corporate debtor shall not have any right of representation, participation or voting in a meeting of the committee of creditors...

plain_english_summary: The Committee of Creditors (CoC) is formed entirely of the company's financial creditors (banks, lenders, bondholders). Related parties (like sister companies or family members of founders who lent money) are strictly barred from sitting on or voting in the CoC to prevent conflicts of interest.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Appointment of resolution professional
text: (1) The first meeting of the committee of creditors shall be held within seven days of the constitution of the committee of creditors. (2) The committee of creditors, may, at the first meeting, by a majority vote of not less than sixty-six per cent. of the voting share of the financial creditors, either resolve to appoint the interim resolution professional as a resolution professional or to replace him.
plain_english_summary: At its first meeting (held within 7 days of formation), the Committee of Creditors votes by a 66% majority to either confirm the IRP as the permanent Resolution Professional (RP) or replace them with someone else.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Resolution professional to conduct corporate insolvency resolution process
text: (1) Subject to section 27, the resolution professional shall conduct the entire corporate insolvency resolution process and manage the operations of the corporate debtor during the corporate insolvency resolution process period.
plain_english_summary: The Resolution Professional (RP) manages the day-to-day operations of the company and drives the entire insolvency resolution process under the instructions of the CoC.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Meeting of committee of creditors
text: (1) The members of the committee of creditors may meet in person or by such electronic means as may be permitted. (3) The resolution professional shall give notice of each meeting of the committee of creditors to every member of the committee of creditors...
plain_english_summary: Governs Committee of Creditors meetings: the RP must give formal notice to all financial creditors, and meetings can be held in person or via video/electronic channels.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Duties of resolution professional
text: (1) It shall be the duty of the resolution professional to preserve and protect all the assets of the corporate debtor including the continued business operations... (2) The resolution professional shall undertake the following actions, namely:— (a) take immediate custody and control of all the assets... (b) prepare an information memorandum... (c) invite prospective resolution applicants...
plain_english_summary: Outlines the comprehensive duties of the RP: taking physical and legal control of company assets, running the business, drafting the Information Memorandum, and inviting outside investors to submit turnaround resolution plans.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Rights and duties of authorised representative of financial creditors
text: (1) Where a financial debt is owed to a class of creditors exceeding such number as may be specified... the resolution professional shall make an application to the Adjudicating Authority to appoint an authorised representative... to act on behalf of such creditors.
plain_english_summary: Provides for an Authorized Representative (like a trustee for a large pool of home-buyers or debenture holders) to vote and represent their collective interests on the Committee of Creditors.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Application for avoidance of transactions not to affect proceedings
text: The filing of an application by the resolution professional under sub-section (2) of section 25 in respect of avoidable transactions shall not affect the proceedings of the corporate insolvency resolution process.
plain_english_summary: If the RP files lawsuits to claw back suspicious or fraudulent asset transfers made before insolvency, those separate avoidance legal proceedings will not delay or halt the main ongoing CIRP timeline.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Replacement of resolution professional by committee of creditors
text: (1) Where the committee of creditors, at any time during the corporate insolvency resolution process, is of the opinion that the resolution professional appointed under section 22 should be replaced, it may replace him with another resolution professional, by a vote of sixty-six per cent. of the voting share.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Committee of Creditors to replace an active Resolution Professional at any point during the insolvency process by passing a vote requiring at least a 66% majority.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Approval of committee of creditors for certain actions
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the resolution professional, during the corporate insolvency resolution process, shall not take any of the following actions without the prior approval of the committee of creditors approved by a vote of sixty-six per cent. of the voting share:— (a) raise any interim finance exceeding specified amount... (b) create any security interest over the assets... (c) change the capital structure... etc.
plain_english_summary: Major Actions Require CoC Approval: The RP cannot take major corporate actions (such as raising fresh debt, selling core assets, or changing capital structure) without obtaining prior approval from at least 66% of the Committee of Creditors.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Preparation of information memorandum
text: (1) The resolution professional shall prepare an information memorandum in such form and manner containing such relevant information as may be specified by the Board in order to formulate a resolution plan.
plain_english_summary: Requires the RP to compile a comprehensive 'Information Memorandum' detailing the company's financial health, asset valuations, liabilities, and operations to share with prospective buyers bidding to rescue the company.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Persons not eligible to be resolution applicant
text: A person shall not be eligible to submit a resolution plan, if such person, or any other person acting jointly or in concert with such person— (a) is an undischarged insolvent; (b) is a wilful defaulter... (c) has been convicted for any offence punishable with imprisonment for 2 years or more... (d) is disqualified to act as a director under the Companies Act... (e) has prohibited active accounts classified as non-performing assets...
plain_english_summary: The Promoters' Block (Section 29A): Prevents willful defaulters, convicted criminals, disqualified directors, and crucially, the original defaulting promoters themselves from bidding to buy back their own bankrupt company during insolvency, unless they clear all overdue debts first.
keywords: Persons not eligible to be resolution applicant

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Submission of resolution plan
text: (1) A resolution applicant may submit a resolution plan to the resolution professional prepared on the basis of the information memorandum.

sub_structure.4: (4) The committee of creditors may approve a resolution plan by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent. of voting share of the financial creditors, after considering its feasibility and viability...

plain_english_summary: Prospective buyers submit formal turnaround 'Resolution Plans' to the RP. The Committee of Creditors evaluates these plans and must approve the winning bid by at least a 66% majority vote.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Approval of resolution plan
text: (1) If the Adjudicating Authority is satisfied that the resolution plan as approved by the committee of creditors under sub-section (4) of section 30 meets the requirements... it shall by order approve the resolution plan which shall be binding on the corporate debtor and its employees, members, creditors...
plain_english_summary: Once the CoC approves a resolution plan, it goes to the NCLT for final legal sanction. When the NCLT approves it, the plan becomes legally binding on all stakeholders, creditors, employees, and government authorities.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Appeal
text: An appeal from an order approving the resolution plan under sub-section (1) of section 31 may be filed on the grounds specified under sub-section (3) of section 61 to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal.
plain_english_summary: Allows aggrieved parties to file an appeal against an NCLT order approving a resolution plan directly to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT).

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Initiation of liquidation
text: (1) Where the Adjudicating Authority,— (a) before the expiry of the corporate insolvency resolution process period or the maximum period permitted for completion... does not receive a resolution plan... or (b) rejects the resolution plan... it shall— (i) pass an order requiring the corporate debtor to be liquidated in the manner laid down in this Chapter...
plain_english_summary: Triggering Liquidation: If the 330-day insolvency timeline expires without a successful turnaround plan, or if the NCLT rejects all submitted resolution plans, the tribunal must issue a formal order to liquidate and shut down the company.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Appointment of liquidator and fee to be paid
text: (1) Where the Adjudicating Authority passes an order for liquidation of the corporate debtor under section 33, the resolution professional appointed for the corporate insolvency resolution process under Chapter II shall act as the liquidator unless replaced by the Adjudicating Authority...
plain_english_summary: When liquidation is ordered, the active Resolution Professional automatically steps into the role of 'Liquidator' to manage asset sales, unless the NCLT or CoC votes to replace them.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Powers and duties of liquidator
text: (1) Subject to the directions of the Adjudicating Authority, the liquidator shall have the following powers and duties, namely:— (a) to verify all claims submitted by creditors... (b) to take into his custody or control all the assets, property, effects and actionable claims of the corporate debtor... (c) to evaluate the assets and sell the immovable and movable property and actionable claims... by public auction or private contract...
plain_english_summary: Outlines the powers and duties of the Liquidator: taking complete control of the company's remaining assets, verifying creditor claims, and selling off properties via public auction or private sale to maximize recovery.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Liquidation estate
text: (1) For the purposes of liquidation, the liquidator shall form an estate of the assets mentioned in sub-section (3), which shall be called the liquidation estate in relation to the corporate debtor.

sub_structure.3: (3) Subject to sub-section (4), the liquidation estate shall comprise all and any of the following items, namely:— (a) assets over which the corporate debtor has ownership rights... (b) assets that may or may not be in possession of the corporate debtor... (c) tangible and intangible assets...

plain_english_summary: The Liquidator creates a consolidated 'Liquidation Estate' comprising all assets, properties, and legal rights owned by the corporate debtor to be pooled together and sold off to pay creditors.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Powers of liquidator to access information
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the liquidator shall have the access to any information systems of the central government, state governments, information utilities, financial institutions, and corporate records.
plain_english_summary: Grants the liquidator sweeping legal power to access private and public databases, financial records, registries, and information utilities to track down all corporate assets and records.
keywords: Powers of liquidator to access information

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Consolidation of claims
text: (1) The liquidator shall receive or collect claims of creditors within thirty days from the date of the commencement of the liquidation process.
plain_english_summary: Requires the liquidator to formally invite and collect all financial, operational, and employee claims against the company within 30 days of the liquidation start date.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Verification of claims
text: (1) The liquidator shall verify the claims submitted under section 38 within such time as may be specified.
plain_english_summary: Mandates that the liquidator review, audit, and verify the accuracy of all claims submitted by various creditors.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Admission or rejection of claims
text: (1) The liquidator may, after verification of claims under section 39, admit or reject the claim, in whole or in part.
plain_english_summary: Gives the liquidator the authority to officially accept or reject creditor claims (in whole or in part) following the verification process.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Determination of valuation of claims
text: The liquidator shall determine the value of claims admitted under section 40 in such manner as may be specified by the Board.
plain_english_summary: Requires the liquidator to calculate and determine the exact monetary value of all accepted claims to structure eventual payouts.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Appeal against decision of liquidator
text: A creditor may appeal against the decision of the liquidator accepting or rejecting the claims to the Adjudicating Authority within fourteen days from the date of the receipt of such decision.
plain_english_summary: If a creditor's claim is rejected or disputed by the liquidator, they have 14 days to appeal that decision to the NCLT.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Preferential transactions and relevant time
text: (1) Where the liquidator or the resolution professional, as the case may be, is of the opinion that the corporate debtor has at a relevant time given a preference in transactions to certain creditors... he shall apply to the Adjudicating Authority for avoidance of preferential transactions...
plain_english_summary: Clawback of Preferential Deals: If a company favored certain creditors over others just before going bankrupt (e.g., paying off a friendly lender while stiffing others), the RP/Liquidator can ask the NCLT to reverse those preferential transfers.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Orders in case of preferential transactions
text: The Adjudicating Authority may, on an application under sub-section (1) of section 43, pass an order- (a) requiring any property transferred in connection with preferential transaction to be vested in the corporate debtor...
plain_english_summary: Empowers the NCLT to issue orders reversing preferential deals, requiring transferred money or property to be returned to the company's liquidation pool.
keywords: Orders in case of preferential transactions

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Avoidance of undervalue transactions
text: (1) If the liquidator or the resolution professional, on an examination of the transactions of the corporate debtor... determines that certain transactions were entered into at an undervalue, he shall make an application to the Adjudicating Authority to declare such transactions void...
plain_english_summary: If a company sold off its assets for next to nothing (under-value transactions) to defraud creditors right before insolvency, the NCLT can declare those sales void and pull the assets back.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Relevant period for avoidable undervalue transactions
text: (1) In an application for avoiding a transaction at an undervalue, the liquidator or the resolution professional shall demonstrate that— (a) such transaction was made with a person within a period of one year preceding the insolvency commencement date... or (b) two years in case of related parties.
plain_english_summary: Sets the look-back window for under-value deals: 1 year for regular third-party transactions, and 2 years if the assets were sold cheap to 'related parties' (family, insiders, or affiliates).

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Application by creditor in cases of undervalue transactions
text: (1) Where an corporate debtor has entered into an undervalue transaction... and the liquidator or the resolution professional has not reported it to the Adjudicating Authority, a creditor... may make an application to the Adjudicating Authority...
plain_english_summary: If the liquidator fails to notice or report a cheap asset giveaway, individual creditors have the right to petition the NCLT directly to review and reverse the under-value transaction.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Orders in cases of undervalue transactions
text: The Adjudicating Authority may, on an application under section 45 or section 47, pass an order— (a) restoring the position as it was before such transaction... (b) requiring any property transferred to be vested in the corporate debtor...
plain_english_summary: Empowers the NCLT to restore the status quo ante, forcing buyers of under-valued assets to return them to the liquidation estate.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Transactions defrauding creditors
text: (1) Where the corporate debtor has entered into a transaction at an undervalue with intent to defraud creditors, the liquidator or the resolution professional shall apply to the Adjudicating Authority to declare such transaction void...
plain_english_summary: Specifically targets intentional asset-hiding schemes designed to cheat creditors. The NCLT can declare transactions defrauding creditors completely void regardless of time windows.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Extortionate credit transactions
text: (1) Where the corporate debtor has been a party to an extortionate credit transaction involving the receipt of financial or operational terms in respect of credit provided by any person at a relevant time... the liquidator or the resolution professional may make an application to the Adjudicating Authority for such transaction to be set aside...
plain_english_summary: Clawback of Usurious Loans: If a distressed company was forced to take out predatory loans carrying extortionate, sky-high interest rates right before bankruptcy, the RP can ask the NCLT to set aside or rewrite those abusive credit terms.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Orders of Adjudicating Authority in respect of extortionate credit transactions
text: Where the Adjudicating Authority after examining the application made under section 50 is satisfied that the terms of an extortionate credit transaction are exorbitant, it may... restore the position as it was before the transaction or set aside the whole or part of the debt created...
plain_english_summary: Empowers the NCLT to rewrite or entirely cancel predatory loan contracts, writing off extortionate interest rates and ordering lenders to refund abusive fees collected from the distressed company.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Secured creditor in liquidation proceedings
text: (1) A secured creditor in the liquidation proceedings may— (a) relinquish its security interest to the liquidation estate and receive proceeds from the sale of assets... or (b) realise its security interest...
plain_english_summary: Secured creditors have a choice during liquidation: they can either surrender their security to the common liquidation pool and take their proportional payout, or enforce their security interest independently to recover their specific collateral.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Distribution of assets
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law enacted by the Parliament or any State Legislature for the time being in force, the proceeds from the sale of the liquidation assets shall be distributed in the following order of priority:— (a) the insolvency resolution process costs and the liquidation costs paid in full; (b) the following debts which shall rank equally between and among the following:— (i) workmen’s dues for the period of twenty-four months preceding the liquidation commencement date; and (ii) debts owed to a secured creditor... (c) wages and any unpaid dues owed to employees other than workmen for the period of twelve months... (d) financial debts owed to unsecured creditors...
plain_english_summary: The Waterfall Mechanism (Section 53): Sets the strict statutory priority order for how money from asset sales is distributed during liquidation: 1) Insolvency & liquidation costs, 2) Workmen's dues (24 months) + Secured creditors ranking equally, 3) Employee wages (12 months), 4) Unsecured financial debts, 5) Government dues, 6) Any remaining equity to shareholders.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Fast track corporate insolvency resolution process
text: (1) A corporate insolvency resolution process may be fast tracked in such manner as may be specified by the Board, where the corporate debtor is— (a) a small company... or (b) a startup... or (c) an unlisted company with total assets not exceeding one crore rupees...
plain_english_summary: Fast-Track CIRP: Smaller companies, startups, and unlisted entities with assets under ₹1 Crore qualify for a fast-tracked insolvency process designed to wrap up much faster than standard cases.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Time-period for completion of fast track corporate insolvency resolution process
text: (1) A fast track corporate insolvency resolution process shall be completed within a period of ninety days from the insolvency commencement date: Provided that the Adjudicating Authority may extend the period... but such extension shall not exceed forty-five days.
plain_english_summary: Fast-Track Timeline: A fast-track insolvency process must be completed within 90 days, with a single potential extension of up to 45 days (max 135 days total).

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Power of- Central Government to make rules
text: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Chapter relating to fast track corporate insolvency resolution process.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to issue rules regarding the execution of fast-track corporate insolvency resolution processes.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Voluntary liquidation of corporate persons
text: (1) A corporate person who intends to liquidate itself voluntarily and has not committed any default may initiate voluntary liquidation proceedings under the provisions of this Chapter.

sub_structure.2: (2) The voluntary liquidation of a corporate person under sub-section (1) shall meet such conditions and procedural requirements as may be specified by the Board...
sub_structure.3: (3) Without prejudice to sub-section (2), voluntary liquidation proceedings shall meet the following conditions, namely:— (a) a declaration verified by an affidavit by the directors of the corporate person... that they have made a full inquiry into the affairs of the company and that the company has no debt or that it will be able to pay its debts in full... (b) the declaration under clause (a) shall be accompanied by— (i) audited financial statements... and records of business operations for the previous two years...

plain_english_summary: Voluntary Liquidation: Solvent companies or startups that have zero defaults can choose to wind down and liquidate themselves voluntarily, provided their directors sign a sworn affidavit declaring that the company is debt-free or can pay all its debts in full.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Adjudicating Authority for corporate persons
text: (1) The Adjudicating Authority, in relation to insolvency resolution and liquidation for corporate persons including corporate debtors and personal guarantors thereof shall be the National Company Law Tribunal having territorial jurisdiction over the place where the registered office of the corporate person is located.
plain_english_summary: Establishes that the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) holding jurisdiction over the company's registered office acts as the exclusive Adjudicating Authority for corporate insolvencies and personal guarantors.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Appeals and Appellate Authority
text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any person aggrieved by the order of the Adjudicating Authority under this part may appeal to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal.

sub_structure.2: (2) Every appeal under sub-section (1) shall be filed within thirty days before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal...
sub_structure.3: (3) An appeal against an order approving a resolution plan under section 31 may be filed on the following grounds, namely:— (i) the material irregularity in exercise of the powers by the resolution professional during the corporate insolvency resolution process...

plain_english_summary: Provides the right to appeal NCLT orders to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) within a 30-day window, detailing permissible grounds for challenging approved resolution plans.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Appeal to Supreme Court
text: (1) Any person aggrieved by an order of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal may appeal to the Supreme Court on a question of law arising out of such order under this Code within forty-five days from the date of receipt of such order.
plain_english_summary: Allows aggrieved parties to appeal NCLAT decisions directly to the Supreme Court of India within 45 days, provided the appeal raises a genuine question of law.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Civil court not to have jurisdiction
text: No civil court or authority shall have jurisdiction in respect of any matter in which the National Company Law Tribunal or the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal is empowered by, or under, this Code to pass any order and no injunction shall be granted by any court or other authority...
plain_english_summary: Civil Court Bar: Standard civil courts are strictly barred from hearing any insolvency matters, disputes, or granting injunctions over issues falling under the jurisdiction of the NCLT or NCLAT.
keywords: Civil court not to have jurisdiction

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Expeditious disposal of applications
text: (1) Where an application is not disposed of or an order is not passed within the period specified in this Code, the National Company Law Tribunal or the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, as the case may be, shall record the reasons for the same in writing...
plain_english_summary: Requires the NCLT and NCLAT to record written explanations if they miss statutory deadlines for disposing of insolvency applications, reinforcing the code's focus on speed.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Fraudulent or malicious initiation of proceedings
text: (1) If, any person initiates the insolvency resolution process or liquidation proceedings fraudulently or with malicious intent for any purpose other than for the resolution of insolvency, the Adjudicating Authority may impose upon such person a penalty which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but may extend to one crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Penalty for Malicious Insolvency Filings: If a creditor or applicant files for insolvency fraudulently or with malicious intent (e.g., to harass a company or extort a settlement), the NCLT can penalize them with fines ranging from ₹1 Lakh to ₹1 Crore.
keywords: Fraudulent or malicious initiation of proceedings
one lakh to one crore fine

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Fraudulent trading or wrongful trading
text: (1) If during the corporate insolvency resolution process or a liquidation process, it is found that any business of the corporate debtor has been carried on with intent to defraud creditors of the corporate debtor or for any fraudulent purpose, the Adjudicating Authority may on the application of the resolution professional pass an order that any persons who were knowingly parties to the carrying on of the business in such manner shall be liable to make such contributions to the assets of the corporate debtor as it may deem fit.
plain_english_summary: Wrongful and Fraudulent Trading: If founders or directors continued running the business while knowing the company was headed for bankruptcy and deliberately defrauded creditors, the NCLT can order them to personally contribute funds back into the company's asset pool.

chapter_title: INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION FOR CORPORATE PERSONS
title: Proceedings under section 66
text: (1) Where the Adjudicating Authority passes an order under sub-section (1) of section 66, it may direct that any sums payable by any person shall be included as a debt due to the corporate debtor...
plain_english_summary: Outlines the procedural mechanics and enforcement powers for recovering personal financial contributions ordered against fraudulent directors under Section 66.

title: Punishment for concealment of property
text: An officer of the corporate debtor shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than three years but which may extend to five years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to one crore rupees, if he— (a) does not disclose to the resolution professional all the property belonging to the corporate debtor...
plain_english_summary: Criminal Penalty for Hiding Assets: If a company officer or founder conceals company property, destroys records, or fails to disclose assets to the RP during insolvency, they face 3 to 5 years in prison and fines up to ₹1 Crore.
keywords: imprisonment for three to five years

title: Punishment for transactions defrauding creditors
text: An officer of the corporate debtor shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than one year but which may extend to five years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to one crore rupees, if he— (a) has done or caused to be done any of the specified acts with intent to defraud creditors...
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalty for officers who engage in intentional transactions designed to cheat or defraud company creditors prior to or during insolvency (1 to 5 years in prison and up to ₹1 Crore in fines).

title: Punishment for misconduct in course of corporate insolvency resolution process
text: (1) On or after the insolvency commencement date, where an officer of the corporate debtor— (a) does not deliver up to the resolution professional all books and papers... or (b) conceals any part of the estate of the corporate debtor... he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than three years and up to five years, and fine up to one crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalty for officers who refuse to hand over books, conceal company books, or lie to the IRP/RP during the insolvency resolution process (3 to 5 years imprisonment and up to ₹1 Crore in fines).

title: Punishment for falsification of books of corporate debtor
text: Where any person, being an officer or a creditor of the corporate debtor, destroys, mutilates, alters or falsifies any books, papers or securities, or makes any false entry in any register... he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than one year, but which may extend to five years, and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to one crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalty for cooking the books: Falsifying, destroying, altering, or making fake entries in company financial records during insolvency carries 1 to 5 years in prison and fines up to ₹1 Crore.

title: Punishment for willful and material omissions from statements relating to affairs
text: Where any officer of the corporate debtor makes any material omission in any statement relating to the affairs of the corporate debtor, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than one year, but which may extend to three years, and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to one crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalty for officers who willfully omit material financial details from official statements submitted during insolvency proceedings (1 to 3 years imprisonment and fines up to ₹1 Crore).

title: Punishment for false representations to creditors
text: Where any officer of the corporate debtor makes any false representation or commits any fraud for the purpose of obtaining the consent of the creditors to any agreement relating to the affairs of the corporate debtor, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than one year, but which may extend to five years, and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to one crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalty for officers who lie, trick, or make false representations to trick creditors into approving an insolvency settlement or restructuring agreement.
keywords: Punishment for false representations to creditors

title: Punishment for contravention of moratorium or resolution plan
text: (1) Where the corporate debtor or any of its officer violates the provisions of section 14 [the moratorium], any such officer who knowingly or wilfully permitted or authorised the violation shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than three years, but which may extend to five years or with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to three lakh rupees, or with both.

sub_structure.3: (3) Where any person violates any of the provisions of a resolution plan approved by the Adjudicating Authority... such person shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than one year, but which may extend to five years, or with fine... or with both.

plain_english_summary: Criminal Penalty for Breaking the Moratorium: Founders or officers who knowingly violate the legal moratorium freeze (Section 14) or breach an approved resolution plan face 3 to 5 years in prison and heavy financial fines.

title: Punishment for false information furnished in application
text: Where any person furnishes information in an application for initiating corporate insolvency resolution process under section 7, section 9 or section 10, which is false in material particulars knowing it to be false or omits any material particulars knowing it to be material, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than one year, but which may extend to five years, or with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to one crore rupees, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Criminal Penalty for Fake Insolvency Applications: Anyone who knowingly submits false information or hides material facts in an initial insolvency application (under sections 7, 9, or 10) faces 1 to 5 years in prison and fines up to ₹1 Crore.
keywords: Punishment for false information in application

title: Punishment for non-compliance of orders
text: Where any person willfully and intentionally disregards or disobeys any order of the Adjudicating Authority, the Appellate Tribunal or the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one crore rupees, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalty for anyone who willfully disregards or disobeys official orders passed by the NCLT, NCLAT, or the IBBI, carrying up to 1 year in prison, a fine up to ₹1 Crore, or both.

title: Penalty for offences in absence of specific provision
text: Where any person contravenes any provision of this Code or the rules or regulations made thereunder for which no specific penalty or punishment is provided, such person shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to two crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: General penalty provision: any violation of the Code, rules, or regulations that lacks a specific designated punishment carries a fine ranging from ₹1 Lakh to ₹2 Crores.

chapter_title: THE INSOLVENCY AND BANKRUPTCY BOARD OF INDIA
title: Establishment and incorporation of Board
text: (1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India to exercise the functions assigned to it under this Code.
plain_english_summary: Establishes the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI)** as the primary regulator and administrative body governing insolvency professionals, agencies, and utilities under the Code.
keywords: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India

chapter_title: THE INSOLVENCY AND BANKRUPTCY BOARD OF INDIA
title: Powers and functions of Board
text: (1) The Board shall, general or special orders, perform all or any of the following functions:— (a) register insolvency professional agencies, insolvency professionals and information utilities... (b) specify standards for the functioning of insolvency professionals... (c) monitor the performance of insolvency professionals...
plain_english_summary: Outlines the sweeping regulatory powers and functions of the IBBI: registering and monitoring insolvency professionals, setting operational standards, and overseeing information utilities.

title: Functions and obligations of insolvency professionals
text: (1) Where any insolvency resolution, liquidation or bankruptcy process has been initiated, it shall be conducted by an insolvency professional... (2) All insolvency professionals shall abide by the code of conduct specified by the Board...
plain_english_summary: Mandates that all insolvency processes must be run by registered Insolvency Professionals (IPs) who are legally bound to follow a strict ethical code of conduct set by the IBBI.

title: Investigation of insolvency professional agencies or professionals
text: (1) The Board may, on receipt of a complaint or on its own motion, appoint one or more persons to conduct an investigation into the affairs of the insolvency professional agency or insolvency professional...
plain_english_summary: Empowers the IBBI to launch formal investigations into the conduct of registered insolvency professionals or agencies based on complaints or independent reviews.

title: Registration of information utilities
text: (1) No person shall carry on its business as an information utility under this Code unless it holds a certificate of registration issued by the Board...
plain_english_summary: Mandates that any entity operating as an 'Information Utility' (digital data repositories that track debt defaults and financial records) must hold a valid registration certificate from the IBBI.

title: Provisions of this Code to override other laws
text: The provisions of this Code shall have effect, notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force or any instrument having effect by virtue of any such law.
plain_english_summary: The Overriding Clause (Section 238): The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code holds supreme legal precedence over all other inconsistent state or central laws, ensuring bankruptcy proceedings are not blocked by conflicting statutes.
keywords: Provisions of this Code to override other laws

title: Limitation
text: The provisions of the Limitation Act, 1963 shall, as far as may be, apply to the proceedings or appeals before the Adjudicating Authority, the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, the Debt Recovery Tribunal or the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal, as the case may be.
plain_english_summary: Clarifies that the standard Limitation Act of 1963 applies to insolvency proceedings before the NCLT and NCLAT, meaning time-barred debts cannot be admitted for insolvency filings.

title: Power of Central Government to make rules
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Code.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to issue rules via official notifications to implement the nationwide framework of the Code.
keywords: Power of Central Government to make rules

title: Power of Board to make regulations
text: (1) The Board may, by notification and consistent with this Code and the rules made thereunder, make regulations to carry out the provisions of this Code.
plain_english_summary: Grants the IBBI regulatory rulemaking power to issue administrative regulations governing insolvency professionals, agencies, and utilities.
keywords: Power of Board to make regulations

title: Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament
text: (1) Every rule and regulation made under this Code shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made before each House of Parliament while it is in session...
plain_english_summary: Requires all rules and regulations framed under the IBC to be laid before both Houses of Parliament for parliamentary scrutiny.

title: Power of Central Government to remove difficulties
text: (1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Code, the Central Government may, by order, published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions not inconsistent with the provisions of this Code as may appear to be necessary for removing the difficulty: Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry of five years from the commencement of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Transitional power enabling the Central Government to issue orders to remove operational difficulties during the rollout of the Code.

title: Repeal of certain enactments and saving
text: (1) The Presidency Towns Insolvency Act, 1909 and the Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920 are hereby repealed.
plain_english_summary: Formally repeals legacy historical insolvency laws (the 1909 and 1920 insolvency acts) to unify all bankruptcy frameworks under the new Code.

title: Amendments to certain Acts
text: The Acts specified in the Eleventh Schedule shall be amended in the manner specified in that Schedule.
plain_english_summary: Provides for consequential amendments to other major commercial statutes (such as the Companies Act and Sick Industrial Companies Act) as specified in the schedules attached to the Code.
